## ADV-129: Tab tear-out releases the strip's scroll container — with an overflowing strip every tab jumps (30px horizontal + 10px vertical) and the dragged tab stops tracking the pointer

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did:
1. Ran `node test-fixtures/adv-p61/probe.cjs spill` (dev build via the canonical
   `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`; fresh `--user-data-dir`).
2. Opened `assets/samples/report.pdf`, `long.pdf`, `form.pdf`, then added 28 empty
   tabs via the strip `+` (`[data-new-tab]`) — 31 tabs. At the default width
   `.tab-list` then has `scrollWidth` 1686 vs `clientWidth` 1656, so it shows its
   thin horizontal scrollbar (`offsetHeight - clientHeight` = 10).
3. Scrolled `.tab-list` to its maximum (`scrollLeft` 30), then started a drag from a
   visible non-active tab's colour chip and moved the pointer straight DOWN
   (`dx` 0) to y=104, past the tear-out threshold (strip bottom 44 + 24). Sampled
   `.tab-area`/`.tab-list` computed `overflow`, `scrollLeft`, scrollbar thickness and
   every tab's bounding box mid-drag; then returned inside and released. Repeated with
   `scrollLeft` 0.
4. Measured the dragged tab against the grab point and against the other tabs' deltas.

Expected (Phase 61 criterion 1): while the pointer leaves the strip the dragged tab's
own box follows the pointer on both axes, and the `overflow: visible` release only
stops the clipping — the strip's layout stays put.

Actual:
- When the tear-out state arms (`data-tab-tearout="true"` on both `.tab-area` and
  `.tab-list`), `overflow` flips `auto` -> `visible`. Because `.tab-list` is ALSO the
  strip's horizontal scroll container (`styles.css:1875`, `overflow-x: auto`), releasing
  the overflow destroys the scroll container: `listScrollLeft` snaps 30 -> 0 and
  `listScrollbarThickness` 10 -> 0 in the same frame.
- On screen every non-dragged tab jumps in one frame (measured dx = +30, dy = +10 for
  each of the first three non-dragged tabs; first tab box t 8..34 -> 18..44); the whole
  strip shifts right and drops 10px and snaps back on release — a visible glitch every
  time a tear-out starts with an overflowing strip.
- The dragged tab no longer tracks the pointer: held straight down at (1790.7, 104),
  the dragged box landed at left 1754.2 (30px to the right of the grab point) and
  top 101 (10px below the pointer). The follow error equals exactly
  `(scrollLeft, scrollbarThickness)`. With 3 tabs (no overflow) the same probe tracks
  within 0px, which is why `e2e/phase61_tab_tearout.spec.cjs` (3 tabs) passes.
- Root cause: `styles.css:2236-2239` releases `overflow` on `.tab-list`, the same
  element that owns the strip's horizontal scroll. A scroll container cannot carry
  `overflow: visible`; the clip has to be released on a wrapper that is not the
  scroller, or the scroll state captured/restored around the release.

Screenshot: `screenshots/adv-p61-spill-rest.png` (rest: `scrollLeft` 30, 10px scrollbar,
tabs t=8..34), `screenshots/adv-p61-spill-tearing.png` (tear-out: `scrollLeft` 0, no
scrollbar, tabs t=18..44, dragged tab floating).

Disposition: ACCEPTED (orchestrator, TFL-44) -> DEF-432. Confirmed break with repro,
measurements and screenshots; the diff-pass released `overflow` on `.tab-list`, which is
itself the strip's horizontal scroll container. Routed to frontend-dev as DEF-432.

### Phase 61 diff-pass — surfaces that held (no finding)

- **H2 stuck tear-out state**: dispatching `pointercancel` on `window` mid tear-out cleared
  `data-tab-tearout` from BOTH `.tab-area` and `.tab-list` and restored `overflow: auto`
  (`cancel` run). The detach release path also cleared both attributes on the origin once the
  document was adopted (`detach` run); no stuck attribute observed.
- **H3 opacity leak**: during tear-out only the dragged `.tab` computed `opacity: 0.6`; both
  non-dragged tabs measured 1, the wrapping `<li>` 1, and the chip child 1. No non-dragged tab
  was faded (`opacity` run).
- **H4 hit-test / selection**: mid tear-out `document.elementFromPoint` at the below-strip point
  resolved to the dragged tab's chip (unclipped, as intended); after release the SAME point
  resolved to `.document-content` with no `[data-tab-id]` ancestor and `overflow` back to `auto`,
  so nothing steals clicks from the canvas (`hittest` run).
- **H5 detach move integrity / drag-back**: releasing past the threshold moved the document
  exactly once (origin 3 -> 2 tabs, target gone, origin not stuck), opened a real second
  `#detached` window with the document loaded (pageCount 34, `.workspace`), and dragging that
  tab out re-adopted it into the origin (origin back to 3 tabs, detached window closed,
  1 window left). No new break from the Phase 61 diff. The pre-existing unsaved-changes/dirty
  and empty-tab detach findings (ADV-117, ADV-118, ADV-120) are untouched by this diff and were
  not re-filed.

### Phase 67 diff-pass — surfaces that held (no finding)

  keyed on `[phase, collapse]` (cleanup clears the timer, so every expand resets the dwell),
  same commit effect keyed on `[phase]` firing after `MOTION_DURATION.standard` (250).
  `NOTICE_AUTO_COLLAPSE_MS === PROTECTION_NOTICE_AUTO_COLLAPSE_MS === 10000`. No off-by-one
  (the `phase67NoticeCollapse` tests pin `NOTICE_AUTO_COLLAPSE_MS - 1` still expanded, `+1`
  closing), no missing dependency, and no state that can hang in `closing` (the commit timer
  always fires; `instant` short-circuits straight to `collapsed`). Both dwell constants exist
  in two places now (protection's inline copy and the hook) — a latent drift surface, but the
  operator ruling (REQUIREMENTS.md:4251) keeps `ProtectionNotice` untouched, so it is a design
  observation, not a defect.
- **Information loss (item 2): SAFE.** All conversion warnings re-render from the persisted

- **Collision / occlusion (item 3): SAFE.** Slots are a 36px pitch with 28px icons: protection

- **Accessibility (item 4): SAFE.** Expanded boxes keep `role="note"` (conversion,

the unreconciled `data-conversion-dismiss` e2e oracles in `phase53_format_import` / `phase56_reading`
(ADV-132), which leave Phase 67 criterion 6 red until they are migrated to the collapse control.

## ADV-133: Colorful-tab modified dot still paints `--tf-tab-ink`; on the new pale Phase 68 tab body the unsaved-changes dot is effectively invisible in all three themes

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: Static diff-pass on the Phase 68 colorful body fill (TFL-116). `git diff` shows the colorful
`.tab::before` body changed from a saturated accent two-stop gradient to `color-mix(in srgb, var(--tf-tab-accent) 18%/34%, var(--bg-elevated))` (`styles.css:2098` inactive, `:2120` active), while the
tab's ink-dependent marks were left unchanged. Recomputing WCAG contrast for every element that still
paints `--tf-tab-ink` over the new body:
- `.tab-modified-dot` background `var(--tf-tab-ink)` (`styles.css:2255`); its ring is `transparent` on
  an inactive tab (`styles.css:2284-2285`) and the full accent on the active tab (`2280-2281`).
- `.tab-close:hover` background `color-mix(in srgb, var(--tf-tab-ink) 22%, transparent)` (`styles.css:2309`).
`--tf-tab-ink` is #ffffff in light (`styles.css:409`) and frosted (`790`), and #0f172a in dark (`582`),
the ink Phase 51 chose for a FULL-STRENGTH saturated body. The dot renders for every tab with
`modified=true`, active or not (`AppHeader.tsx:1170` -> `AnimatedTab.tsx:219`).

Expected: the modified/unsaved-changes dot stays clearly visible on either tab body (its whole purpose),
and the close-button hover reads as feedback, the same >= 3:1 non-text bar the rest of the tab surface holds.

Actual: with the body now pale, the 7px dot measures 1.32-1.52:1 against an INACTIVE colorful tab and
1.73-2.17:1 against the active one, in every theme and every slot (white dot in light/frosted, near-black
in dark). On an inactive tab its only outline is `transparent`, so it is fully invisible; on the active tab
a 1.5px accent ring survives but the dot fill is lost. The close-button hover wash is ~1.07:1 against the
light body, so hover feedback is nearly imperceptible in light/frosted.

Reproduction (static/rendered; no app run needed for the numbers): switch the tab strip to the colorful
style and edit a document that is NOT the active tab. Its tab shows no visible modified dot. To confirm
rendered: read the computed `background-color` of `.tab-modified-dot` over an inactive colorful tab and
compare it with the `.tab::before` composite (18% accent over `--bg-elevated`).

Evidence: `src/renderer/styles.css:2255` (dot ink), `:2309` (close hover wash); new body `:2098`/`:2120`;
saturated-era ink tokens `:409`/`:582`/`:790`. Static diff/contrast math; the adversary ran no app.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-441 (MEDIUM). CTO triage: real regression introduced by the Phase 68 body-fill
change; the unsaved-changes dot is the tab's state signal and must not vanish. Assigned to frontend-dev,
scoped to colorful tabs so `standard` styling is untouched. qa re-verification (TFL-115) proves the dot and
close-hover are visible on the pale body and sets CLOSED.

## ADV-134: The single-suppression gate hides read-only checkbox / radio / dropdown / listbox fields entirely — pdf.js never paints them under ENABLE_FORMS, and the overlay returns null before its NonFillableView fallback

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: HIGH

What I did: Static diff-pass on the Phase 65 single-layer form-field diff — `PageView.tsx:705`
(`annotationMode: AnnotationMode.ENABLE_FORMS`) and `FormsOverlay.tsx:170-174` (the one suppression
gate) — then traced the installed pdf.js 4.10.38 core to establish exactly which widget subclasses
that mode leaves painted on the canvas versus which it drops. The gate's own comment asserts
"A read-only widget is therefore ALWAYS painted on the canvas (`hasOwnCanvas = readOnly && !noHTML`)"
(`FormsOverlay.tsx:155-159`); I tested that assertion against the dependency, not the comment.

Findings from `node_modules/pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.worker.mjs`:
1. `WidgetAnnotation.getOperatorList` (`:54759`) returns an EMPTY operator list (`separateForm: true`)
   when `intent & RenderingIntentFlag.ANNOTATIONS_FORMS && !(this instanceof SignatureWidgetAnnotation)
   && !this.data.noHTML && !this.data.hasOwnCanvas`. So, under this mode, a widget reaches the canvas
   only if it is a Signature, or `noHTML` is set, or `hasOwnCanvas` is true.
2. `hasOwnCanvas` is set to true only by `TextWidgetAnnotation` (`this.data.readOnly && !noHTML`, `:55202`),
   the PushButton branch of `ButtonWidgetAnnotation` (`:55363`), `SignatureWidgetAnnotation`
   (`this.data.noRotate`, `:55894`), and the markup annotations. A checkbox or radio is the SAME
   `ButtonWidgetAnnotation` class but takes the `_processCheckBox` / `_processRadioButton` branch, which
   never sets `hasOwnCanvas` (`:55355-55362`). `ChoiceWidgetAnnotation` (dropdown/listbox, `:55702`) never
   sets it either.
3. `noHTML` defaults to `isLocked && isContentLocked` — ANNOTATION flags (`:53940`) — which a field-level
   `/Ff` ReadOnly bit does not set. So for an ordinary read-only checkbox/radio/choice, `noHTML` is false.

Consequently a read-only checkbox, radio, dropdown and listbox is NOT painted onto the canvas under
`ENABLE_FORMS`. The new gate suppresses exactly those fields: `if (kind === "signature" ||
(field.readOnly === true && isRealField)) return null;` (`FormsOverlay.tsx:172-174`) returns before the
`NonFillableView` branch at `:182-189`, and `PageView` renders no pdf.js `AnnotationLayer` (grep: no
`AnnotationLayer` import anywhere in `src/`), so there is no HTML control either. Before this diff
(default `AnnotationMode.ENABLE`) the widget was canvas-painted AND the overlay rendered a visible
disabled control (e.g. `CheckboxEditor` `disabled={field.readOnly === true}`, `FormsOverlay.tsx:327`), so
the field was at least visible; the gate now makes it disappear.

Secondary gap, same class: a push-button field is a `PDFButton`, which `formFieldKind` (`src/main/services/forms.ts:152-166`)
does not match, so it falls through to `kind: "text"`, `fillable`. pdf.js still paints it (`hasOwnCanvas`
true for push buttons, `:55363`) while `FormsOverlay` mounts an editable text box over it — the exact
double surface this phase set out to remove survives for push buttons.

Expected: a read-only fillable field keeps exactly one visible, truthful surface — the native canvas
appearance for a read-only TEXT widget (which does set `hasOwnCanvas`), and the disabled overlay control
(or the `NonFillableView` reason) for every kind pdf.js does not paint.

Actual: read-only checkbox / radio / dropdown / listbox fields render NOTHING: no overlay editor, no
disabled control, no reason label, and no canvas appearance. The user sees a gap where the form's
printed box is, with no affordance at all — and the read-only explanation added for ADV-123/124 is
unreachable for these kinds. This is a regression from the pre-diff behaviour, on the high-risk
legal/immigration form class where read-only computed/locked fields are common.

Reproduction (static; no app run): take a PDF whose AcroForm has a check box with `/Ff` ReadOnly
(bit 1) set (a read-only `/FT /Ch` dropdown behaves the same). Render it: pdf.js's
`WidgetAnnotation.getOperatorList` returns `separateForm: true` with an empty opList (so the canvas is
blank there), and `FormsOverlay`'s gate returns `null` (so no overlay). Confirm by instrumenting
`page.render`'s operator list or by reading `hasOwnCanvas`/`noHTML` on the widget — both false while
`readOnly` (field) is true.

Evidence: `src/renderer/forms/FormsOverlay.tsx:170-174` (gate), `:182-189` (unreached fallback), `:327`
(disabled control removed by the gate); `src/renderer/components/PageView.tsx:705` (ENABLE_FORMS);
`node_modules/pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.worker.mjs:54759` (mode gate), `:55202` (text), `:55355-55365`
(button: push button only), `:55702` (choice), `:53940` (`noHTML` default); `src/main/services/forms.ts:152-166`
(push-button kind fall-through). Static analysis; the adversary ran no app and edited no product file.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-444 (HIGH) + DEF-445 (MEDIUM). CTO triage: the primary finding is a real
Phase 65 regression - the overlay suppression gate assumes every read-only widget is canvas-painted, but
`hasOwnCanvas` is set only for text / push-button / signature widgets, so read-only checkbox/radio/choice
fields render nothing. Renderer-only fix for DEF-444 (narrow the gate to signature + read-only text),
assigned to frontend-dev. The push-button double-surface is pre-existing and needs an engine kind flag
plus a renderer suppression (DEF-445), sequenced after DEF-444. Phase 65 ruling 6's false premise
corrected by ruling 7 in REQUIREMENTS.md.

## ADV-135: Book View — changing an annotation's colour via the colour popover also turns the book page; the popover is portaled so the DEF-446 guard's DOM check cannot see it

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: Drove the shipped dev build (dist built 2026-10-01 09:00, master HEAD `ab62660`
plus the uncommitted DEF-446 guard tree) through `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`, opened
`assets/samples/report.pdf`, entered Book View (`[aria-label="Book View"]`), armed ink through the
`[data-book-tools]` toolbar and placed a stroke on page 1 (page stayed 1, stroke committed on page 1
as expected), switched to the select tool, clicked the stroke so its `.ann-content-action` action bar
appeared, then opened the action bar's colour box (`[data-content-action-bar] [data-ann-color-box]`)
and clicked a built-in swatch in the portaled picker (`[data-color-popover] [aria-label="Built-in green"]`).

Expected: the annotation's colour changes to green and the view stays on the annotation's page
(page 1), exactly as the placement gesture keeps still (DEF-446 fix).

Actual: the colour IS applied (`color` goes `#2563eb` -> `green`) AND the book advances in the same
click. Single layout: `[data-book-page]` 1 -> 2. Double layout (stroke placed on the right page):
the spread advances from pages [1,2] to [3,4] (left-page indicator 1 -> 3). The annotation stays
attached to its correct page (page 1 / page 2), so this is a navigation bug, not data loss, but the
user is thrown off the page they are editing every time they recolour an annotation.

Root cause: `AnnColorBox` mounts its `ColorPalette` with `createPortal(..., document.body)`
(`src/renderer/annotations/AnnColorBox.tsx:119`); the colour box lives inside the annotation overlay,
so the React synthetic `click` from a swatch bubbles through the REACT tree to the Book View page
`<figure>` `onClick` (`src/renderer/components/BookView.tsx:430-439` / `:466-475` / `:503-512`). The
DEF-446 guard suppresses a turn only when `(e.target).closest('.annotation-layer') != null` or the
capture-phase `annLayerPressRef` is set; for the portaled swatch the DOM target is body-rooted, so
`closest('.annotation-layer')` is null, and the pointerdown happened on the portal (not inside the
layer), so `annLayerPressRef` was set false. Both guards miss, and the figure turns. This is a
surviving repro of the DEF-446 class via a different trigger (a portaled annotation control), not a
re-litigation of the closed placement-gesture case.

Evidence: `screenshots/adv-135-single-before.png` / `adv-135-single-after.png` (page 1 -> page 2 with
the stroke recoloured green) and `screenshots/adv-135-double-before.png` / `adv-135-double-after.png`
(spread [1,2] -> [3,4]). Observed console snapshots from the probe (single layout):
`after-mark-click {page:"1", actionBar:1, color:"#2563eb"}` then
`after-pick-green {page:"2", actionBar:1, color:"green"}`; double layout:
`beforePage:"1", afterPage:"3", beforeColor:"#2563eb", afterColor:"green", pageTurned:true`.
The page turn first appears at the swatch click, not at the selection click (which leaves the page on
1), isolating the popover as the trigger.

Reproduction steps (deterministic; launched only through `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`):
1. `launchApp()`; stub `dialog.showOpenDialog` -> `assets/samples/report.pdf`; click
   `[aria-label="Open PDF document"]`; wait for `[aria-label="Book View"]`.
2. Click `[aria-label="Book View"]`; wait for `[data-book-view]`.
3. In `[data-book-tools]`, arm ink (inline `[data-tool="ink"]`, else
   `[data-ann-dropdown-toggle]` -> `[data-ann-dropdown-menu] [data-tool="ink"]`).
4. Drag on the book page (`mouse.move`/`down`/`move(+140,+70,{steps:8})`/`up`).
   Assert `[data-book-page]` is still "1" and an ink `page:1` exists.
5. Arm select, then click `[data-annotation-layer="1"] [data-annotation-id="<id>"]`; wait for
   `[data-content-action-bar]`.
6. Click `[data-content-action-bar] [data-ann-color-box]`, then
   `[data-color-popover] [aria-label="Built-in green"]`.
7. Observe `[data-book-page]` becomes "2" (and the engine annotation's `color` becomes `green`).

Ad-hoc probe run: `node "$PAPERCLIP_RUN_SCRATCH_DIR/probe-sel.cjs"` (single) and
`probe-confirm3.cjs` (double). Baseline specs remained green (see report).

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-448 (MEDIUM). CTO triage (TFL-64): real, deterministic, evidence-backed
navigation bug — the colour popover lives in a portal, so neither DEF-446 guard (`.annotation-layer`
DOM containment, capture-phase pointerdown ref) sees the swatch click; the React synthetic click still
bubbles to the Book View page `<figure>` `onClick`. Not a re-litigation of the closed placement case;
it is the same DEF-446 class reached through a portaled annotation control. Blocks Phase 66 criterion 7
(all DEF/ADV opened by the phase CLOSED/REJECTED); assigned to frontend-dev, scoped BookView-local
(broaden the turn guard to annotation controls outside `.annotation-layer`). qa FIX-READY verification
then CLOSED.

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: LOW

renders the reader button only when `sourceFormat === "epub"` (`src/renderer/App.tsx:609-654`) and
`onOpenComicView` is documented as superseded. But the registry entry `openComicView`
(`src/renderer/state/toolsRegistry.ts:1454-1463`), its app action wiring (`src/renderer/App.tsx:9290`,
`:10661`) and its availability gate (`readingViewGate` returns `enabled: true` for
`sourceFormat === 'cbz' | 'cbt'`, `src/renderer/state/dockModel.ts:170-185`) were left live, so the

Note: REQUIREMENTS Phase 66 ruling 6 names "the surviving comic controls" without enumerating them;
if the CTO intends `openComicView` to survive as a palette verb, this entry can be REJECTED on that
basis. Filed because the task's item 3 states the old comic view must be gone and the Book View entry
is to work where the old comic trigger did.

Disposition: REJECTED (CTO, TFL-64) - the finding is accurate but out of Phase 66 scope. REQUIREMENTS
Phase 66 ruling 6 explicitly protects "the surviving comic controls" and only asks for phase-56 spec

canvas entry is singular (the retired `[aria-label="Open comic view"]` trigger is gone; `[aria-label=
"Book View"]` is the only visible entry, App.tsx:598-654). The `openComicView` command-palette verb is
a pre-existing Phase 56 control reached only through Control+K, it mounts the SAME in-window overlay
shell (no second BrowserWindow, so ruling 1 holds), and it does not affect any Phase 66 success
criterion. Retiring it would regress the controls ruling 6 protects and force churn across the shared
tools registry and its specs (readingView.test.tsx:410/479, toolsRegistry.test.tsx:73,
e2e/installed/phase57_packaged_surface.spec.cjs:166) at phase close. Logged as a cleanup candidate in
docs/FEATURE-BACKLOG.md for the CEO to schedule as its own item if desired.


## ADV-137: Phase 70C swapped `--accent` -> `--accent-text` on a rule whose own background is white, so the multi-pane divider grip drops to 2.72:1 in dark theme (below the 3:1 icon floor)

- Session: diff-pass (TFL-170, Phase 69C/70 brand + export-string diff)
- Suggested severity: LOW

What I did: read the uncommitted 70C swap set in `src/renderer/styles.css` and checked every swapped rule against the background it paints. One swapped rule sets its OWN background to `var(--fg-on-accent)` (which is `#ffffff` in all three themes, styles.css:411/589/801):

```
.src/renderer/styles.css:14000  .multi-divider:hover .multi-divider-grip,
.src/renderer/styles.css:14001  .multi-divider:active .multi-divider-grip {
.src/renderer/styles.css:14002    background: var(--fg-on-accent);   /* #ffffff */
.src/renderer/styles.css:14003    color: var(--accent-text);         /* was var(--accent) */
```

The grip's content is the Lucide `GripVertical` icon (`src/renderer/components/MultiPane.tsx:205-207`), so `color` is an icon foreground, not text.

Expected: the swap target `--accent-text` is tuned for a DARK surface (dark `#A78BFA`, frosted `#6D28D9`, light `#7C3AED`). On this rule's fixed WHITE capsule, the pre-swap token was correct in every theme: `--accent` `#7C3AED` on `#ffffff` = 5.70:1. After the swap, dark theme renders `#A78BFA` on `#ffffff` = **2.72:1**, under the 3:1 non-text/icon floor (Phase 69 criterion 4 and the look-and-feel contrast discipline). Frosted (7.10:1) and light (5.70:1) are unaffected, so the regression is dark-theme only.

Actual: dark theme, multi-pane mode, hover/focus the divider grip -> light-violet icon on a white capsule at 2.72:1. Before the 70C swap the same rule rendered 5.70:1.

Root cause (static): the swap was applied by matching `color: var(--accent)` blanket-style; this rule is a background/foreground pair (white capsule + accent glyph) that should have KEPT `var(--accent)` (dark `#7C3AED` = 5.70:1 on white), or moved to a token that is dark in every theme. `--accent-text` is the wrong token because the surface here is light in all three themes. This is exactly the "swapped rule that now clashes on its own background" class in the task's vector 2.

Reproduction steps:
1. Read `src/renderer/styles.css:14000-14005` and confirm `background: var(--fg-on-accent)` + `color: var(--accent-text)`.
2. Confirm `--fg-on-accent: #ffffff` in all three theme blocks (styles.css:411, 589, 801).
3. Contrast `#A78BFA` on `#ffffff` = 2.72:1 (below 3:1), vs pre-swap `#7C3AED` on `#ffffff` = 5.70:1.
   (`node -e` luminance/contrast probe; no runtime app needed for the arithmetic.)

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-449 (LOW). Real dark-theme contrast regression on a fixed-white surface; the blanket `--accent` -> `--accent-text` swap used a surface-tuned token on a light capsule. Fix owned by frontend-dev (TFL-171).


## ADV-138: The dark-theme `.crop-editor-label` override still pins `color: var(--accent)`, nullifying the 70C swap in exactly the theme it was added for — dark text measures 2.94:1 (below the 4.5:1 floor)

- Session: diff-pass (TFL-170, Phase 69C/70 brand + export-string diff)
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: checked the ~40 swapped `color: var(--accent)` -> `var(--accent-text)` text rules for any later/more-specific rule that re-pins `--accent`. Found that the base rule was swapped but its dark-theme override was not:

```
.src/renderer/styles.css:11559  .crop-editor-label { ... color: var(--accent-text); }   /* 70C swap at :11564 */
.src/renderer/styles.css:11569  :root[data-theme="dark"] .crop-editor-label { color: var(--accent); }
```

Because the dark selector has higher specificity (attribute + class vs class), in dark theme the label resolves to `var(--accent)` (`#7C3AED`), not `var(--accent-text)` (`#A78BFA`). The crop label is real text (`font-size: var(--fs-xs); font-weight: 500`).

Expected: Phase 69 criterion 4 (dark-surface accent text raised to >= 4.5:1) and Phase 70 criterion 4 ("Every `color: var(--accent)` text rule on a dark surface resolves to `--accent-text` and clears 4.5:1 in all three themes"). The intended dark resolution `#A78BFA` on the dark dialog surface `--bg-elevated` (`#191e24`) = 6.16:1.

Actual: dark theme `--accent` `#7C3AED` on `#191e24` = **2.94:1**, far below 4.5:1. So the crop-editor label is the one label the 70C token was added to fix, and it is the one that does not get the fix in dark theme.

Root cause (static): the blanket swap matched the base `.crop-editor-label` rule only; the theme-scoped override at styles.css:11569 was left untouched, so it continues to override the swapped declaration in dark theme. The `--sem-primary` route Phase 69 originally specified would have avoided this (dark `--sem-primary` is also `#A78BFA`), but the literal `--accent` override defeats either approach.

Reproduction steps:
1. Read `src/renderer/styles.css:11559-11569`.
2. Confirm the dark override at :11569 is `color: var(--accent)` and has higher specificity than the swapped base rule.
3. Contrast `#7C3AED` on `#191e24` = 2.94:1 vs the intended `#A78BFA` on `#191e24` = 6.16:1.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-450 (MEDIUM). Real: a higher-specificity dark override re-pins `--accent`, so the 70C token does not reach the very label it targets in dark. Fix owned by frontend-dev (TFL-171).


## ADV-139: The accent-family "on-wash" ink `--dock-primary-fg` was not rebased by the violet hue swap — pressed titlebar buttons and the active page-layout icon render blue (blue-700 / #63a8e8) on a violet accent wash

- Session: diff-pass (TFL-170, Phase 69C/70 brand + export-string diff)
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: after the 69C hue swap moved the accent family to violet, grepped every accent-derived token for a leftover blue hue. `--dock-primary-fg` is explicitly documented in-code as the SAME accent family one step deeper ("blue-700 is the same accent family one step deeper", styles.css:420-425; "the bright family blue is the dark-theme counterpart", styles.css:597-601; "blue-700 (the frosted family blue)", styles.css:808-810) but its value is still blue in all three themes:

```
.src/renderer/styles.css:601   --dock-primary-fg: #63a8e8;   (dark,   bright blue)
.src/renderer/styles.css:810   --dock-primary-fg: #1d4ed8;   (frosted, blue-700)
```

It is `color` ink on the accent wash at:

- `.canvas-page-layout .tool-btn-active` (styles.css:4271-4278) — the ACTIVE page-layout option icon,
- `color: var(--stage-hue, var(--dock-primary-fg))` (styles.css:16376) — the stage primary verb.

Expected: a single brand violet accent (Phase 69 criterion 5; look-and-feel "ONE accent color used consistently for primary actions and selections"), and the in-code comment's own promise that this token is the accent family one step deeper. The accent wash it sits on is now `rgba(124,58,237,0.20)` over the surface (`#2d244c` on dark `--bg-elevated`).

Actual: the pressed titlebar button and the active page-layout icon paint blue (`#63a8e8` dark / `#1d4ed8` light) on top of that violet wash. It is not a contrast failure (measured 5.65:1 dark, 4.83:1 light) but it is a visible two-hue clash: a blue control on a violet accent surface, contradicting the hue swap the rest of the accent family received.

Root cause (static): the 69C swap only rebased the enumerated Phase 69 tokens (`--accent*`, `--sem-primary`, `--tf-accent*`, `--select-edge`) and the 70C text rules; `--dock-primary-fg` is an accent-family derived token that was left at its pre-swap blue value, so its hue no longer tracks the brand. (Same class, lower visibility, in the remaining hard-coded blue washes: `--hit` / `--hit-active` styles.css:469-470/849-850, `--glass-selected-bg` / `--glass-selected-border` styles.css:216-217, `--sample-card-border-hover` styles.css:452/833, `:root[data-theme="dark"] .crop-editor-mask` background styles.css:11555, and the frosted accent-glow box-shadows styles.css:14346/5459 that `designTokensContract.test.ts:1044/1053` still pins at `rgba(37, 99, 235`, i.e. blue.)

Reproduction steps:
1. Read `src/renderer/styles.css:425`, `:601`, `:810` and confirm `--dock-primary-fg` is blue in all three themes.
2. Read its consumers at `:1746`, `:4277`, `:16376`.
3. In the dev build (dark theme), press the titlebar Open button or select a page-layout option and observe the blue ink against the violet wash. Static proof is sufficient; no runtime measurement needed for the hue.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-451 (MEDIUM). Real and impactful: the 69C hue swap is materially incomplete. `--dock-primary-fg` plus the remaining hard-coded blue washes/glows (`--hit`/`--hit-active`, `--glass-selected-*`, `--sample-card-border-hover`, dark `.crop-editor-mask`, the frosted accent glows pinned blue by `designTokensContract.test.ts:1044/1053`) still render blue against the violet accent. Fix owned by frontend-dev (TFL-171).


## ADV-140: The active colorful tab never reaches the strip foot / canvas — it floats 6.5px above the strip bottom (7.5px above the canvas top) in all three themes, so Phase 72 item 2's "engulf" is absent

- Session: diff-pass (TFL-212, Phase 72 tab surfaces)
- Suggested severity: HIGH

What I did: launched the dev build (`npm.cmd run build`, then `node test-fixtures/adv-p72-probe.cjs a`), opened two bundled documents so one colorful tab is ACTIVE and one is INACTIVE, and measured the tab/strip geometry from `getBoundingClientRect()` and `getComputedStyle()` in light, dark and frosted.

The strip content box is 43px high (`--chrome-titlebar-h: 44px` minus the header's 1px bottom border). The ACTIVE colorful tab measures 30px high with `align-self: flex-end` (styles.css:2126), yet its measured box is `topGap = 6.5px` and `bottomGap = 6.5px` to `.tab-list` in every theme — i.e. it is vertically CENTRED, not dropped. Its foot sits at y=36.5 while `.tab-list` ends at y=43 and the canvas top (`.app-header` bottom) is y=44, so the fill stops 6.5px short of the strip bottom and 7.5px short of the canvas.

Expected: Phase 72 operator item 2 and success criterion 2 (`docs/phase-specs/phase-72.md:24,61`): the active colorful tab extends DOWN to the strip's bottom edge / canvas top, bottom gap <= 1px, no separator line, its fill continuous with the canvas. Inactive tabs are the only ones that float (>= 2px clear of both edges).

Actual: the active tab is the same centred chip as the inactive tabs, only 4px taller; it does not reach the strip foot, does not touch the canvas, and the strip's own 1px border still separates it from the canvas. The `align-self: flex-end` never takes effect: the flex item of `.tab-list` is the wrapping `<li>` (`motion.li` in `src/renderer/components/AnimatedTab.tsx:157-165`), whose computed `display` is `list-item` and `align-self` is `auto`; the property is declared on the inner `.tab` div, so it is ignored. Measured `parentTag: "LI"`, `parentDisplay: "list-item"`, `parentAlignSelf: "auto"` on every active tab.

Reproduction steps:
1. `npm.cmd run build`
2. `node test-fixtures/adv-p72-probe.cjs a`
3. Read the `themes.{light,dark,frosted}.tabs[]` entries with `"active":true`: `topGap` and `bottomGap` are both `6.5`; `alignSelf` is `"flex-end"` but `parentDisplay` is `"list-item"`.
4. Zoomed light capture: `screenshots/adv-p72-a-zoom-active-light.png` (active "Empty tab"; a lighter strip band is visible below the rounded chip). Full strip: `screenshots/adv-p72-a-header-light.png`, `-dark.png`, `-frosted.png`.

Fixture: `test-fixtures/adv-p72-probe.cjs` (scenario `a`).

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-455 (HIGH). CTO triage: reproducible and real - the active
colorful tab is centred (topGap = bottomGap = 6.5px) and never reaches the strip foot or
the canvas, so operator item 2 / success criterion 2 ("engulf") is not met. Root cause is
exact: `align-self: flex-end` is declared on the inner `.tab` div (`styles.css:2122-2128`)
but the flex item of `.tab-list` is the wrapping `<li>` (`AnimatedTab.tsx:157-165`, computed
`display: list-item`, `align-self: auto`), so the declaration is inert. Renderer fix,
routed to frontend-dev (TFL-213). qa retests and closes.


## ADV-141: At the 640px minimum window with 10 tabs the strip overflows by 140px — 5 tabs' right edges and the "+" control lie past the strip's right edge and are clipped (unreachable), violating Phase 72 items 7-8

- Session: diff-pass (TFL-212, Phase 72 tab surfaces)
- Suggested severity: HIGH

What I did: launched the dev build, opened 10 bundled documents, then resized the main window to the 640x800 minimum and measured the strip (`node test-fixtures/adv-p72-probe.cjs b`).

At 1280x800 the fit works (`.tab-list` clientWidth 376, scrollWidth 376, 10 tabs uniform 32px, no clipping). At the 640x800 minimum the measured result is:

- `.tab-list` clientWidth = **156**, scrollWidth = **296** (horizontal overflow = **140px**)
- 10 colorful tabs all clamp to the hard floor of 24px (`HARD_MIN_TAB_WIDTH`), width spread 0
- **5** tabs have `right > strip.right` — the rightmost tab's right edge is at x=436 while the strip's right edge is x=330
- the `.tab-new` "+" button's left edge is x=442, i.e. entirely past the strip's right edge (strip right 330)

`overflow-x` computes to `hidden`, so the overflowing tabs and the "+" control are clipped out of the bar and unreachable.

Expected: Phase 72 item 8 and success criterion 7 (`docs/phase-specs/phase-72.md:30,50,66`): with 10 tabs at the 640px minimum window every tab keeps the SAME width, NO tab's right edge exceeds the strip's right edge, `.tab-list` `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`, and the strip contains every tab without scrolling.

Actual: the uniform width applies (width spread 0.0), but the `HARD_MIN_TAB_WIDTH = 24` floor cannot fit 10 tabs in a 156px strip, so the row overflows by 140px and the tail tabs (plus the new-tab affordance) are clipped away. The Phase 72 claim that the hard floor "still contains every tab" is false at the required 640px state. This is the same surface as ADV-122 / ADV-128 (tabs unreachable at the 640px minimum), which the Phase 72 sizing change did not close.

Reproduction steps:
1. `npm.cmd run build`
2. `node test-fixtures/adv-p72-probe.cjs b`
3. Read `min640`: `list.clientWidth=156`, `list.scrollWidth=296`, `horizOverflow=140`, `clipped=5`, `rightMost=436` vs `list.right=330`, `plus.left=442`.
4. Capture: `screenshots/adv-p72-b-overflow-640.png` (the squeezed tab row is cut at the strip's right edge, before the toolbar icons).

Fixture: `test-fixtures/adv-p72-probe.cjs` (scenario `b`).

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-456 (HIGH). CTO triage: reproducible and real - at the 640px
minimum with 10 tabs the row overflows 140px and 5 tabs plus the "+" control are clipped out
of the bar, violating operator item 8 / success criterion 7. Root cause is a code/comment
contradiction in `planTabOverflow`: the comment (`AppHeader.tsx:84-87`) says the hard floor
"is exceeded if the tabs cannot fit", but the implementation clamps the fit width UP to
`HARD_MIN_TAB_WIDTH = 24` (`AppHeader.tsx:138-142`), which forces the overflow. Contract
criterion 7 is achievable once the width is allowed to satisfy the fit inequality, so no
contract change is needed; routed to frontend-dev (TFL-213). qa retests and closes.

## ADV-143: Phase 73 dirty dot is 100% clipped away at the 640px minimum with 10 tabs; the qa containment oracle cannot see it

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: HIGH

What I did: rebuilt the renderer so the working-tree CSS is served (`npm.cmd run build:renderer`) and ran one adversarial probe, `node test-fixtures/adv-p73/probe.cjs b`, which opens 10 then 20 real documents at the 640px minimum window, dirties tab 0 (`report.pdf`) through the real Rotate control (`runTool(win,'rotate')`), and for each tab measures the dirty dot's `getBoundingClientRect()` / computed style, `.tab-title`'s padding-box clip rect (`overflow: hidden`), and a `document.elementFromPoint()` hit-test at the dot centre. Baseline `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase73_dot.spec.cjs` is 1 passed / 0 failed.

Expected (Phase 73 ruling 6, success criteria 1/5/6 - `docs/phase-specs/phase-73.md:19,35,39`): "the dot must remain fully painted ... if the title is squeezed to the point where a reserved dot plus close cannot fit, the dot still wins its full box (the title ellipsizes first) and is never cut." The dot should be painted and hit-testable at every squeezed width.

Actual: at 10 tabs / 640px the strip is a uniform 10px per tab (`--tf-tab-width: 10px`, list clientWidth 156 == scrollWidth 156), but `.tab-title` is squeezed to a 1px border-box (clip box x[180.5, 181.5]). The dot's 5px box lays out at x[181.5, 186.5] - its left edge exactly on the title's clip right edge - so `.tab-title { overflow: hidden }` clips 100% of it. `elementFromPoint` at the dot centre returns `tab tab-active`, not the dot: it is neither painted nor hit-testable. Pushing harder to 20 tabs / 640px (4px tabs), the dot (x[180, 185]) also overflows the tab body itself (tab right x182, `dotToTabRight = -3`). In both cases the dot retains computed `visibility: visible`, `opacity: 1`, `box-shadow: none`, `offsetWidth 5` - the `tab-modified-dot-hidden` state is NOT applied - so every static/computed assertion stays green while the user sees a bare tab. This is the operator's original "partially cut-out" complaint reproduced as total removal, and it falsifies the diff's own comment ("so ... no ancestor clip can cut it"): the dot's own box is contained, but the `.tab-title` that contains it is narrower than the dot, so the title's clip still cuts it.

The qa spec cannot catch this by construction: `e2e/phase73_dot.spec.cjs:95-112` (`assertContained`) checks only `dot.left - title.left >= 0` (here exactly +1, passes) and compares `getBoundingClientRect()`s, which ignore an ancestor's `overflow: hidden`. The spec's own green log prints `[P73 squeezed] tabWidths=[10,...]` and `[P73 squeezed-640] ... title={"width":1}` while reporting the state as contained. The dot is the only unsaved-changes signal, so at the supported minimum window width with 10+ open tabs a user can close a modified document with no visible warning.

Raw probe output (decisive fields):
```
### {"scenario":"b","label":"10-tabs-640","summary":{"count":10,"list":{"clientWidth":156,"scrollWidth":156},"widths":[10,10,10,10,10,10,10,10,10,10],"widthMin":10},"dirtyTab0":{"active":true,"tab":{"left":178,"right":188,"width":10},"title":{"left":180.5,"right":181.5,"width":1,"paddingLeft":1,"clipLeft":180.5,"clipRight":181.5,"overflow":"hidden"},"close":{"left":189.5},"dot":{"left":181.5,"right":186.5,"width":5,"offsetWidth":5,"visibility":"visible","opacity":"1","className":"tab-modified-dot"},"hit":"tab tab-active","paint":{"rightOfClip":true,"leftOfClip":false,"fullyClipped":true,"hitIsDot":false}}}
### {"scenario":"b","label":"20-tabs-640","summary":{"count":20,"list":{"clientWidth":156,"scrollWidth":156},"widths":[4,...],"widthMin":4},"dirtyTab0":{"tab":{"left":178,"right":182,"width":4},"title":{"left":179,"right":180,"width":1},"dot":{"left":180,"right":185,"width":5},"hit":"LI","paint":{"rightOfClip":true,"fullyClipped":true,"hitIsDot":false},"clearance":{"dotToTabLeft":2,"dotToTabRight":-3,"dotToCloseLeft":3}}}
### {"scenario":"b-verdict","tenFullyClipped":true,"tenHit":"tab tab-active","twentyFullyClipped":true,"twentyHit":"LI","twentyTabWidth":4,"twentyTitleWidth":1}
```

Reproduction steps:
1. `npm.cmd run build:renderer`
2. `node test-fixtures/adv-p73/probe.cjs b`
3. Read the `10-tabs-640` line: `dot.left (181.5) == title.clipRight (181.5)`, `paint.fullyClipped: true`, `hit: "tab tab-active"`.
4. Cross-check the green `e2e/phase73_dot.spec.cjs`: it logs the same `tab width 10` / `title width 1` and its `assertContained` still passes.

Screenshot: screenshots/adv-p73-b-zoom-dirty-tab0-10tabs.png (8x-zoomed dirty tab 0: no dot painted); screenshots/adv-p73-b-10tabs-640.png (header: the dirty tab is a bare sliver); screenshots/adv-p73-b-zoom-dirty-tab0-20tabs.png (20-tab sliver, no dot).

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-462 (qa reproduced and filed, TFL-245; qa hardened `e2e/phase73_dot.spec.cjs` with a hit-test + ancestor-clip oracle, which now FAILS on the unfixed tree). Real product defect: the Phase 73 dot is fully clipped by `.tab-title{overflow:hidden}` at the supported squeezed width, and the Phase 73 e2e oracle was blind to ancestor clips. Fix routed to frontend-dev; qa retests and closes DEF-462.

### Phase 73 diff-pass - surfaces that SURVIVED (no ADV filed)

Same probe, scenario `a` (`node test-fixtures/adv-p73/probe.cjs a`), on 2 tabs at full width, all three themes:
- Surface 3 (dirty-only): clean tab dot computes `visibility:hidden, opacity:0` and `elementFromPoint` at its centre returns `tab-title`; dirty tab dot is `visible, opacity:1` and hit-tests as `tab-modified-dot`. Holds.
- Surface 4 (ring legibility): ring present (`border-top: 1px solid`, Chromium floors 1.5px at DPR 1), resolves to `--fg-strong` 55% and differs from the fill in light (`fill rgb(124,58,237)`), dark (`fill rgb(167,139,250)`) and frosted (`fill rgb(109,40,217)`); `box-shadow: none`. Zoom screenshot adv-p73-a-zoom-dirty-tab0.png shows a clearly legible ringed dot. Holds.
- Surface 5 (layout/padding-left 1px): an injected probe-only `padding-left: 0` A/B produced byte-identical tab widths `[180,180]`, close lefts `[492.84,674.84]`, title widths `[134,134]` and clip text - no width/uniformity/close shift. Holds.
- Surface 6 (mousedown on the dot): mousedown at the dot centre changed the active id from the clean tab to the dirty tab, so the dot does not swallow activation. Holds.
- Surfaces 1/2 at squeezed widths are the ADV-143 failure, not a separate close-collision finding: at 10 tabs `dot.right (186.5) < close.left (189.5)`, so there is no dot/close overlap (the close itself overflows the 10px tab, which is the pre-existing Phase 72 area, outside this pass).

## ADV-144: Phase 74's hover accent outline on `.form-editor` is dead in the dark and frosted themes (and dark focus loses its wash/border) - the themed rule out-specifies `:hover`/`:focus`

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: LOW

What I did: static diff-pass on the Phase 74 (DEF-461) CSS change, plus a static `@cantoo/pdf-lib` walk of the real `956.pdf` copy. I read the working-tree diff of `src/renderer/styles.css` (the Phase 74 block is uncommitted; HEAD `d8fff9c`, tree dirty) and the built stylesheet the running app serves, `dist/renderer/assets/index-X0hu2dAG.css`, and computed the CSS cascade by selector specificity for the themed `.form-editor` rules. No Electron launch (the shared `.paperclip-build.lock` is held fresh by frontend-dev for TFL-248; see the pending-dynamic note below).

The shipped rules, in source order (verbatim from `dist/renderer/assets/index-X0hu2dAG.css`):

```
.form-editor:hover{border-color:var(--accent-soft)}
:root[data-theme=dark] .form-editor{color:#0f172a;background:0 0;border-color:#0000}
:root[data-theme=frosted] .form-editor{color:var(--fg-strong);background:0 0;border-color:#0000}
.form-editor:focus{border-color:var(--accent-hover);box-shadow:0 0 0 1px var(--accent-soft);background:#ffffffeb}
:root[data-theme=frosted] .form-editor:focus{background:#fffffff0}
```

Specificity: `.form-editor:hover` and `.form-editor:focus` are `(0,2,0)` (one class + one pseudo-class). `:root[data-theme=...] .form-editor` is `(0,3,0)` (`:root` pseudo-class + `[data-theme=...]` attribute + `.form-editor` class). Higher specificity wins regardless of source order, so in the dark and frosted themes the themed `.form-editor` declaration sets `border-color:#0000` (transparent) and there is no `:root[data-theme="..."] .form-editor:hover` rule to restore it: the border is `transparent` on hover. This governs every `.form-editor` control - text `<input>`, `<textarea>`, dropdown `<select>` and listbox `<ul>`.

Expected (Phase 74 block comment, `src/renderer/styles.css:7000-7006`, and this diff-pass probe item 3): "Hover reveals a subtle accent outline; focus keeps the clear accent border and a light wash under the caret" - in light, dark AND frosted.

Actual:
- Light theme: hover outline `--accent-soft`, focus wash + `--accent-hover` border. Holds.
- Dark theme: hover border stays `transparent` (no outline). Focus border stays `transparent`, and focus's `background:#ffffffeb` (`(0,2,0)`) is also beaten by `:root[data-theme=dark] .form-editor{background:0 0}` (`(0,3,0)`), so the dark focus wash is absent too; only the non-overridden `box-shadow:0 0 0 1px var(--accent-soft)` remains as a faint ring. The dark focus border regressed from `var(--accent)` (pre-Phase-74 dark base set `border-color:var(--accent)`) to transparent.
- Frosted theme: hover border stays `transparent` (no outline). Focus wash is present because `:root[data-theme=frosted] .form-editor:focus` (`(0,3,0)`, later) sets `background:#fffffff0`; focus border still resolves to transparent (no themed focus border rule).

Scope note (not a finding): `.form-checkbox:hover{border-color:var(--accent)}` and `.form-radio:hover .form-radio-dot{border-color:var(--accent)}` have no themed `.form-editor`-style override (`:root[data-theme=...] .form-checkbox/.form-radio-dot` do not exist), so checkbox and radio-group hover still work in all three themes. The regression is confined to the `.form-editor` family.

Reproduction (static - deterministic, no Electron needed):
1. `git rev-parse HEAD` -> `d8fff9c966fab3995b2cdf457ba9a1790762c3e2` (dirty tree).
2. Read `dist/renderer/assets/index-X0hu2dAG.css` (offset ~100768): the four rules above are byte-adjacent in that order.
3. `Select-String -Path src/renderer/styles.css -Pattern 'form-editor'` -> only lines 7007/7021/7025/7035/7041/7050 (no `:root[data-theme="dark"] .form-editor:hover` or `:root[data-theme="dark"] .form-editor:focus`).
4. Specificity `(0,3,0) > (0,2,0)` -> `border-color`/`background` from the themed rule win on `:hover`/`:focus`. Dynamic confirmation (a computed-style read on a hovered `.form-editor` per theme) is queued in `test-fixtures/adv-p74/probe.cjs overlay` and is pending the build lock.

Screenshot: pending the dynamic probe (`screenshots/adv-p74-*.png`); the cascade above is theme-independent and already decisive on the shipped `dist` bytes.

DYNAMIC CONFIRMATION (this run, build lock released). The static entry above was written against HEAD `d8fff9c` / `dist/renderer/assets/index-X0hu2dAG.css`. This run re-ran it against the current tree: HEAD `645320f3cd715281d04f2ee2a5aaebf31cbac8b3` (Phase 78), dirty tree, `dist/renderer/assets/index-B4IQBP4K.css`. The four rules are still byte-adjacent and unchanged in that stylesheet (`Select-String '\.form-editor'` -> 7 rules; substring read offset of first `.form-editor` shows `.form-editor:hover{border-color:var(--accent-soft)}` then `:root[data-theme=dark] .form-editor{...border-color:#0000}` / `:root[data-theme=frosted] .form-editor{...border-color:#0000}` then `.form-editor:focus{...background:#ffffffeb}` / `:root[data-theme=frosted] .form-editor:focus{...}`). No `:root[data-theme="dark"] .form-editor:hover` or `:root[data-theme="dark"] .form-editor:focus` exists. Computed-style confirmation via `node test-fixtures/adv-p74/theme-hover.cjs` (launches only through `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`), reading a real `.form-editor` text control at rest / `:hover` / `:focus` per theme:

- light: rest border `rgba(0,0,0,0)`; hover border `rgba(124,58,237,0.12)` (=`--accent-soft`); focus border `rgb(139,92,246)` (=`--accent-hover`) + background `rgba(255,255,255,0.92)` + `box-shadow rgba(124,58,237,0.12) 0 0 0 1px`. Correct.
- dark: rest border `rgba(0,0,0,0)`; hover border `rgba(0,0,0,0)` (NO outline); focus border `rgba(0,0,0,0)` (NO accent border) + background `rgba(0,0,0,0)` (NO white wash); only the `box-shadow rgba(124,58,237,0.12) 0 0 0 1px` ring remains. Confirmed regression.
- frosted: rest border `rgba(0,0,0,0)`; hover border `rgba(0,0,0,0)` (NO outline); focus border `rgba(0,0,0,0)` (NO accent border) + background `rgba(255,255,255,0.94)` (wash present from the frosted focus rule).

Scope note re-confirmed dynamically: the multi-widget group radio dot hovers to `rgb(124,58,237)` in all three themes (`.form-radio:hover .form-radio-dot` has no themed override). Raw: `test-fixtures/adv-p74/theme-hover.json`, `test-fixtures/adv-p74/log-theme-hover.txt`.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-470. CTO triage: real regression introduced by the Phase 74 transparent-at-rest change - the themed `:root[data-theme=dark|frosted] .form-editor` rule (0,3,0) out-specifies `.form-editor:hover`/`:focus` (0,2,0), so the dark/frosted hover outline and dark focus accent border/wash are dead. The fix's whole point is an invisible-at-rest control with an interaction affordance; losing that affordance in two of three themes is not acceptable. Owner: frontend-dev, scoped to `src/renderer/styles.css` themed hover/focus rules. qa re-verification proves light/dark/frosted hover+focus computed styles.

## ADV-146: Book View turn leaf is a live annotation hit surface - an armed-tool stroke begun during a page turn commits to the OUTGOING page

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM (silent wrong-page write; ~350ms window; an armed tool is required)

What I did: launched the app through `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`, opened a 16-page PDF, entered Book View, armed `ink` (`[data-book-tools]`), clicked Next (`[data-book-next]`), paused the turn leaf mid-swing (`document.querySelector('[data-book-turn]').getAnimations()[0].pause(); ...currentTime = 55`), read `document.elementFromPoint` at the page centre, drove a short real mouse drag there, and let the turn settle.

Expected: once the turn has begun the static spread and label already show the destination, so a stroke started then should mark the destination page - or the transient leaf should be non-interactive and the stroke ignored.

Actual: `elementFromPoint` resolves to the turn leaf's own `[data-annotation-layer]` for the OUTGOING page with `pointer-events: auto`, and the drag commits ink to the outgoing page. Double: label `Page 3-4 of 16`, static `[3,4]`, element layer page 2, ink on page 2. Single: label `Page 2 of 16`, static `[2]`, element layer page 1, ink on page 1. The mark is not visible after the flip and would be saved to the wrong page with no warning.

Root cause (static): `renderTurnLeaf` wires the leaf faces to the armed `annotationTool` (`BookView.tsx:399-437`, tool at `:410`); `.book-view-turn { pointer-events: none }` (`styles.css:18717-18725`) is overridden for descendants by `.annotation-layer-active { pointer-events: auto }` (`styles.css:5862`), which `AnnotationOverlay` sets when a tool is armed or an annotation is selected.

Evidence: `test-fixtures/adv-tfl271/` (`cw.spec.cjs`, `probe.spec.cjs`, `cw-double-*.png`, `cw-single-*.png`, run logs).

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-467 (MEDIUM; owning frontend-dev via TFL-273).

## ADV-150: Save-time form fill report calls every untouched empty multi-widget option GROUP `option-unknown` ("option not found: Off") - the operator's "93 filled, 12 skipped"

- Session: diff-pass (TFL-254, Phase 74 chunk 5)
- Suggested severity: LOW (misleading report/status, no data loss)

What I did: ran the Phase-74 diff-pass dynamic probe on a temp copy of the operator's real encrypted `956.pdf` (copy `test-fixtures/tfl225/956-real.pdf`, sha256 `37a51c4f332209a61141fdd6028dba0fe2b7c34681dba486ea08ece652e792fe`, 315235 bytes, 6 pages), current tree HEAD `645320f3cd715281d04f2ee2a5aaebf31cbac8b3` (Phase 78), dirty tree, `dist/renderer/assets/index-B4IQBP4K.css`.

1. `node test-fixtures/adv-p74/probe.cjs recon` - opened the copy, typed `ADVP74` into one text field, saved, captured the full `formFillReport` (105 rows). Report summary: `93 filled, 12 skipped`; every one of the 12 skipped rows is a multi-widget option group (`mg.title`, `mg.comm`, `mg.oth mig`, `mg.app`, `mg.prov assist`, `mg.reason ex`, `mg.also ar`, `mg.ending ar`, `mg.end comm`, `cc.person rec`, `ta.assist`, `ar.also`), each with `status: option-unknown`, `detail: "option not found: Off"`. Full row data: `test-fixtures/adv-p74/recon-save-report.json`.
2. `node test-fixtures/adv-p74/report-filled.cjs` - selected the last widget of `mg.title` (`ms`) and of `mg.reason ex` (`public`), saved, captured the report. Summary: `95 filled, 10 skipped`; both selected groups report `status: filled, detail: null`. Raw: `test-fixtures/adv-p74/report-filled.json`.

Expected: an option group the user never touched has no value to write; its save-time row must not claim an option was requested and missing. The radio-group branch already models the correct behaviour (`src/main/services/form-fill.ts:763-775`: empty selection -> `clear()` -> `filled`); an empty group should read as a no-op / "no value set", not `option-unknown`.

Actual: all 12 untouched empty groups are reported `option-unknown` with detail `option not found: Off`. The UI renders that reason as "option not available - option not found: Off" (`src/renderer/forms/FormsOverlay.tsx:681-684` + `reportStatusReason` `src/renderer/forms/model.ts:319-320`), so a correctly-filled document shows 12 false error lines. This is exactly the "93 filled, 12 skipped" the operator reported.

Root cause (static read): these 12 fields are pdf-lib `PDFCheckBox` instances with more than one widget (pdf-lib does not model them as `PDFRadioGroup`; `formFieldKind` labels them `radio` at `src/main/services/forms.ts:164-166`, but `applyFieldValue` dispatches on `instanceof` and reaches the checkbox branch first at `src/main/services/form-fill.ts:737`). At save time `provided === undefined`, so `chosen = buttonGroupValue(field)` (`forms.ts:127-135`), which reads the field `/V`; an untouched group's `/V` is `/Off`, so `chosen === "Off"`. `setButtonGroupValue(field, "Off")` returns `false` because `"Off"` is not one of the widgets' on-states (`forms.ts:210`), and the branch maps that `false` to `option-unknown` with `option not found: ${chosen}` (`form-fill.ts:742-744`). The `false` return means the field is left untouched, so there is no corruption - only the report is wrong. When a value is actually selected, `buttonGroupValue` returns the on-state, `setButtonGroupValue` succeeds, and the row is `filled` (verified in run 2).

Verdict (the task's item 2): NOT a fill failure and NOT data loss. The 12 groups are genuinely empty, an untouched group stays empty across save/reopen, and a *filled* group reports `filled` and round-trips (see the clean group round-trip below). The defect is report truthfulness: `option-unknown` / "option not available - option not found: Off" is a false error for a field where no value was ever set.

Suggested fix (not applied): in the save-time (`provided === undefined`) checkbox-group path, treat an empty/`Off` field value as a no-op and report a "no value set" outcome (or reuse the radio branch's empty -> `clear()` -> `filled`) instead of `option-unknown`; reserve `option-unknown` for a real user-supplied value that matches no widget on-state.

Screenshots: not needed for the report text (the report is captured as text/DOM); the group round-trip screenshots below show the selections that DO persist.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-471. CTO triage: confirmed false error state on a correctly-filled document. No data loss, but the operator's post-save report reads "93 filled, 12 skipped" with 12 lines of "option not available - option not found: Off" for groups they never touched - exactly the kind of "incorrect tick" distrust this phase exists to remove. Owner: backend-dev, scoped to the save-time empty-group path in `src/main/services/form-fill.ts` (report `filled`/no-value no-op instead of `option-unknown`). qa re-verification proves an untouched save reports 105 filled / 0 skipped and a filled group still reports `filled`.

### Phase 74 chunk 5 - design critique of the changed surface (skill: design-critique)

User: a migration agent / applicant completing the official Form 956 (PDF). Job on this surface: tick the correct printed option box and type into the correct printed field, then save and reopen with confidence. Success: the document reads back with the same ticks/values and does not look broken.

- Must-fix - **Error states (ADV-150):** the post-save report shows a false error state on a correctly-filled document - `93 filled, 12 skipped` with 12 lines reading "option not available - option not found: Off" for option groups the user never touched. The summary's job is to build confidence that the save captured the work; instead it implies 12 failures. Try: render untouched empty groups as "no value set" (or omit them) and reserve the "option not available" wording for a real user-supplied mismatch.
- Should-fix - **Affordance/states (ADV-144):** in dark and frosted, a form text/select field gives no hover outline and its focus accent border/wash disappear, so the only sign a field is interactive/focused is the faint box-shadow. Light is correct. Try: add `:root[data-theme="dark"|"frosted"] .form-editor:hover/:focus` rules at equal-or-higher specificity that keep the transparent-at-rest base but restore the hover/focus accent.
- Nice-to-fix - **Affordance (read-only):** read-only controls are signalled only by `opacity: 0.75` and the `disabled` attribute, with no tooltip naming why (cf. `skipped-readonly`); a title/`aria-description` would explain it.
- Strengths to keep: the transparent-at-rest overlay makes the form's own printed box the single visible surface (the operator's core DEF-461 complaint); groups render one tick at a time with per-widget hit targets; a filled group is truthfully reported `filled` and survives save/reopen; the save report clearly separates filled from skipped.

## ADV-154: At the 30-preset cap a newly-saved preset is silently dropped from disk while the picker shows it as saved - a phantom entry that vanishes on reopen

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: LOW

What I did: launched the dev build through `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` with a fresh
temp user-data dir seeded with `printPresets` = 50 valid distinct-name entries
(`p00`..`p49`), then opened `report.pdf`, opened the standalone print window, and
confirmed the picker lists exactly 30 (`p00`..`p29`). I then saved a NEW name
`extra` via the real control (`fill [data-print-preset-name] = "extra"` ->
click `[data-print-preset-save]`), waited for the success notice, read
`settings.json` back, and repeated with a second new name `extra2`. Command:
`cmd /c "npx playwright test e2e/phase81_print_presets_adversary.spec.cjs -g \"B cap\""`.

Expected: per the phase contract `cap 30` is a persisted-list ceiling. Saving a
31st distinct name should either be refused with a visible error or replace/
evict predictably, but whichever way it resolves, the picker and the persisted
list must agree. The success notice must not assert a save the disk did not take.

Actual: the renderer's `savePreset` appends to its in-memory `presets` list and
calls `savePresets(next)` without applying the cap; the main-process
`normalizePrintPresets` then truncates the written list to its first 30 entries,
so the newest name is dropped. Measured after the first save: disk list = 30
(`extra` absent), picker = 31 (`extra` present), notice "Preset \"extra\"
saved.". After the second save: disk = 30 (`extra` and `extra2` both absent),
picker = 32 (both present). So every new preset saved while at the cap reports
success, appears in the picker for the rest of the session, and is gone on the
next launch - silent loss of user-created data plus a UI/disk divergence that
grows without bound in-session. No page error was raised.

Evidence:
- `screenshots/adv-154-phantom-presets.png` (picker showing 32 options after the two phantom saves).
- `test-fixtures/phase81-presets/adv-154-persisted-after-phantom-saves.json` (the on-disk settings.json after both saves: exactly 30 presets, neither `extra` nor `extra2`).

Affected file: `src/renderer/components/usePrintControls.ts` (`savePreset`
does not enforce `PRINT_PRESETS_CAP`) with `src/main/services/settings.ts`
(`normalizePrintPresets` silently truncates).

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-477 (CTO, TFL-317, 2026-10-02; severity MEDIUM - silent
loss of a user-created preset at the cap boundary plus a success notice that asserts a
save the disk did not take)

### Phase 81 printPresets diff-pass - attacks that did NOT reproduce (defended)

Every attack below was executed against the shipped dev build; the outcome is
recorded so a silent pass is not mistaken for coverage.

- **A1 non-array `printPresets`**: seeded `printPresets: "not-an-array"` with a
  distinctive `recentsCap: 7` and `theme: "dark"`. The app booted on the STORED
  settings (`recentsCap` 7 - not the default 10), so the whole-file recovery path
  was NOT taken; the picker listed zero presets (field absent, consumer default
  `[]`); no page error. Defended.
- **A2 hostile entry list**: seeded `[null, 7, "x", {name:"   "},` two `ok1`
  entries with different settings, a 41-char name, `{name:"ok2",settings:[1,2]}`,
  `{name:"ok3",settings:null}`, and an `ok4` whose known values were all invalid
  (`copies:500`, `scaling:"bogus"`, `pagesPerSheet:3`, `duplex:"nope"`) with
  injected `deviceName`/`pageRanges`/`paperSource`/`bogusUnknown``]`. The picker
  listed exactly `ok1, ok4, ok5`; `ok1` upserted to the later settings
  `{copies:3, duplex:"shortEdge"}`; `ok4` normalized to `{}` with
  `deviceName`/`pageRanges`/`paperSource`/unknown keys all dropped; the 41-char
  and non-object entries were skipped. `recentsCap` 7 survived (no recovery), no
  page error. Defended.
- **B cap on load**: 50 valid distinct-name entries -> exactly the first 30
  survived the load, in order, and the persisted file stayed at 30 across both
  saves (the cap itself holds; the renderer/disk divergence is ADV-154).
- **C same-name upsert**: saving `Alpha` again with later options left exactly
  one `Alpha` at the FIRST position carrying the later settings (`copies:3`).
  Defended.
- **D read-modify-write clobber**: seeded non-default `theme`, `recentsCap`,
  `recentFiles`, `homeTools`, `tabStyle` and `geometry`, captured the normalized
  baseline after the print window settled, then saved a preset, saved a second,
  and deleted one. After each write the disk's non-`printPresets` fields were
  byte-for-byte equal to the baseline - no clobber or loss. (The seam reads main's
  live in-memory `current`, and `save` updates `current` synchronously before its
  write queue, so the read-modify-write sees concurrent settings changes.)
  Defended.
- **E rapid double-save in one task**: two programmatic `[data-print-preset-save]`
  clicks in a single `page.evaluate`. Exactly one `Rapid` entry on disk and one
  option in the picker; the pre-existing `Seed` entry was not lost. Defended.
- **F disabled while running / apply safe**: with the document loaded and a real
  printer selected, stub `window.tflex.printJob` to a never-resolving promise and
  click Print; all four preset controls (`[data-print-preset]`,
  `[data-print-preset-name]`, `[data-print-preset-save]`,
  `[data-print-preset-delete]`) reported `disabled: true` while `running`. Applying
  a preset on the loaded surface re-seeded the controls (`duplex` -> `longEdge`)
  with no page error. Defended.
- **G name edges**: whitespace-only name showed `[data-print-preset-error]` and
  wrote nothing to disk or the picker; exactly 40 chars persisted; a 41-char
  `fill` was truncated to 40 at entry by `maxLength={40}` (the field visibly held
  40 chars) and the main-process normalizer independently rejects >40, so no
  wrong-name write could reach disk silently; a duplicate name replaced rather
  than appended. Defended.
- **H offline**: `printPage.on('request')` recorded zero http(s) requests across
  opening the print window and saving a preset. The new path adds no network call.
  Defended.

### Phase 81 printPresets diff-pass - design critique of the changed surface (skill: design-critique)

User: someone who prints PDFs and wants to reuse a set of print options. Job on
this surface: pick a saved option snapshot, or save the current options under a
name. Success: the right options reload and stay available next time.

- Must-fix - **States (ADV-154):** the success notice claims a save the disk did
  not take at the cap boundary; the picker then carries entries that disappear on
  reopen. Try: enforce the 30 cap in `savePreset` (refuse a 31st with the
  existing `[data-print-preset-error]` wording, or evict the oldest) so notice,
  picker and disk always agree.
- Should-fix - **Inputs:** the name field offers no overwrite signal before
  replacing an existing preset; `Save preset` silently upserts a duplicate name.
  Try: when the typed name matches an existing preset, change the button to
  "Overwrite preset" (or add a hint) before the click.
- Nice-to-fix - **States:** when a preset is selected and a control is then
  changed, the select still reads as that preset with no "modified" cue. Try: a
  subtle dirty marker on the select, matching how the app marks unsaved tabs.
- Strengths to keep: the snapshot deliberately excludes `deviceName`/page scope
  so applying a preset never silently re-routes a job; the controls disable
  cleanly while a print runs; a blank name fails loud; same-name upsert keeps its
  original position; the preset row renders before the printer list so it is
  reachable even when no printer is installed.

Pass/fail per attack surface:

     `...prev` and writes only `spellCheck`, so it cannot clobber sibling fields
     locally. **But the `settings.changed` echo filter never compares
     `spellCheck`** - `sameSettings` (settingsEcho.ts:81-98),
     `differsOnlyInRecentFiles` (:111-138) and `differsOnlyInGeometry` (:212-233)
     all omit it. That is exactly the DEF-072 class the file's own header
     (:51-60) declares closed. A stale echo whose only drift is `spellCheck`

     latest toggle. See ADV-156 for the repro.
2. **DICTIONARY LOAD - PASS.**
   `DictionaryService.load` (dictionary.ts:20-35) maps ENOENT -> `not-found`,
     any other throw -> `read-failed`, and only returns `ok`; it never rejects.
     `spellClient.loadSpellDictionary` try/catches the IPC/absent bridge and
     resolves `{dictionary:null, error}` (spellClient.ts:33-45), so the renderer
     can never see an unhandled rejection. The wrapper renders
     `[data-spell-status]` for the off/loading/error states
     (SpellCheckTextarea.tsx:263-270,341-345) and computes `ready` only on
     `enabled && status==='ready' && dictionary!==null` (:189), so a failed load

     spellDictionary.test.ts (missing dir, dir-in-place-of-file) and

     uses; TextPropertiesPanel routes it to `onTextChange` and the blur to
     `onTextCommit` (:266-267), so single-commit-on-blur is preserved and no
     engine op fires (undo/redo remain the host session's). The popover container
     `onMouseDown preventDefault` (:324) keeps the textarea focused so accepting
     does not blur prematurely. The 150 ms debounce gates tokenising on
     `effectiveText != null` (:190-195), so keystrokes are never blocked; the
     mirror renders the debounced text so offsets stay aligned. Right-click on a
     correctly spelled token returns before `preventDefault` (:216) -> native
     menu. Composition/IME is untouched because the wrapper still owns a single
     real `<textarea>`. The one break: a misspelled token whose first letter has

4. **FIX DELTA (DEF-482) - PASS.**

     settings write path (App.tsx:1256-1260 bumps `settingsWriteSeqRef` and sets
     `settingsPersistedRef` in the same synchronous step, so the snapshot cannot
     lag the seq). DocumentView.tsx:3716-3730 adds
     `spellCheck.enabled` + `spellCheck.status` to `textSelectionKey`; every
     pre-existing key component is retained, so no other selection publish is
     dropped. The only extra publishes are the loading->ready transition, which
     is a bounded one-per-load and is required so the Inspector receives the
     resolved spell state. The persist handler does not fight the echo for
     `spellCheck` **only because the echo filter ignores it** - which is ADV-156,
     not a defence. The fix's own behaviour is otherwise correct (T5 pass).
5. **OFFLINE RULE - PASS.**
   No `fetch`/`http(s)`/`XMLHttpRequest`/`net.request`/`axios`/`WebSocket`
     reference exists anywhere in the delta (grep exit 1). The dictionary is read
     from `assets/dictionary/` by `DictionaryService` and shipped by
     electron-builder; the load path never touches the network.

### Phase 82 spell-check diff-pass - design critique of the changed surface (skill: design-critique)

User: someone editing text in a PDF who wants typos surfaced and fixed without
leaving the document. Job on this surface: see misspellings while typing, and
replace one with a correction in place. Success: the underline is trustworthy and
the fix lands where the user pointed, in one action, without breaking the edit
session.

- Must-fix - **States (ADV-157):** right-clicking a misspelled token with no
  candidate suggestions paints an empty suggestion listbox - a control that
  promises choices and offers none. Try: when `suggestions.length === 0`, do not
  open the popover (fall through to the native menu) or show a single
  "No suggestions" disabled row, so the popover is never an empty box.
- Should-fix - **States / consistency (ADV-156):** the spell-check toggle's
  persisted value can be reverted by a stale settings echo, so the switch and
  the underlines can disagree with what the user last chose. Try: add
  `spellCheck` to `sameSettings` / `differsOnlyInRecentFiles` /
  `differsOnlyInGeometry` and to the DEF-072 coverage guard so the toggle the
  user sees is the toggle that survives.
- Nice-to-fix - **Affordance:** the toggle is an icon-only button; its state is
  carried by `aria-pressed` + an active class + a `title`, but there is no
  visible text label. Sighted keyboard users relying on the title only see it on
  hover. Try: keep the icon but expose "Spell check on/off" in the row, matching
  the surrounding text-panel controls.
- Strengths to keep: the status line is honest ("Loading dictionary...",
  "Spell check unavailable - dictionary could not be loaded", "Spell check
  off") rather than a blank; the mirror is `aria-hidden` and pointer-transparent
  so the single `<textarea>` keeps all real interaction and accessibility; the
  debounce keeps tokenising off the keystroke path; the toggle disables with an
  explanatory title when no spell host is wired.

## ADV-156: `settings.changed` echo filter ignores `spellCheck`, so a stale echo reverts the user's spell-check toggle (DEF-072 class reopen)

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM
- Affected phase: 82 (offline spell-check; C1 contract + DEF-482 fix delta)
- Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-480 (MEDIUM) - filed by CTO on ADV triage, 2026-10-02; assigned to frontend-dev

What I did: read the CTO-named echo path and reproduced the decision function the
App calls. `src/renderer/state/settingsEcho.ts` compares every `AppSettings` field
in `sameSettings` (:81-98), `differsOnlyInRecentFiles` (:111-138) and
`differsOnlyInGeometry` (:212-233) - except the new `AppSettings.spellCheck`
(types.ts:249). `App.tsx:169` imports `shouldApplyEcho` and `App.tsx:1310-1319`
calls it on every `settings.changed` payload; on `true` it runs `setSettings(echo)`
wholesale. `trackAndSave` (App.tsx:1256-1260) advances `settingsWriteSeqRef`,
snapshots `settingsPersistedRef` and fires `window.tflex.saveSettings`; main
(`settings.save` in services/settings.ts:1374-1416) normalises, writes, and
broadcasts the full normalised settings including `spellCheck` via `broadcast`
(index.ts:288-291). I wrote `test/unit/renderer/adv_phase82_settingsEcho.test.ts`
and ran `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/renderer/adv_phase82_settingsEcho.test.ts`
-> 5 passed, pinning the observed behaviour:
`sameSettings({spellCheck:on},{spellCheck:off}) === true` and
`shouldApplyEcho(staleEcho(spellCheck:off), writeSeq=2, persisted(spellCheck:on)) === true`.
I also confirmed the DEF-072 coverage guard (`settingsEcho.test.ts:905-957`)
lists every optional field but not `spellCheck`, so the "every optional
AppSettings field" guard passes while the new field is uncovered.

Expected: `sameSettings` must return false when only `spellCheck` differs (the
DEF-072 invariant, stated verbatim in the settingsEcho.ts header at :51-60), and
`shouldApplyEcho` must discard a stale echo whose only drift is `spellCheck`, so
the user's latest flip survives.

What happened: with every other field equal, a `spellCheck`-only difference is
invisible to the filter. Concretely: user toggles spell check OFF (write 1),
then ON (write 2) - or toggles once while any second settings write is in
flight. The renderer's local state is already write 2 (ON) before the echo for
write 1 lands. That stale echo carries `spellCheck:{enabled:false}`; `sameSettings`
ignores the field, finds every other field equal, returns true, and
`App.tsx:1319 setSettings(staleEcho)` writes the toggle back to OFF. If echo
delivery is ordered, echo 2 then restores ON and the reversal is transient; if
writes interleave at main's `await writeFile` and echo 2 arrives before echo 1
(DEF-037 exists precisely because that reordering happens), the wrong value
persists until the user toggles again. The same omission lets a
recent-files-only or geometry-only echo that also carries an outdated
`spellCheck` apply and revert the toggle.

Evidence: `test/unit/renderer/adv_phase82_settingsEcho.test.ts` (green while the
defects stand; invert the assertions to guard the fix);
`src/renderer/state/settingsEcho.ts`; `src/renderer/App.tsx:1256-1260,1310-1319`;
`src/shared/types.ts:249`; `test/unit/renderer/settingsEcho.test.ts:905-957`.

Suggested fix (for the developer, not applied by me): add a `spellCheck`
comparison (`enabled` and `language`) to `sameSettings`,
`differsOnlyInRecentFiles` and `differsOnlyInGeometry`, and add `spellCheck` to
the DEF-072 `requiredFields` coverage list in settingsEcho.test.ts.

## ADV-157: a misspelled token with no suggestions opens an empty suggestion popover

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: LOW
- Affected phase: 82 (offline spell-check; C2 UI, SpellCheckTextarea)
- Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-481 (LOW) - filed by CTO on ADV triage, 2026-10-02; assigned to frontend-dev

What I did: inspected `SpellCheckTextarea.handleContextMenu`
(src/renderer/spell/SpellCheckTextarea.tsx:201-231) and `suggestSpellCorrections`
(src/shared/spell.ts:160-186), then reproduced the candidate filter against the
shipped dictionary in
`test/unit/renderer/adv_phase82_settingsEcho.test.ts` (run
`npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/renderer/adv_phase82_settingsEcho.test.ts`
-> 5 passed). A 46-character run of `q` (under `SPELL_WORD_MAX = 48`) is tokenised
as one token, `isSpellMisspelled` returns true, and `suggestSpellCorrections`
returns `[]` because the double loop requires a candidate sharing the first
letter with a length within two - there is no `q` word of length 44..48 in the
bundled list.

Expected: per the task's own rule, a context-menu action must never open an empty
popover. `handleContextMenu` already returns early (native menu) for a correctly
spelled word or a non-token offset; a misspelled token with zero candidates must
do the same (or show a "No suggestions" row).

What happened: `handleContextMenu` calls `e.preventDefault()` and
`setPopover({token, suggestions: suggestSpellCorrections(...).slice(0,LIMIT), ...})`
whenever the token is misspelled, regardless of `suggestions.length`
(:216-228). The render then paints the `[data-spell-suggest]` `role="listbox"`
with an `aria-label="Spelling suggestions"` and zero `[data-spell-suggestion]`
children (:317-340) - a control that offers no options and no "no suggestions"
message.

Evidence: `test/unit/renderer/adv_phase82_settingsEcho.test.ts`
("ADV-157 repro"); `src/renderer/spell/SpellCheckTextarea.tsx:201-231,317-340`;
`src/shared/spell.ts:160-186`.

Suggested fix (for the developer, not applied by me): in `handleContextMenu`,
when the computed `suggestions` array is empty, return before `preventDefault`
so the native menu shows, or render a single disabled "No suggestions" row.
