## ADV-158: Booklet creep under subset 'both' (the default) is derived from the side count in the main compose but from the physical-sheet count in the preview, so the printed creep disagrees with the preview

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: pure probe `probe2.cjs` (bundled from `src` with esbuild, run under
Node). For a 16-page selection, `subset='both'`, `bookletGutterPt=0`,
`bookletCreepPt=10`, I (a) extracted the `padding-left` values from
`composePrintHtml` (the real main compose) and (b) recomputed the renderer
preview exactly as `usePrintControls.bookletSides` does - `sheetCount =
bookletPageCount(pages)/4` (physical sheets = 4), `sheetIndex =
floor(sideIndex/2)` - using the same shared `bookletSideOffset`.

Expected: byte-for-byte the same margins in preview and compose (CTO ruling 2:
the shared module is "consumed by BOTH the renderer preview and the main compose
so they can never disagree"; e2e for 16 pages expects `[0,10,10,0]` per physical
sheet).

Actual: `compose` = `[0,0,3.333,3.333,6.667,6.667,10,10,10,10,6.667,6.667,3.333,3.333,0,0]`
(16 cells = 8 sides), `preview` = `[0,0,10,10,10,10,0,0]` (8 cells), `match:false`.
Cause: `src/main/services/print.ts:441-446` calls
`bookletSideOffset(sheetIndex, sheets.length, ...)` where `sheets.length` is the
SIDE count (2 x physical sheets for `both`) and `sheetIndex` is the side index;
the preview calls it with the physical-sheet count/index
(`usePrintControls.ts` `bookletSides`). For subset `front`/`back` the two agree
(probe2 `creep-front`/`creep-back` first-cell values `[0,10,10,0]` match). Only
the default `both` disagrees.

Evidence: `<scratch>/probe2.ts` line `creep-both`; `src/main/services/print.ts:441-446`;
`src/renderer/components/usePrintControls.ts` (`bookletSides`).

Suggested fix (not applied): in `composePrintHtml`, derive the physical sheet
count/index for `both` (e.g. pass `sheets.length / (settings.bookletSubset === 'both' ? 2 : 1)`
and, for `both`, `sheetIndex = floor(sheetIndex/2)`), or have the preview call
`bookletSideOffset` with the side count.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-484 (MEDIUM). CTO triage: real break of the shared-source-of-truth rule (Phase 83 CTO ruling 2) - the preview and the main compose disagree on booklet creep for the default subset `both`. Owner: backend-dev. Fix in `composePrintHtml` (derive the physical-sheet count/index for `both`) so both consumers match.

## ADV-159: A Page order set under Single/N-up leaks into Booklet: compose stacks the 2-up sheet 1x2 or mirrors the page pair, while the control is shown disabled and the preview is always two columns

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: HIGH

What I did: pure probe `probe2.cjs`. Built a `PrintDialogState` with
`layoutMode:'booklet'` and `pageOrder:'verticalReversed'` (reachable: set N-up to
4 and Page order to Vertical reversed while in Single, then switch Layout to
Booklet - the select is disabled but its value is retained).
`buildPrintSettings(state)` returned `{pageOrder:'verticalReversed',
pagesPerSheet:2, landscape:true, layoutMode:'booklet'}`. Then
`composePrintHtml({images:[A,B], settings:{layoutMode:'booklet', pagesPerSheet:2,
pageOrder:<order>}})` was run for each order and the emitted grid and image DOM
order inspected.

Expected: Booklet is a fixed 2-column landscape imposition; the disabled Page
order control must not affect it (ruling 7: non-applicable controls are disabled,
not silently applied; ruling 2: preview and compose cannot disagree).

Actual: for `vertical`/`verticalReversed` the composed grid becomes
`grid-template-columns: repeat(1,...); grid-template-rows: repeat(2,...)` - a
1x2 stacked portrait sheet, not 2-up. For `horizontalReversed`/`verticalReversed`
the two page images swap in the DOM (`A_first:false`) - the saddle-stitch side is
mirrored. The preview ignores `pageOrder` entirely and always draws 2 columns
(`PrintPanel.tsx` booklet branch), so preview and print disagree. `seedPrintDialogState`
also carries the stale `pageOrder` into the Booklet surface.

Evidence: `<scratch>/probe2.ts` `P3-pageorder-grid`/`P3-pageorder-order` (probe.cjs)
and `build-settings-booklet-stale-pageOrder`/`seed-booklet-stale-pageOrder`;
`src/renderer/pdf/printSettings.ts:204-238` (`base.pageOrder = state.pageOrder`
is spread into the booklet settings); `src/main/services/print.ts:434`
(`printSheetLayout(perSheet, settings.pageOrder)` for booklet).

Suggested fix (not applied): force `pageOrder:'horizontal'` on the booklet/poster
settings build (or have `composePrintHtml` use the horizontal layout for booklet),
so the disabled control cannot change the imposition.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-485 (HIGH). CTO triage: real break of ruling 7 (non-applicable controls are disabled, not silently applied) and ruling 2 (preview/compose agreement) - a stale `pageOrder` from Single/N-up silently changes the booklet imposition to a stacked/mirrored sheet. Owner: backend-dev. Force the fixed horizontal 2-up layout in booklet compose; the renderer must not carry a stale pageOrder.

### Phase 83 diff-pass - design critique of the changed print surface (skill: design-critique)

Click to retry."}` and the error branch (`UpdateIndicator.tsx:253-267`) renders a **Retry** button with `onClick={onDownload}`; `onDownload` (`UpdateIndicator.tsx:172-179`) calls `api.download()`. ## ADV-163: Classifier bypass - a malformed-feed error whose embedded XML contains the literal phrase "No published versions on GitHub" is still misread as up-to-date

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: LOW

What I did: enumerated the error strings reachable from electron-updater 6.8.9 `GitHubProvider.getLatestTagName`/`getLatestVersion` and drove each through the REAL `isNoReleasesError` classifier via the real `UpdateService` (read-only probe; output `adv162-classifier-result.json`). `Bad credentials`, the wrapped 401, a channel-file 404, a plain malformed feed, DNS/offline failures and an HTTP 403 rate-limit all mapped to `error` correctly.

Expected: only the genuine empty-feed signatures map to `up-to-date`: `No published versions on GitHub` (thrown by `feed.element("entry", false, ...)`, `GitHubProvider.js:48`) and the `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'assets')` TypeError (`PrivateGitHubProvider.js:26`). Every auth/network/parse failure must surface as `error`.

Actual: `ERR_UPDATER_INVALID_RELEASE_FEED` (`GitHubProvider.js:107-109`) wraps the raw feed body: `Cannot parse releases feed: ${e.stack || e.message},\nXML:\n${feedXml}`. Because the matcher is an unanchored substring test (`/no published versions/i`, `update-service.ts:97`), a malformed feed whose XML body contains that phrase is classified as empty. Probe: the fabricated message `Cannot parse releases feed: Error: Unexpected close tag,\nXML:\n<feed><title>No published versions on GitHub</title></feed>` returned `{"kind":"up-to-date"}` instead of `error`. Reachability is low (the feed URL is fixed to the operator-controlled public repo `tanzimtipu/tflex-releases`, and the response body would have to carry the literal phrase while failing to parse), but it contradicts the fix's stated intent that a real failure must never be swallowed. This is an informational bypass, not likely exploitable by a remote attacker.

Screenshot: none (probe output `adv162-classifier-result.json`).

Disposition: REJECTED - informational hardening candidate, not reachable by any actor the product defends against. The feed URL is fixed to the operator-controlled public repo tanzimtipu/tflex-releases over HTTPS, and the bypass needs that repo's response body to carry the literal phrase "No published versions on GitHub" while failing to parse; a MITM is out of threat model for a signed HTTPS feed. A genuine empty feed still correctly maps to up-to-date. No fix in this phase; the raw-body substring risk is noted for future hardening (e.g. match electron-updater error codes, not message substrings).

### OTA updater fix diff-pass - design critique of the changed update-state surface (skill: design-critique)

User: an installed-build user whose app checks for updates on launch or via the toolbar/About surface. Job: know truthfully whether a newer version exists and install it. Success: the check result is never a lie, and a failure offers a recovery action that actually works.

- Must-fix - **States (ADV-162):** the error state offers a "Retry" control that silently does nothing because it calls `download()` instead of `check()`. An error state must state what went wrong and the action it offers must work. Try: wire the error branch's Retry to `update.check()`.
- Should-fix - **Copy:** the error body renders the raw electron-updater string verbatim (`state.message`), e.g. "Unable to find latest version on GitHub (https://github.com/...) ... HttpError: Response code 401". Try: a friendly first line ("Couldn't check for updates. Check your connection and try again.") with the raw text behind an expandable details.
- Should-fix - **Affordance:** the error chip's `aria-label` promises "Click to retry." while the visible label is only "Retry"; once wired, keep label and behaviour in sync.
- Nice-to-fix - **Consistency:** the About dialog's error state offers only OK (dismiss) while the toolbar offers Retry. After fixing Retry, offer it on both surfaces so they agree.
- Strengths to keep: the state machine is exhaustive (`assertNever`), `error` is a first-class `UpdateState` with the message preserved end-to-end, and the classifier now truthfully surfaces real failures instead of demoting them to up-to-date - the truthful-state rule is the strongest part of this change.

## ADV-164: Redaction drops a glyph when a mark touches the axis-aligned bounding box of a ROTATED glyph but not the glyph itself (over-removal)

- Session: diff-pass (phase 84 gate)
- Suggested severity: LOW

What I did: adversarial diff-pass on the Phase 84 content-stream rewrite (`src/shared/redaction.ts` `tokenizeContentStream`/`removeRedactedGlyphs`, `src/main/services/engine.ts` `applyRedactions`/`_applyRedactionsImpl`, `src/main/services/settings.ts` `normalizeRedactionColor`, the new `RedactionOverlay.tsx`). I read the diff, then bundled the pure shared module with the repo's esbuild and attacked the SAME geometry the engine calls, and drove the real engine in the built app through `e2e/phase84_redaction_adversary.spec.cjs`. Per-vector results:

1. Partially covered `TJ` array - PASS. Pure: middle "SECRET" removed exactly (5 glyphs), siblings `AA`/`BB` intact. Engine-level on a real pdf-lib Helvetica page (`[(AA) (SECRET) (BB)] TJ`): apply removed exactly 6 glyphs, `exportText` went `AASECRETBB` -> `AABB`, saved stream `[(AA) -4056 (BB)] TJ` (redacted run absent, siblings byte-intact).
2. Mark spanning a transform - PASS. `q 2 0 0 2 100 50 cm ... (ABCDE) Tj`: mark over glyph C removed exactly 1 glyph, exportText `ABCDE` -> `ABDE`; a 90-degree `cm` mapping removed exactly the visually covered glyph. The rotated-glyph AABB over-approximation is the one break (below).
3. Encrypted / open-prefix document - PASS. Built an AES-256 PDF with an EMPTY user password (owner-restricted open-prefix), opened it with no prompt, applied a mark: 12 glyphs removed, `SECRET-ALPHA` gone, `PUBLIC-BETA` intact. Save produced a re-parseable 1-page file (254-byte decoded stream), and reopening through the app loaded it and returned `PUBLIC-BETA`. The rewrite corrupts neither the decrypted prefix nor the xref. (`pdf-lib``getContents()` + the stream `transform` decrypts correctly, so `decodePageContentStreams` sees plaintext.)
4. No-text mark - PASS. A mark over a vector-only rectangle returned `removedGlyphs: 0` plus the readable warning "Redaction mark 1 on page 1 covered no removable text (images and vector content are not removed)." The unrelated `KEEP-ME` text and the rectangle's path ops (`0.2 0.3 0.6 rg`, `h f`) survived the rewrite. No silent no-op, no wrongly removed glyph.
5. Undo/save byte round-trip - PASS. apply -> `engine.undo` restored the term -> re-apply -> save -> reload. Saved page stream balanced (`q`/`Q` = 3/3, `BT`/`ET` = 2/2), redacted run replaced by a kerning number (`[-7668] TJ`), `PUBLIC-BETA` intact, reloaded file returns `PUBLIC-BETA` only.
6. Extra stress - PASS except the rotated-glyph case. Multiple `Tf` (8/8), nested `q/Q` CTM restore (10/10), `'`/`"` show operators, page-edge partial coverage, unresolvable font -> typed `RedactionUnsupportedError` with nothing applied, no-intersection -> byte-identical content.

Expected: a mark that visually covers no part of a glyph must not remove it. `removeRedactedGlyphs` is supposed to remove "exactly the glyphs whose page-space boxes intersect a mark".

Actual: `glyphBox` (`src/shared/redaction.ts:603-631`) transforms the four glyph-cell corners and returns their **axis-aligned bounding box**; `rectsIntersect` (`:492-499`) tests the mark against that AABB. For a glyph rotated by an angle that is not a multiple of 90 degrees, the AABB is strictly larger than the true rotated quad, so a mark can touch the AABB sliver and remove a glyph it does not visually cover. Repro (pure module, deterministic): content `q 0.7071067811865476 0.7071067811865476 -0.7071067811865476 0.7071067811865476 200 200 cm BT /F1 10 Tf 1 0 0 1 0 0 Tm (A) Tj ET Q`; the single glyph's true 45-degree quad has corners (201.77,198.23) (205.30,201.77) (197.53,209.55) (193.99,206.01), AABB x[193.99,205.30] y[198.23,209.55]; call `removeRedactedGlyphs(content, [{ rect: { x: 194.0, y: 207.0, width: 0.5, height: 2.0 } }], fixedAdvance500)`; the rect lies entirely OUTSIDE the quad but its AABB returns `removedGlyphs: 1` (output `... Tm [-500] TJ ...`) instead of `0`. Reachability: the app's Rotate verb sets page `/Rotate` (`engine.ts:2121`), which does NOT rotate content-stream text, so this fires only for documents whose content stream rotates text itself - watermarks, vertical table headers/labels, and imported/rotated-text PDFs. It is an over-removal (confidentiality-safe: it removes more, never less) but it silently deletes a neighbouring character the user did not mark.

Screenshot: none (pure-geometry repro; deterministic output logged by `e2e/phase84_redaction_adversary.spec.cjs` test `ADV84-A`, probe `A2c-over-removal`, and by `screenshots/adv-p84-tj-partial-applied.png` / `screenshots/adv-p84-encrypted-prefix-applied.png` / `screenshots/adv-p84-no-text-warning.png` for the passing vectors).

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-491 (LOW). Owner backend-dev: tighten the glyph hit test in `src/shared/redaction.ts` from the rotated glyph cell's axis-aligned bounding box to the true rotated quad, so a mark that touches only the AABB sliver does not remove a glyph it does not cover; add the deterministic 45-degree repro as a unit case. Dispatched as TFL-409. Note: this entry is the only ADV from the Phase 84 diff-pass; vectors 1-3 and 4-6 otherwise PASSED.

## Phase 84 redaction diff-pass - design critique of the changed redaction surface (skill: design-critique)

User: a TFlex user who must permanently remove confidential text (a name, an account number) before sharing or archiving a PDF. Job: mark the sensitive region and trust that the SAVED file no longer contains it. Success: after save + reopen, neither text extraction nor copy/paste returns the redacted term, while the surrounding text is unchanged.

- Should-fix - **Truthfulness (states):** "Apply redactions" reads as an irreversible commit, but the engine pushes ONE undo snapshot and app-level Ctrl+Z fully restores the redacted text (verified: after `engine.undo` the term `SECRET-ALPHA` was extractable again). A user who believes the redaction is permanent can silently un-redact and save the secret back in. Try: make the permanence boundary explicit - e.g. after apply, label the state "Redactions pending save" and either warn on undo ("This will restore the redacted text") or drop the redaction snapshot from the general undo stack.
- Should-fix - **Affordance (accessibility):** the `[data-redact-unsupported]` button is `disabled` with a `title` tooltip. A disabled button is not focusable and does not reliably fire hover on all platforms, so the "disabled-with-tooltip" reason promised by the spec is unreachable for keyboard and some pointer users. Try: render it as `aria-disabled` (focusable) with the reason as visible/`aria-describedby` text, or a small inline note beside it.
- Nice-to-fix - **Accessibility (targets):** the swatches and mode buttons are 22x22 px, below the 44x44 px touch target. Try: keep the visual size but pad the hit area.
- Nice-to-fix - **States (success):** a successful apply only clears the pending marks and shows warnings; there is no positive confirmation that the glyphs were removed. Try: a short `role="status"` line ("Redacted N characters on page X").
- Strengths to keep: every verb is a real `<button>` with a stable `data-redact-*` hook; the fail-loud `[data-redact-warning]` (`role="alert"`/`role="status"`) makes a no-text mark non-silent; the typed `redaction-unsupported` refusal leaves the document byte-for-byte unchanged; the enabled/disabled states of Apply/Clear/Undo correctly track the pending-mark count.

## ADV-179: The Bates stamp ignores `AppSettings.editDefaultFont` - the label is always drawn in Helvetica even when the user's default edit font is Times, Courier or a bundled family (REQUIREMENTS.md:5333)

- Session: diff-pass (phase 89 gate)
- Suggested severity: LOW

What I did: adversarial diff-pass on the Phase 89 Bates diff. Statically traced the font that `engine.addBates` actually uses from every caller. `_addBatesImpl` embeds `settings.font ?? 'Helvetica'` (`src/main/services/engine.ts:4385`, and the same expression selects the label font again for the encodability pre-check at `:4365`/`:4369`). The only product caller is the renderer: `BatesDialog` builds `settings` without a `font` key (`src/renderer/components/BatesDialog.tsx:218`), and `onBatesConfirm` forwards that payload unchanged to `engineRef.current.addBates?.(...)` (`src/renderer/App.tsx:6405-6408`). Nothing between the dialog and the engine injects `AppSettings.editDefaultFont`. Compare the established engine pattern for the text-edit op, which does consult it: `payload.font ?? DEFAULT_SETTINGS.editDefaultFont ?? 'Helvetica'` (`src/main/services/engine.ts:2892`).

Expected: REQUIREMENTS.md:5333 (Phase 89, item 6) - "The op embeds `settings.font ?? AppSettings.editDefaultFont ?? 'Helvetica'` via the existing `embedEditFont`". A user whose Edit default font is `Times` (or `Courier`, or a bundled family) should get that font in the Bates label.

Actual: the label is drawn in Helvetica for every UI-driven run, regardless of the persisted `editDefaultFont`. The fallback chain in the op stops at `'Helvetica'`; `editDefaultFont` is never consulted on the Bates path.

Reproducibility: deterministic. Confirmed by source trace plus the executed probe suite (below): the engine-level attacks A1-A8 all pass, which is exactly why this defect hides - it is a missing fallback, not a wrong stamp. To observe: set `editDefaultFont: 'Times'` in settings.json, open the Bates dialog, apply with any prefix; the run succeeds but the baked stamp is Helvetica (the `TFbates*` font resource resolves to the Helvetica standard font). The probe would need one added assertion that the payload reaching `engine.addBates` carries a `font` (the renderer test `phase89BatesDialog.test.tsx` currently asserts the payload shape without `editDefaultFont`). Fix is renderer-side: seed `font: settings?.editDefaultFont ?? 'Helvetica'` into the payload in `onBatesConfirm`, or have the op read the live default.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-512 (CTO, TFL-464, 2026-10-03)

## ADV-180: The Bates encodability pre-check is font-agnostic - a bundled font that CAN draw a Latin-Extended/Greek prefix is refused anyway (over-refusal), because the check hardcodes StandardFont/WinAnsi semantics (REQUIREMENTS.md:5333)

- Session: diff-pass (phase 89 gate)
- Suggested severity: LOW

What I did: read the pre-check that gates the whole op before any mutation. `_addBatesImpl` calls `undrawableStandardFontChars(label)` for every label (`src/main/services/engine.ts:4364-4372`), and that helper is built on `sanitizeForStandardFont` (`src/main/services/engine.ts:5236-5246`, `:5208-5228`), which unconditionally drops every code point `> 0xFF` and replaces controls with a space. This runs for every `settings.font`, including the bundled families that `embedEditFont` actually embeds as real TTFs (`src/main/services/fonts.ts:208-250`): `Liberation Sans` and `DejaVu Serif` cover U+0100..U+FFFF ranges (Latin Extended-A, Greek, Cyrillic) that the embedded font can draw but WinAnsi cannot.

Expected: REQUIREMENTS.md:5333 says the refusal is for "a prefix/suffix character the **chosen** standard font cannot encode"; the check should reflect `settings.font` (or, at minimum, accept what the font that will actually be embedded can encode).

Actual: any prefix/suffix containing a single code point above U+00FF is refused with `engine-error` even when the chosen bundled font can encode it. The op never reaches `embedEditFont`, so the decision is made against the wrong font.

Reproducibility: executed and deterministic. `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/main/phase89BatesAdversary.test.ts` A4b/A5c log:
`[p89adv|A4b] bundled Greek font=DejaVu Serif ok=false code=engine-error msg=addBates: the DejaVu Serif font cannot encode "Ω" in the stamp label`
`[p89adv|A5c] Latin-Extended-A font=DejaVu Serif ok=false code=engine-error msg=addBates: the DejaVu Serif font cannot encode "ā" in the stamp label`
Independent confirmation that the chosen font CAN draw both: embedding `assets/fonts/DejaVuSerif.ttf` via `@cantoo/pdf-lib` + `@pdf-lib/fontkit` and calling `font.encodeText` returns real glyph ids (`Ω -> <0001>`, `ā -> <0002>`, `Я -> <0003>`), while `世 -> <0000>` (`.notdef`). So the CJK refusal is correct, but the blanket `> 0xFF` rule over-refuses every bundled-encodable non-Latin-1 character. Reachability note: the shipped `BatesDialog` exposes no font control, so this is reachable only through the IPC channel directly (a buggy/hostile caller or a future font picker), not through the current UI. No corruption: the refusal is all-or-nothing and leaves the bytes unchanged.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-513 (CTO, TFL-464, 2026-10-03)

## Phase 89 diff-pass - named-attack results (session: diff-pass, phase 89 gate)

The Phase 89 diff was attacked with an engine-level probe, `test/unit/main/phase89BatesAdversary.test.ts` (A1..A11 plus A4b/A5c observations). It mirrors the dev engine test's fixtures and adds the named hostile sequences. The probe was EXECUTED against the shipped engine once the build mutex freed:

`npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/main/phase89BatesAdversary.test.ts --reporter=verbose` -> `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 13 passed (13)` (duration 1.81s), exit 0. The only log lines were the two A4b/A5c observations quoted in ADV-180.

Did NOT reproduce - EXECUTED and PASSED:

1. **First + last page** (`engine.ts:4344-4354`, `:4389-4397`): `pageCount = doc.order.length`; `origIdx = doc.order[page1-1]` maps the 1-based visible page through the live order, so page 1 and page `pageCount` both resolve. Probe A1.
2. **Out-of-order `[3,1,2]`** (`engine.ts:4361`, `:4389-4398`): `formatBatesSeries` and the stamp loop both iterate `settings.pages` in list order; the k-th listed page gets `startNumber + k`. Probe A2.
3. **Padding smaller than the number** (`src/shared/bates.ts:54`): `String(number).padStart(padding,'0')` pads to a MINIMUM width and never truncates; padding 1 with number 12 yields `12`. Probe A3.
4. **Font substitution** (StandardFont + bundled paths, `fonts.ts:208-250`): `embedEditFont(..., false, false)` is exercised for `Times`/`Liberation Sans`/`DejaVu Serif`; no crash path located in the metric/encode calls. Probe A4 (observed A4b/A5c are ADV-180).
5. **Unencodable CJK prefix** (`engine.ts:4364-4372`): the label check runs before `snapshotDocWithPdf`, so the whole op is refused before any mutation and no undo entry is pushed. Probe A5.
6. **Repeated apply** (`engine.ts:4386`, `:4449-4451`): each run mints a fresh random `runId` for its resource names and markers and pushes its own snapshot, so run 2's undo restores run 2's pre-state (which already contains run 1). Probe A6.
7. **Undo/save round-trip** (`engine.ts:4382`, `:4449-4452`): one `snapshotDocWithPdf` per run => one undo entry; only listed pages get `addContentStream(ref)`, so unselected page content objects are not rewritten. Probe A7 also compares raw unselected content bytes across a serialize + reopen.
8. **Bates-then-watermark** (`engine.ts:4468-4489` watermark scan vs `:303` Bates marker): the two markers use distinct prefixes and `readWatermarkMarker` returns null for a Bates stream; `deleteWatermark` (`:4557-4593`) removes only streams whose marker id matches, and cleans only the watermark's own resource names. Probe A8 asserts the watermark list/pages and that Bates labels and markers survive a watermark delete.

Confirmed breaks (filed above): ADV-179 (editDefaultFont ignored), ADV-180 (font-agnostic encodability pre-check).

Extra stress vectors, also EXECUTED and PASSED (beyond the eight named attacks):

9. **Reorder before stamp** (A9): `applyOp {kind:'reorder', page:2, param:0}` then `addBates([1])` stamps the moved original page (CHARLIE) and leaves visible pages 2-5 unlabelled - the `doc.order` mapping is honoured after a reorder.
10. **AcroForm document** (A10): `addBates` + `undo` restores the form-bearing bytes and the `fullname` field; re-apply + save + reopen keeps both the field and the `AF-001` label. No AcroForm loss on the content-stream bake.
11. **User-password AES-256 document** (A11): open with the user password, stamp, save; the output reopens with the same password and returns `E-001` alongside `SECRET-DOC`. The bake does not corrupt an encrypted save.

Verdict: **FAIL** - two confirmed requirement deviations (ADV-179, ADV-180), both LOW severity. Attacks 1-11 all PASS against the shipped engine: no content-stream bake, undo, save-round-trip, marker-collision or Bates/watermark-interference break was found, and no crash, hang, data loss or document corruption was produced. The fail is not a data-integrity failure; it is two unmet REQUIREMENTS.md:5333 clauses (the `editDefaultFont` fallback and the chosen-font encodability semantics) plus the design-critique Should-fix items above.

## Phase 89 Bates dialog - design critique of the changed UI surface (skill: design-critique)

User: a legal/accounting user who must apply sequential Bates numbers to selected pages of a document before filing. Job: configure prefix/suffix/start/padding/position, choose the pages, and apply a stamp that survives save. Success: the applied labels are correct, sequential and visible, and any refusal is legible and changes nothing.

- Should-fix - **Validation timing (inputs):** `Apply` is enabled for an invalid `padding` (e.g. the user types `0` or `2.5`): `valid` checks only `pages.length` and `startNumber` (`BatesDialog.tsx:215-216`), so the engine's generic "settings are invalid" is only surfaced after the click. Try: validate `padding` in `valid` (1..64) and show the inline hint before apply, matching the range hint already present.
- Should-fix - **Copy (error states):** a bad option shows the engine's bare `engine-error` text (e.g. "addBates: settings are invalid") in `[data-bates-report]`; it names no field. Try: map known refusals to field-level copy ("Padding must be a whole number from 1 to 64.").
- Nice-to-fix - **Affordance (preview):** the preview frame shows only the first/last label in a text hint and the next label floating in the slot; it does not visualize the chosen page set, so a narrowed range is only legible from the hint. Try: label the hint with the actual page numbers, not just the count.
- Nice-to-fix - **Accessibility:** the nine position buttons are ~22px swatches (same `watermark-slot` class as Phase 18); below the 44x44 target. Try: pad the hit area.
- Strengths to keep: every control is a real `<button>`/`<input>` with a stable `data-bates-*` hook; `aria-pressed`/`aria-label` on the position grid; the rising-edge re-seed guard keeps the post-apply report and the user's page scope while persisting defaults; the Apply button disables while busy and the report is `role="alert"` on error / `role="status"` on success.

## Phase 93 Book View page-turn diff-pass (TFL-535) - adversarial probe

Session label: `diff-pass`. Scope: the renderer-only Book View page-turn rework
(TFL-519): `src/renderer/components/BookView.tsx` plus the Book View CSS block
(`src/renderer/styles.css` ~`19057-19290`, the `tf-book-turn-*` keyframes and the
`data-book-turn-cycle` restart selectors). Product code, tests, `REQUIREMENTS.md`
and `AGENTS.md` were read but not modified. Spec:
`e2e/phase93_adversarial_flip_probe.spec.cjs`; screenshots
`screenshots/phase93/adv-*.png`; run logs
`test-fixtures/TFL-535-phase93-adversary-run{1,2,3,4}.log`.

Exact command (Electron build must exist first; `dist/renderer` was rebuilt from
source with `npm.cmd run build:renderer` because the checked-in bundle predated the
Phase 93 CSS; `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` unset per the qa note):

- `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- phase93_adversarial_flip_probe.spec.cjs --reporter=line`
  -> **8 passed (1.6m)**, exit 0 (run4, the final run; run3 also 8 passed).

Attack-surface results (all PASS against the shipped build):

- **A. One-tick and ~30ms-spaced bursts forward/backward at both clamps -
  HOLDS.** A 6-click one-tick burst coalesces to exactly two steps (`1 -> 3`);
  a 14-click 30ms spaced burst lands on page 6, clean; a next burst at page 12
  stays on 12 with Next disabled; a Previous-nav burst at page 1 stays on 1 with
  Previous disabled; a plain next still advances afterwards. Watch: `maxLeaves = 1`,
  `turningNoLeaf = false`.
- **B. Direction reversal and a queued clamp step - HOLDS.** At `[5,6]`, 3x next +
  3x prev in one tick returns to `[5,6]`. At `[9,10]`, a 4-click one-tick burst
  (turn + queued next) lands exactly `[11,12]`, Next disabled, no residual.
- **C. Single/double toggled mid-turn - HOLDS.** Double->single and
  single->double while a leaf is mid-swing both leave `leaves = 0`,
  `data-book-turning` cleared, no `book-view-page-turning` class, and the surface
  turns normally afterwards.
- **D. Close Book View mid-turn then re-enter - HOLDS.** Closing mid-swing unmounts
  the view with no surviving turning figure; re-entry starts on page 1 with a clean
  single committed surface (`1` canvas), no ghost, and Next advances. (The layout
  resets to the stored comic default on re-entry - by design, Phase 66 feature D.)
- **E. Page-zone clicks at both spread edges and over the crease during a turn -
  HOLDS.** Right (next), left (prev) and a 2px-crease-centre click fired mid-swing
  all settle clean; both edge zones still act afterwards (the crease seam shares
  the page-zone edges, so a dead-centre crease click is a page-zone click, not a
  separate control - expected).
- **F. Reduced motion flipped MID-SESSION then back - HOLDS.** After a live CDP
  `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the next turn mounts no leaf, sets no
  `data-book-turning`, commits `[3,4]` instantly with no half transform; clearing
  the preference live restores the animated leaf on the next turn (`[5,6]`).
- **G. Animations OFF via Preferences MID-SESSION - HOLDS.** Toggling
  `[data-prefs-animations]` off while Book View is open leaves Book View mounted and
  usable; the next turn mounts no leaf, sets no turning state, and commits `[3,4]`.
- **H. Storm audit - HOLDS.** 12 alternating page-zone/nav turns, then 6
  open/close Book View cycles: no residual leaf, no stuck `data-book-turning`, no
  ghost canvas (idle single = 1 canvas, idle double = 2), `anyTurningClass = 0`, the
  armed `arrow` annotation tool survives every turn, and nav still advances after
  the cycles.

Watch invariant across every sequence: `maxLeaves <= 1` and
`turningNoLeaf = false` (the stage never claimed turning with zero leaf mounted).

Verdict: **no break confirmed.** Every named hostile attack class held against the
shipped build; no crash, hang, residual turning state, stale committed page, doubled
canvas, lost armed tool, or stalled control was produced. No ADV entry is filed.

### Reproduced non-findings (probe iteration notes)

The first probe run (`run2`) failed 4 assertions that were **probe-assumption
errors, not product breaks**, and were corrected before the passing runs:

1. In single layout the whole page figure's click action is always `next`; the
   backward clamp can only be driven through the Previous nav. The corrected test A
   uses `[data-book-prev]` for the first-page clamp.
2. The reversal test originally started on `[1,2]`, where the left page zone is
   clamped (`noPrev`), so the reverse clicks were correct no-ops and the turn
   coalesced forward. Corrected test B starts on `[5,6]`.
3. Re-entering Book View re-seeds the layout from the stored comic default (single
   here), so the re-entry layout is not the in-session toggle. Corrected test D
   asserts page 1 + a valid layout and drives advancement via Next.
4. The 2px crease seam shares the page-zone edges, so a dead-centre crease click at
   rest lands on the adjacent page zone. Corrected test E asserts clean state and a
   valid spread instead of no movement.

### Run-1 environment note (not a product finding, not filed as ADV)

The first `npm.cmd run build:renderer` (needed to refresh the stale checked-in
bundle) picked up another in-flight task's transiently broken source state and the
dev app booted with `ReferenceError: useBackdropClose is not defined`, so all 8
tests failed at `waitForSelector('.sample-card')`. A second build minutes later, after
the concurrent dialog-shell edit settled, produced a bootable bundle and the run
above. This is the shared-workspace build-race hazard, not a Phase 93 defect:
`DeletePageDialog.tsx`/`DialogShell.tsx` were being edited concurrently and no longer
reference the unbound symbol. The `.paperclip-build.lock` was held by this adversary
for the rebuild and released afterwards.

## Phase 93 Book View page-turn - design critique of the changed UI surface (skill: design-critique)

User: a reader who opens a PDF or comic and wants to page through it in a book-like
spread. Job: turn pages forward/back without flicker, at a glance knowing what page
they are on. Success: the spread always shows the page the indicator names once the
turn settles, and both directions are reachable. Context: a read-only overlay opened
from the DocumentView canvas; closing restores the document view.

- Should-fix - **Clarity (indicator vs. content):** the progress label leads the turn
  (`displayIndex = turn.target`) while the spread holds the outgoing index for the
  ~350ms swing, so the header can read "Page 5-6" over a spread still showing `[3,4]`.
  This is deliberate and short, but on a slow turn or a chained turn it is the one
  moment header and page disagree. **Try:** keep the lead, but only after the first
  rAF of the turn, or dim the label by the same transient class until commit.
- Nice-to-fix - **Consistency (layout persistence):** toggling to single (or double)
  is session-only; closing and reopening Book View returns to the stored default
  (`ADV` probe D: double -> re-entry single). A reader who set their preferred layout
  must re-set it each entry. **Try:** remember the last-used Book View layout for the
  session (or write it back as the comic reading default) - if that is inside Phase
  66 feature D scope.
- Nice-to-fix - **Affordance (single-mode back):** in single layout the page body
  turns only forward; going back needs the Previous nav button, while double layout
  gives both edge zones. **Try:** a left-edge back zone in single mode for parity.
- Nice-to-fix - **Affordance (crease hit):** the 2px crease has no hit area of its
  own and shares the page-zone edges, so a click on the seam page-turns. Not harmful,
  but it is a visible "dead-looking" strip that is actually active. **Try:** give the
  crease `pointer-events: none` so the zones are the only hit targets.
- Strengths to keep: transform-only turn over the already-painted outgoing canvas (no
  blank pre-paint frame); the reduced-motion / Animations-OFF path mounts no leaf and
  commits synchronously with no half transform; the single queued step and the
  `animationend`-then-400ms-fallback commit leave no residual leaf or stuck
  `data-book-turning` under any burst tested; nav buttons disable at both clamps; the
  armed annotation tool survives turns and the read-only surface never doubles a
  canvas.

### Design critique: the dock/home EDIT-mode remove badge (skill: design-critique)

User: someone curating their action dock / home launcher. Job: remove a tool from the
row in edit mode. Success: the badge is obviously the verb's remove control and one
press removes the right tool.

  two same-class controls now rely on different containment stories (verb padding vs
  `.welcome` padding). **Try:** a shared badge-containment contract so one fix does not
  silently diverge from the other.
- Nice-to-fix - **Affordance (target size):** the badge is 16x16 px, below the 24px
  desktop minimum; it now sits flush in the verb's top-right corner and overlaps the
  verb glyph's corner. **Try:** keep `top:0; right:0` but consider a 1-2px inset that is
  still non-negative, so the glyph corner stays readable.
- Strengths to keep: the badge reads as the verb's corner control (z-index 1, themed
  `--sem-attention`); it is a `role="button"` span, never a nested `<button>`; it stops

  accessible name; the pen/plus stay real in-row flex items, so this diff moved only

## ADV-181: The Phase 95-B recurrence guard is a first-match source scan - a later `.action-dock-minus` rule, an `inset` shorthand, `!important` or a custom property re-introduces the negative badge overhang while the guard still reports all-pass

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: LOW

What I did: ran `node test-fixtures/phase95-adversary/adv546_guard_defeat.cjs`
(read-only). It loads the shipped `src/renderer/styles.css`, replicates the guard's
exact `ruleBody` / `allBodies` / `decl` helpers from
`test/unit/renderer/phase95_dockMinusContainment.test.ts`, and evaluates the four
guard predicates against the shipped sheet plus five hostile cascade mutations:
M1 appends a second `.action-dock-minus { top:-5px; right:-5px }`; M2 appends the
higher-specificity `.action-dock[data-dock-edit='true'] .action-dock-minus { top:-5px;
right:-5px }`; M3 appends `.action-dock-minus { inset:-5px -5px auto auto }`; M4
appends `top:-5px !important; right:-5px !important`; M5 appends
`top: var(--adv-badge-overhang)` with `--adv-badge-overhang:-5px`.

Expected: the guard, whose stated purpose (`...test.ts:1-16`) is to prevent recurrence
of the `top:-5px; right:-5px` overhang, fails when a later cascade rule re-introduces a
negative inset.

Actual: all four guard assertions PASS for every mutation M1-M5 (log:
`test-fixtures/phase95-adversary/adv546_guard_defeat.log`). `ruleBody(".action-dock-minus {")`
returns only the FIRST matching rule, so a later duplicate rule that wins the cascade
(M1 computes effective `top=-5px; right=-5px`) is invisible to test 1; `allBodies` is
consulted only for the verb-overflow selector, never for the badge, so the higher-
specificity M2 override is never seen either. M3/M4/M5 additionally bypass `decl`,
which only reads `top`/`right` longhands terminated by `;` (an `inset` shorthand, an
`!important` value and a `var()` value are not parsed). The guard pins the shipped
literal only: any future stylesheet edit that restores the exact defect passes CI.

Screenshot: n/a - console run; the full output is in the session report above and in
`test-fixtures/phase95-adversary/adv546_guard_defeat.log`.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-517 (Phase 95; recurrence-guard hardening, routed to frontend-dev on TFL-531). The runtime oracle is the stronger guard, but the unit source-scan must also resist a later duplicate `.action-dock-minus` rule, an `inset` shorthand, `!important` and a `var()` overhang.

## ADV-182: In the dock's arrows lane the remove badge is partially clipped again the moment a verb is hovered

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: `node test-fixtures/phase95-adversary/adv546_lane_hover.cjs`. Launch the
shipped dev app through `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` `launchApp`, open `report.pdf`, enter dock
EDIT mode, resize the window to 700x900 (the rung where the dock engages its arrows
lane: `data-dock-arrows-lane="true"`), then measure every `[data-dock-minus]` against
the ACTIVE clip ancestor - the lane scroller `[data-dock-scroll]`, whose computed
`overflow-x`/`overflow-y` are both `auto` - before and after hovering a leading verb
(`rotate`) and a middle verb (`split`).

Expected: the Phase 95 ruling 2 containment contract - the badge lives inside its
verb's border box at `top:0; right:0`, so the lane scroller can never PARTIALLY clip it
(the same PARTIAL-CLIP contract `e2e/phase95_dock_edit_overflow.spec.cjs` asserts).

Actual: at rest every badge is flush with the scroller's clip top (`topEscape=0`,
contained within the 0.5px tolerance). On hover the verb lifts by
`--motion-translate-micro` (2px, `styles/animations.css:73`), so the verb top moves
from `clipTop` to `clipTop-2` and the badge (which rides the verb) paints above the
scroller's top edge: measured `verbTop=799 clipTop=801 badgeTop=798.04 topEscape=+2.96
partial=true` for both hovered verbs. The lane's `overflow-y:auto` then cuts the top
~3px of the badge (and the verb's top edge). The oracle measures only the resting
state, so it never sees this.

Screenshot: `screenshots/p95-lanehover-rotate.png`, `screenshots/p95-lanehover-split.png`.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-518 (Phase 95; in-scope recurrence, routed to frontend-dev on TFL-531). Hovering a verb in the arrows lane re-clips the badge top by ~3px. The fix plus the extended hover oracle are required before the phase can close.

Attack-surface result (issue items 1-6):

1. Dropped props: NONE. No removed glyph in the diff carried `onClick`, `style`,

   glyph either already declared `aria-hidden` or was inside an `aria-hidden` container
   or a labelled control; no removed glyph carried a `title`/`aria-label`, and no
   migrated control became icon-only. The `icon={X}` prop sites
   (`Inspector.tsx:463`, `DialogShell.tsx:174`) both sit on labelled/`aria-label`ed
   controls and the wrapper is used inside them.

   extra element; `className` is forwarded to that root, so no wrapper element was
   introduced to capture clicks or change flex sizing.

   `16->sm(16)`, `13->xs(14)`, `28->hero(32)`, `12->xs(14)`), but every chrome surface is
   governed by the pre-existing context SVG sizing layer (`.app-header svg`,
   `.titlebar svg`, `.context-panel svg`, `.side-rail svg`, `.inspector svg`,
   `.command-palette svg`, `.ann-toolbar svg` = 18px; `.action-dock svg`/`.canvas-pill
   svg` = 20px; `.stage-rail svg` = 22px), which overrides the SVG `width`/`height`
   attributes - so those were already painted at the token size before the migration.
   The uncovered deltas are cosmetic (+1..+4px: `TextPropertiesPanel`, `AnnotationCommentBox`,
   `PreferencesDialog`, `Welcome`, `MultiPane`, `PrintWindow`) and the one fixed-size
   container that changed (`AnnCommentIcon`, badge box 16->20, glyph 10->14) was itself
   resized to match the pre-existing `.ann-comment-icon { min-width:20px; height:20px }`
   CSS, so the glyph now FITS where it previously clipped. No hit-area or alignment
   regression.
5. Exceptions: HOLD. `Pin` still encodes state via `fill` (`CommandPalette.tsx:538-543`);
   `Slash` still renders dynamic size/stroke (`AnnotationToolbar.tsx:727-731`); `StickyNote`
   still scales with zoom (`AnnotationOverlay.tsx:2075`). The direct-render census over the
   changed files finds exactly these two live exceptions in-file (the third is in the

6. High-risk surfaces: labels and handlers unchanged on all nine (DeletePageDialog,

## ADV-186: Two stacked DialogShell surfaces both dismiss on ONE Escape — the shell has no top-most Esc guard

- Session: phase-92 gate (TFL-513-G diff-pass)
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: ran a Playwright probe through the canonical launcher only (`test-fixtures/phase92-adversary/probe_stacking.cjs`, launched via `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`). Opened the About sheet from the Command Palette (`[data-palette-tool-id="about"]`), then injected `update:statusChanged` `{kind:"available"}` (App.tsx:1715-1726 `onCheckForUpdate` opens the Update prompt without closing About, so `aboutOpen` and `updatePromptOpen` are both true). Verified the stack: `[data-about-dialog]` = true, `[data-update-prompt]` = true, `[data-dialog-shell]` count = 2. Then pressed Escape once.

Expected: per TFL-513-G attack item 6, the top surface owns Esc — one Escape dismisses only the Update prompt and leaves About open (no double-close).

Actual: one Escape dismissed BOTH surfaces. After the keypress: `{ about: false, update: false, shells: 0 }` (`test-fixtures/phase92-adversary/probe_stacking.log`). Cause: `DialogShell.tsx:146-156` adds an independent `window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey)` for every open shell, and `e.preventDefault()` does not stop the other listeners, so every open shell's `onClose` fires on the same keydown. There is no owner/stack guard. This widened UpdatePromptDialog's Esc, which pre-Phase-92 was scoped to its backdrop's React `onKeyDown` (HEAD `UpdatePromptDialog.tsx:566-568`), to a global window listener; AboutDialog already had a window listener at HEAD (`AboutDialog.tsx:241-248`), so the pair previously only both-closed when focus sat inside the update backdrop. Post-adoption it closes both unconditionally.

Screenshot: n/a (probe). Fixture/evidence: `test-fixtures/phase92-adversary/probe_stacking.cjs`, `test-fixtures/phase92-adversary/probe_stacking.log`.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-525 (MEDIUM). CTO triage (2026-10-03): real, reachable via Update prompt stacked over About; frontend-dev to add a top-most guard so only the topmost open `DialogShell` handles Esc. Fix-linked below.

## ADV-187: Three adopted dialogs lost their custom close-X accessible name to the shell default "Close dialog"

- Session: phase-92 gate (TFL-513-G diff-pass)

What I did: for every adopted surface, compared the pre-Phase-92 `.modal-close` `aria-label`/`title` (from `git show HEAD:...`) with the current DialogShell close button, and checked which adopters pass the additive `closeAriaLabel` prop (only `AboutDialog.tsx:350`, `PreferencesDialog.tsx:316`, `UpdatePromptDialog.tsx:532`). The shell default is `closeAriaLabel = "Close dialog"` (`DialogShell.tsx:125`, emitted at `DialogShell.tsx:219-220`).

Actual: three adopters omit `closeAriaLabel` and now render the default, losing their shipped name:
- `PasswordPromptDialog.tsx:100-109` — X is now `aria-label`/`title` "Close dialog"; HEAD `PasswordPromptDialog.tsx:100` was `aria-label="Cancel"` (no title). The click still cancels.
- `CloseTabPromptDialog.tsx:101-107` — X is now "Close dialog"; HEAD `CloseTabPromptDialog.tsx:120` was `aria-label="Cancel close"`. The click still chooses "cancel".

'Cancel OCR' : 'Close'}` — i.e. while OCR is running the header X no longer announces that it cancels the run.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-526 (LOW). CTO triage (2026-10-03): frontend-dev to pass `closeAriaLabel` on the three adopters (PasswordPromptDialog "Cancel", CloseTabPromptDialog "Cancel close", OcrDialog dynamic `running ? 'Cancel OCR' : 'Close dialog'`). Fix-linked below.

## ADV-188: The Bates update dialog defaults the page scope to All pages, so editing a partial run silently re-stamps every page (a 2-page run becomes all pages)

- Session: phase-90 gate (diff-pass)
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: exercised the Phase 90 update path in isolation. Mounted the shipped `BatesDialog` in update mode (`test/unit/renderer/phase90BatesDialogScopeAdversary.test.tsx`) with an applied run that covers only pages 1-2 of a 5-page document (`editTarget.pages = [1,2]`, `totalPages = 5`), then clicked `[data-bates-apply]` (the "Update numbering" action) without touching the page-scope control, and captured the `settings` the dialog emits to `onConfirm`.

Expected: editing an applied run's position/formatting keeps the run on its OWN pages. The same phase's watermark update mode does exactly that: `WatermarkDialog` seeds `rangeAll = false`, `rangeFrom = pages[0]`, `rangeTo = pages[pages.length - 1]` from `WatermarkInfo.pages` (`src/renderer/components/WatermarkDialog.tsx:242-250`).

Actual: the dialog emits `settings.pages = [1,2,3,4,5]`. The update-mode re-seed block sets `setRangeAll(true)` unconditionally (`src/renderer/components/BatesDialog.tsx:233`), and `batesPagesForScope(true, ...)` returns every page (`BatesDialog.tsx:150-152`). `onBatesConfirm` forwards that payload unchanged to `engine.updateBates(docId, editId, settings)` (`src/renderer/App.tsx:6444-6451`), and `_updateBatesImpl` removes every stream of the run then re-bakes the handed `settings.pages` (`src/main/services/engine.ts:4794-4798`). So a user who opens the REVIEW list, picks a two-page Bates run, nudges its X/Y or padding and presses "Update numbering" gets the number stamped on every page - a document-wide content change they did not request (recoverable with one undo, and the "All pages" radio is visible, but the default is wrong and inconsistent with the sibling watermark edit).

Reproducibility: deterministic. Probe log:
`[p90adv|SCOPE] run pages=[1,2] emitted pages=[1,2,3,4,5] editId=bates-1`
Command: `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/renderer/phase90BatesDialogScopeAdversary.test.tsx --reporter=verbose` -> Test Files 1 passed / Tests 1 passed, exit 0. The shipped `test/unit/renderer/phase90BatesDialog.test.tsx:249-276` covers update mode but never asserts `settings.pages`, so the suite does not catch it. Engine proof that `updateBates` faithfully applies the `pages` it is handed: `test/unit/main/phase90BatesAdversary.test.ts` E7. Chunk D's own report records the same effect from the other side: its Phase 90 e2e had to "set the edit scope explicitly (the update dialog honestly defaults to All pages)", which worked around the default rather than fixing it.

Fix (not applied - the adversary does not patch): seed the Bates update mode from `editTarget.pages` exactly as the watermark update mode does (when `pages.length > 0`: `rangeAll = false`, `rangeFrom = pages[0]`, `rangeTo = pages[pages.length - 1]`), and add the missing page-scope assertion to `phase90BatesDialog.test.tsx`.

Screenshot: n/a - probe + log (paths above).

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-527 (MEDIUM). CTO triage (2026-10-03): confirmed Phase 90 defect (criterion 3 - editing an applied run must apply the intended change, not a document-wide one); inconsistent with the sibling `WatermarkDialog` update mode. Fix assigned to frontend-dev as TFL-633; blocks Phase 90 phase-close. Design-critique Should-fix #2 (the signature row's edit pencil performs select) is REJECTED for this phase - Phase 90 Ruling 7 defines a signature row's "edit" as the on-canvas move/resize reached by selecting the row, so the behaviour matches the contract; the glyph-label polish is out of scope here.

## Phase 90 (TFL-632) adversarial diff-pass — named-attack results

Session: phase-90 gate (diff-pass). Scope: the Phase 90 diff only - explicit Bates x/y placement, the addressable Bates run (`getBates`/`updateBates`/`deleteBates`), the unified review list, and `updateWatermark`. Product code was read but never modified. Probes: `test/unit/main/phase90BatesAdversary.test.ts` (E1..E9) and `test/unit/renderer/phase90BatesDialogScopeAdversary.test.tsx`.

Exact commands and results (build mutex held by this adversary and released afterwards):
- `npm.cmd run build` -> exit 0 (typecheck + `dist/renderer` vite build + `dist/main`/`dist/preload` esbuild).
- `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/main/phase90BatesAdversary.test.ts --reporter=verbose` -> **Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 9 passed (9)** (2.25s), exit 0.
- `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/renderer/phase90BatesDialogScopeAdversary.test.tsx --reporter=verbose` -> 1 passed; log `[p90adv|SCOPE] run pages=[1,2] emitted pages=[1,2,3,4,5] editId=bates-1` (the ADV-188 confirmation).

Attack-item results:

1. **E1 edit a run after a reorder - HOLDS.** `addBates([2,4])`, then `applyOp {kind:'reorder',page:4,param:0}` (ECHO to front). `getBates` reports the run at the new visible pages `[3,5]` with labels `['A1-001','A1-002']`; `updateBates` to `[1,2]` removes both old markers (pages 3 and 5 clear) and bakes exactly one marker on each new page, and ONE undo restores the post-reorder, pre-edit state.
2. **E2 delete one of two runs sharing a prefix - HOLDS.** Two runs both prefix `S-` on `[1,2]` and `[4,5]`; deleting the first by id leaves the second's `pages`/`labels` intact and clears pages 1-2. Deletion is keyed on the marker `id`, never the prefix.
3. **E3 update to each page edge - HOLDS.** Updated a one-page run through `(0,0)`, `(PW,0)`, `(0,PH)`, `(PW,PH)` and `(14400,14400)`. The drawn `Tm` clamps only to the page bounds: right edge `x = PW - w`, bottom edge `y = 0.2h`; all `Tm` values are inside the page. An out-of-bounds update (`x=-5`) is refused and leaves the run and the bytes intact.
4. **E4 a Phase 89 marker (no `settings`) listed + refused-on-edit + deletable - HOLDS.** A hand-baked `%TFLEX-BATES {id,page,label}` marker lists with the shipped defaults, `updateBates` refuses with the readable "older version" message and mutates nothing, and `deleteBates` removes exactly it. A Phase-90-shaped marker whose `settings` fails validation (`{pages:'nope'}`) is treated identically (E4b observation: it lists as a legacy run).
5. **E5 Bates-then-watermark-then-`updateWatermark` interference - HOLDS.** After `addBates` + `addWatermark`, `updateWatermark` re-bakes only the watermark (pages `[1,2]`, new text); the Bates labels and markers survive. ONE undo reverts only the watermark text; deleting the watermark leaves the Bates run fully intact, and the two marker prefixes never cross-read.
6. **E6 two runs on overlapping pages - HOLDS.** Runs `O1-` on `[1,2,3]` and `O2-` on `[2,3,4]`: pages 2 and 3 carry two interleaved markers each. Deleting run 1 removes only its streams (pages 2-3 drop to one marker, page 1 clears) while run 2 survives; updating run 2 to page 5 afterwards does not resurrect run 1.
7. **E7 undo/save byte round-trip after update and after delete - HOLDS.** A six-page run on `[1,3]` updated to padding 2/start 7/x30/y40 gives a new serialized SHA; ONE undo restores the pre-update SHA byte-for-byte, ONE redo restores the post-update SHA. Save + reopen returns `B-07`/`B-08` on pages 1 and 3 and a `getBates` record with padding 2, x 30, y 40. `deleteBates` likewise round-trips byte-for-byte through one undo/redo, and a save + reopen returns an empty `getBates` and no labels.
8. **E8 (extra) a non-finite UPDATE refuses before removing the existing run.** For `x = NaN, Infinity, -1, 14401` the update is a typed `engine-error`, the run's labels are unchanged and the serialized bytes are hash-identical - the validate-before-remove ordering holds, so no partial edit is possible.
9. **E9 (extra) repeated update/delete storm stays stable.** Six alternating updates (including an out-of-order page list) leave exactly one marker per selected page and one run in `getBates`; deleting a run added repeatedly empties every page with no resurrection.

Engine verdict: **no engine break confirmed.** No content-stream, marker, undo, save-round-trip, overlap or Bates/watermark-interference break was produced; no crash, hang, data loss or document corruption. The only confirmed break this pass is renderer-only (ADV-188, the update dialog's page-scope default).

## Phase 90 residual e2e-failure triage (TFL-632) — regression vs pre-existing

Chunk D ran the two C1-touched specs and left six residual failures. Method: inspect the C1/C2 diff (the Inspector `review-elements` slot, the ContextPanel unified list, the App wiring) and the Phase 90 file set, then check whether each failing assertion executes Phase 90-changed code. The two C1/C2-RE-POINTED assertions themselves (`chunk456` P6/P8: `[data-inspector-slot="review-elements"]`, `[data-review-category="signatures"]`; layout_retest DEF-318: the signatures category title is hit-testable) **PASS** per Chunk D's counts (11/2 and 1/4), so the unified-list change did not regress the surfaces it re-pointed.

All six residual failures are pre-existing / unrelated to the Phase 90 diff - none is a Phase 90/C1 regression:

1. `phase36_chunk456_gate` **P4, dock full-refusal text** (notice reads "Pinned Zoom out to the dock" where the spec expects the "Dock is full" refusal). Not Phase 90. The dock-pin limit lives in `CommandPalette`/`dockModel`/`commandPalette`/`toolsRegistry`, and `git status` shows NONE of those files modified in the working tree - the palette pin contract is byte-identical to HEAD, so the failure exists at HEAD. ## Phase 90 Bates update + unified review list - design critique of the changed UI surface (skill: design-critique)

User: a legal/accounting user who must keep a Bates series correct across a filing. Job: see every applied review element in one place, jump to it, change an applied run's position/numbering without disturbing the rest of the document, and delete what is no longer needed. Success: an edit changes only what the user intended, and every row is reachable and legible.

- Should-fix - **Error prevention (edit scope):** the Bates update dialog defaults the page scope to "All pages" instead of the run's own pages (ADV-188), while the sibling watermark update seeds the run's scope. A user nudging X/Y on a 2-page run silently stamps every page. Try: seed `rangeFrom`/`rangeTo` from `editTarget.pages` (and set `rangeAll=false`) exactly as `WatermarkDialog` does; keep "All pages" a deliberate user choice.
- Should-fix - **Consistency (row actions):** for a signature row, `[data-review-element-edit]` performs the same action as select (jump to the placement) and the pencil glyph promises an editor that does not open (`App.tsx` `onEditReviewElement` returns after `onSelectReviewElement`). The tooltip says "Edit <label>" but no editing surface appears. Try: label the signature row's action "Move/Resize on page" (or hide the pencil for signatures) so the affordance matches the outcome.
- Nice-to-fix - **Clarity (row labels):** a Bates row shows `first - last` labels and a watermark row shows `type · text`; both are good, but the signature row reads only `Signature p<page>`, so two placements on one page are indistinguishable. Try: include a short id suffix or placement time.
- Nice-to-fix - **Affordance (empty categories):** each category keeps its heading with a `No ... applied.` line, which is honest; consider collapsing the three empty categories to a single "No Bates numbering, watermarks or signatures applied." line to cut REVIEW-panel length when only annotations exist.
- Strengths to keep: the list is one component re-parented by both panels (no second copy); every row is a real `<button>` with a stable `data-review-*` hook and an explicit `aria-label`; select/edit/delete are disabled (not hidden) when the host supplies no handler, and a per-row `[data-review-element-error]` slot carries a loud, readable refusal; the update dialogs carry `data-bates-mode="apply"|"update"` / `data-watermark-mode="apply"|"update"` so the mode is observable.

## ADV-189: Every dialog paints elevation-2, but the Phase 96 ladder and doc declare dialog/sheet = elevation-3

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: LOW

What I did: opened `report.pdf`, clicked `[data-open-preferences]`, and measured the computed `box-shadow` of the prefs dialog root (`document.querySelector('[data-prefs-dialog]').closest('[data-dialog-shell]')`, whose class is `sheet sheet-prefs`) against fresh probe elements carrying `var(--elevation-2)` and `var(--elevation-3)`, in light, dark and frosted. Command: `node test-fixtures/phase96-adversary/probe_state_and_dialog.cjs`; the shipped `e2e/phase96_design_system.spec.cjs` `dialog` guard (spec lines 411-430) measures the same element but only `console.log`s it.

Expected: `docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:176` names `dialog / sheet` as level 3 and `:195` maps `--shadow-dialog -> var(--elevation-3)` (pinned by `test/unit/renderer/designSystem.test.ts:219-240`); the dialog/sheet shadow should therefore equal `var(--elevation-3)`.

Actual: the dialog shadow equals `var(--elevation-2)` exactly and never `--elevation-3`, in all three themes. Light measured `rgba(15,23,42,0.10) 0 2px 8px, rgba(15,23,42,0.12) 0 8px 24px` (= elevation-2); dark `rgba(0,0,0,0.5) 0 2px 8px, rgba(0,0,0,0.55) 0 8px 24px`; frosted the same elevation-2 plus glass insets. Both dialog surfaces consume `--shadow-popover`, not `--shadow-dialog`: `.modal-dialog { box-shadow: var(--shadow-popover); }` (`src/renderer/styles.css:5728`) and `.sheet { box-shadow: var(--shadow-popover); }` (`src/renderer/styles.css:8616`). After the Phase 96 ladder, `--shadow-dialog` has exactly one consumer in the whole stylesheet, `.reading-view` (`styles.css:18239`) — not a dialog. The `designSystem.test.ts` elevation suite passes because it only asserts the token mapping (`--shadow-dialog === var(--elevation-3)`), never a dialog consumer; the shipped e2e dialog guard never asserts the shadow at all.

Reproducibility: deterministic. Probe record: `{"pass":1,"check":"dialog-elevation","shellClass":"sheet sheet-prefs","dialogShadow":"rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.1) 0px 2px 8px 0px, rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.12) 0px 8px 24px 0px","elevation2":"rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.1) 0px 2px 8px 0px, rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.12) 0px 8px 24px 0px","elevation3":"rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.14) 0px 4px 16px 0px, rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.18) 0px 12px 40px 0px"},"matchesElevation2":true,"matchesElevation3":false`.

Fix (not applied — the adversary does not patch): either consume `--shadow-dialog` on `.modal-dialog`/`.sheet` (and add the dialog assertion to the shipped e2e's `dialog` guard) or amend `DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` sections 10/12 to declare dialog/sheet at level 2. One of the two must move; the doc and the shipped dialog cannot both be right. Note the consumer predates Phase 96 (Phase 92 adopted DialogShell with `--shadow-popover`), but the level-3 claim and the orphaned `--shadow-dialog` token are introduced by this Phase 96 diff.

Screenshot: screenshots/phase96/dialog-light.png (shipped spec), screenshots/phase96/adv-zero-page.png (probe).

- Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-529 (LOW, Should-fix). CTO triage (2026-10-04): the Phase 96 ladder and DESIGN-SYSTEM.md declare dialog/sheet = level 3, but .modal-dialog (styles.css:5728) and .sheet (styles.css:8616) consume --shadow-popover (level 2), leaving --shadow-dialog (level 3) orphaned. Phase 96 owns the elevation ladder (Ruling 5), so the shipped dialog must move onto the documented step. Assigned frontend-dev (TFL-649): consume --shadow-dialog on .modal-dialog/.sheet, add a dialog-shadow assertion to the shipped e2e, keep the unit token mapping. Blocks Phase 96 phase close.

## Phase 96 (TFL-648) design-system visual refresh — design critique of the changed UI surface (skill: design-critique)

User: a TFlex desktop PDF user on Windows (knowledge worker / document reviewer) who opens, reads and edits PDFs. Job on the changed surfaces: find and run a tool (command palette), read a document's facts and its per-page editable content (Inspector / ContextPanel), and understand why a surface is empty. Success: every surface is self-explanatory, and every control the empty state or panel shows does its job. Flow position: inside the app shell, after a document or none is open.

### Must-fix (blocks ship)
- None. No crash, hang, data loss or unreachable control was produced.

### Should-fix (before broader rollout)
- **Consistency (elevation):** a dialog is the deepest common overlay, but it reads at the same depth as a menu/popover (level 2), contradicting the ladder the doc and unit test claim (ADV-189). **Try:** consume `--shadow-dialog` on `.modal-dialog`/`.sheet`, or move the doc to level 2.
- **Accessibility (states):** the decorative empty-state hero mark is 2.2-2.9:1 in light/dark, under the doc's own 3:1 graphic floor (ADV-190). **Try:** strengthen the tint or state the decorative exemption explicitly.

### Nice-to-fix (when there's room)
- **States (empty surfaces):** the two designed empty states added for zero-page/no-document are unreachable, so users never see them and the suite cannot verify them (ADV-191). **Try:** re-point them at a reachable condition or remove them.

### Strengths to keep
- One shared `EmptyState` (optional hero / headline / help) with `data-*` pass-through, so every adopter keeps its existing hook and there is a single place to change the pattern.
- The DEF-528 hero override is pinned by a genuine DOM-match guard (not a string pin) and the mark renders at exactly 32px in all three themes.
- Interaction states are visibly distinct: hover / active / selected / disabled each use a different token step, and selected carries the accent ring.
- Docked panels stay flat and the command palette rides level-2 as documented; the palette no-results and edit-content empty states read clearly and are keyboard-reachable.


## ADV-192: Phase 97 per-machine installer overwrites Adobe Acrobat's default handler for all eight PDF-family extensions

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: HIGH

What I did: Read electron-builder's own NSIS wiring and the machine registry (read-only). `node_modules/app-builder-lib/out/targets/nsis/NsisTarget.js:630-650` feeds every `win.fileAssociations` row into the `APP_ASSOCIATE` macro, and `node_modules/app-builder-lib/templates/nsis/include/FileAssociation.nsh:65-74` writes `WriteRegStr SHELL_CONTEXT "Software\Classes\.${EXT}" "" "${FILECLASS}"` - the extension's DEFAULT value - in addition to the `OpenWithProgids` candidate value. The live registry confirms the eight types are currently owned per-machine by Adobe Acrobat, with no per-user choice to shield them: `reg query "HKLM\Software\Classes\.xdp"` -> `(Default) REG_SZ Acrobat.XDPDoc`; PowerShell probe of `HKLM\Software\Classes\.<ext>` -> `.aaui=Acrobat.aaui`, `.bpdx=AcrobatBPDXFileType`, `.fdf=Acrobat.FDFDoc`, `.pdx=AcrobatPDXFileType`, `.rmf=Acrobat.RMFFile`, `.sequ=Acrobat.Sequence`, `.xdp=Acrobat.XDPDoc`, `.xfdf=Acrobat.XFDFDoc`; and `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\FileExts\.<ext>\UserChoice` is ABSENT for all eight (probe script: `test-fixtures/phase97-adversary/reg_probe.ps1`, run via `powershell -File`).

Expected: per Phase 97 (`docs/phase-specs/phase-97.md` lines 9 and 35) and `electron-builder.yml:36-43` ("This never sets the Windows default handler on its own - the user picks that in Settings"), Jovrel is only a SELECTABLE candidate for the non-pdf family types (an `OpenWithProgids` entry). The user's existing Acrobat default for these eight types must be untouched.

Actual: the per-machine installer's generated `registerFileAssociations` overwrites `HKLM\Software\Classes\.<ext>` (Default) from `Acrobat.*` to `Jovrel.<ext>` for all eight types, because electron-builder's APP_ASSOCIATE writes the extension default, not just OpenWithProgids. Because no `UserChoice` exists for any of the eight on this machine, that HKLM default IS the effective handler: double-clicking a `.xdp`/`.fdf`/`.xfdf`/... then launches Jovrel, which answers "cannot display it yet", instead of Adobe Acrobat. The user's OS default is silently changed for eight file types the app explicitly claims only to be a candidate for.

Repro: on the installed machine, `reg query "HKLM\Software\Classes\.xdp"` (shows `Acrobat.XDPDoc` before a Jovrel install); read `FileAssociation.nsh:66` + `NsisTarget.js:647`; then install the Phase 97 build and re-query (expected `Jovrel.xdp`). Recovery requires the user to reset each type by hand in Windows Settings.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-525 (HIGH, owner backend-dev). CTO triage (2026-10-04): confirmed. `fileAssociations` claims the OS default in electron-builder's NSIS target, which contradicts the "selectable candidate" contract and silently changes the user's existing handlers for eight types Jovrel cannot render. Fix: register the eight as candidates only (ProgID + `OpenWithProgids` + `RegisteredApplications`/`Capabilities`), never the `.<ext>` DEFAULT; `.pdf` stays as shipped. Fix chunk dispatched before the phase can close.

## ADV-193: Phase 97 acrobat: protocol overwrites Adobe's per-machine registration and uninstall deletes it unconditionally

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: HIGH

What I did: Read `electron-builder.nsh:249-272` and inspected the machine registry (read-only). `HKLM\Software\Classes\acrobat` EXISTS and is Adobe's: default value `URL:Acrobat Protocol`, `URL Protocol` = ``, `DefaultIcon` = `C:\Program Files\Adobe\Acrobat DC\Acrobat\Acrobat.exe`, `shell\open\command` = `"C:\Program Files\Adobe\Acrobat DC\Acrobat\Acrobat.exe" /u "%1"`, plus `shell\open\ddeexec\application` and `shell\open\ddeexec\topic`. `HKCU\Software\Classes\acrobat` and `HKCR:\acrobat` are absent, so this HKLM key is the machine's only `acrobat:` protocol handler. Evidence command: `powershell -NoProfile -File test-fixtures/phase97-adversary/reg_probe.ps1`.

Expected: per the phase's "selectable ... candidate" framing, Jovrel registers without disturbing a pre-existing third-party `acrobat:` registration, and uninstall removes only registration Jovrel created (the same identity-guarded discipline the legacy-cleanup steps use at `electron-builder.nsh:108-192`).

Actual: `customInstall` (`electron-builder.nsh:256-259`) unconditionally overwrites the existing HKLM class root default, `DefaultIcon` and `shell\open\command` with Jovrel's exe, so Jovrel HIJACKS Adobe Acrobat's per-machine `acrobat:` protocol for every user (a URL protocol has no OpenWithProgids candidate slot - writing the class root IS the handler). Then `customUnInstall` (`electron-builder.nsh:270-272`) runs `DeleteRegKey SHELL_CONTEXT "Software\Classes\acrobat"`, unconditionally deleting the WHOLE key - including Adobe's `DefaultIcon` and `shell\open\ddeexec` subkeys, which Jovrel never created and does not restore. After a Jovrel install+uninstall cycle, Adobe's `acrobat:` protocol is gone. Ruling 5 mandated the write, but did not weigh the third-party clobber; the delete in particular has no identity guard.

Repro: `reg query "HKLM\Software\Classes\acrobat" /s` and `...\shell\open\command` on this machine (Adobe's values above); read `electron-builder.nsh:256-272`; install the Phase 97 build, re-query the class root (Jovrel's default), uninstall, re-query (key deleted entirely).

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-526 (HIGH, owner backend-dev). CTO triage (2026-10-04): confirmed. Writing the URL-protocol class root is a machine-wide hijack and the unconditional uninstall delete destroys third-party registration Jovrel never created. Fix: candidate-only registration (`Jovrel.acrobat` ProgID + `OpenWithProgids` + `Capabilities\URLAssociations`), identity-guarded uninstall that never deletes `Software\Classes\acrobat`. Fix chunk dispatched with DEF-525.

## ADV-198: Escape on a live text-run edit silently loses the edit (document data loss)

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: HIGH

What I did: `e2e/tfl525_adversary_diffpass.spec.cjs` S1 (line 129), plus the
mirror unit probe `test/unit/renderer/tfl525_adversary_diffpass.test.tsx` A3.
With the app open on `assets/report.pdf` page 1, armed the Edit Text verb
(`gotoStage(win, 2)` then `[data-dock-verb="editText"]`), clicked a text run,
typed `"<run text> ZZESC<n>"` into the Inspector Text field (a live run session),
then pressed Escape. Then Save As and reparsed the saved file with pdfjs.

Expected: the host's target-change effect commits a run session when the target
clears ("so no edit is lost", `src/renderer/components/DocumentView.tsx:1509`);
Escape disarms the tool, so the live run edit must be committed exactly once -
exactly as a dock tool switch (S4) and selecting another run (S2) already do.

Actual: the run edit is silently DISCARDED. `committedAfterEscape=false` (the
marker is absent from the saved PDF's page-1 text). Unit A3 reproduces it against
the real `EditOverlay`: `onCommitTextEdit` call count after a tool switch = 0.
Root cause: `pendingRunCommitTargetRef` is parked ONLY in the run bar's Confirm
handler (`EditOverlay.tsx:1594-1600`). On Escape there is no field blur, so
`commitTextSession` clears the session and bumps `textCommitToken` only AFTER the
Escape/disarm has cleared the overlay's `textTarget` (the `[tool, page]` reset
effect, `EditOverlay.tsx:517-529`). The token effect then reads
`textTarget ?? pendingRunCommitTargetRef.current` (`EditOverlay.tsx:609`) = null,
returns before `onCommitTextEdit`, and the keystrokes are gone with no engine op
and no undo entry. A dock tool switch does not hit this because its mousedown
blurs the field first, while `textTarget` is still the run.

Screenshot: screenshots/tfl695-s1-escape.png

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-540 (CTO, 2026-10-04). CTO RULING: Escape is the keyboard abort for a live text session and must be an explicit DISCARD - the same semantics as the run/box Cancel and the DEF-539 box-Escape fix: the run edit is reverted and the document left unmodified. The adversary's suggested expectation (Escape commits the run edit) is OVERRIDDEN; blur / click-away / tool-switch remain the commit gestures. The defect is that the run Escape path reaches the discard by ACCIDENT (the commit-token effect reads a cleared `textTarget` and returns), so it is nondeterministic and no test locks it. Fix: on Escape/disarm, call `discardTextSession` for a live RUN session too (mirroring the box handling TFL-693 added) and add the missing assertion. Severity recommended MEDIUM (the observable result already matches the intended revert; the risk is nondeterminism, not active data loss under this ruling). qa to file as DEF-540.

## ADV-199: A whitespace-only run Confirm still reaches the engine and dirties the document

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: `e2e/tfl525_adversary_diffpass.spec.cjs` S3 (line 180), plus unit A5.
Armed Edit Text, selected a text run, filled the Inspector Text field with three
spaces (a live whitespace-only run session), clicked the run bar's Confirm, then
read `window.tflexDiagnostics()` and Save-As + reparse.

Expected: the same rule DEF-538 added for boxes ("a box with no visible content
carries nothing: never reach the engine") and the pre-existing annotation guard
(`session.text.trim() === ""`, `DocumentView.tsx:1371`) apply to the run kind too:
a whitespace-only commit places nothing and does not mark the document modified.

Actual: the run branch has NO trim guard (`DocumentView.tsx:1439-1441` just bumps
`textCommitToken`), and the EditOverlay token effect commits whenever
`next !== target.text`. Real app: `confirmCount=1`, `modified=true` after the
whitespace-only Confirm, and unit A5 records one `onCommitTextEdit` with
`newText="   "`. The engine masks the run's rect and draws no visible glyphs, so
an accidental space visibly deletes the run; the original glyphs stay only in the
content stream, so a later extraction still shows them (the mask is visual-only) -
which is why the file is dirty but the string survives reparse.

Screenshot: screenshots/tfl695-s3-whitespace.png

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-541 (CTO, 2026-10-04). Confirmed: the run commit branch has no trim guard, so a whitespace-only run Confirm reaches the engine (`modified=true`) and masks the run with no visible glyphs. Apply the same rule DEF-538 added for boxes and the pre-existing annotation guard (`session.text.trim() === ""`, `DocumentView.tsx:1371`): a whitespace-only run commit places nothing and leaves the document unmodified. Severity MEDIUM. qa to file as DEF-541.

## ADV-201: Phase 100 DriftGuard is blind to motion-duration LONGHANDS - a live raw `animation-duration: 9s` in the scanned stylesheet passes

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: read `test/unit/renderer/foundationGuards.test.ts`, then extracted the
guard's OWN scan functions verbatim (the block from `const ENFORCED_PROPS` through
`cssViolations`) into a scratch probe at
`$PAPERCLIP_RUN_SCRATCH_DIR/advGuardEvasion.ts` and ran it with `node` from the repo
root (transcript: `screenshots/adv-phase100/guard_evasion_probe.log`). I fed
`cssMotionFileViolations` seeded declarations and the real `src/renderer/styles.css`
text. The unmodified guard test itself passes: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs
run test/unit/renderer/foundationGuards.test.ts` is 22/22 green, so these are misses,
not a red suite.

Expected: phase-100 ruling 5 ("Motion one-off guard") requires any `transition:` or
`animation:` in a migrated rule body to reference a `--tf-motion-*`/`--motion-*`/
`--tf-ease-*` token or `none`, with no raw ms/s duration. `animation-duration`,
`transition-duration`, `animation-delay` and `transition-delay` are the same motion
declarations in longhand form, so a raw duration written longhand should be flagged
exactly like the shorthand.

Actual: the guard's motion regex is
`(?:^|[;{\s])(transition|animation)\s*:\s*([^;}\n]+)`, which only matches the exact
property name immediately followed by `:`. `cssMotionFileViolations(".x { animation-duration:
9s; }")` and `cssMotionFileViolations(".x { transition-duration: 200ms; }")` both
return `[]`. This is live in the scanned stylesheet:

```
styles.css:12720-12722
:root[data-theme="frosted"] .side-rail::after,
:root[data-theme="frosted"] .tools-palette::after {
  animation-duration: 9s;
```

The probe reports `present_in_styles_css=true guard_flagged=false` for it. The
shorthand is also leaky: `styles.css:12715` `animation: acrylic-sheen 7s
var(--tf-ease-standard) infinite;` is exempted because `--tf-ease-*` matches
MOTION_TOKEN even though its `7s` duration is raw - the token check exempts the whole
declaration, not just the duration slot. Controls that ARE caught by the same
function: `.x { transition: opacity 200ms ease; }` and `.x { animation: spin 1.4s

(the preload/renderer forwards `message`, `error_name`, `stack_trace`; `transport.ts`
