## ADV-207: The route inserts a batch row-by-row with no transaction - a mid-batch invalid row inserts the earlier rows, returns 500 with the raw Postgres constraint name, and the client's at-least-once retry duplicates them

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: posted a 3-row batch where rows 1-2 are valid and row 3 has `level:"BOGUS"`,
then queried `public.bug_reports` for the two good messages. Also posted a single invalid
`level` to read the error body.

Expected: an invalid row rejects the whole request with a 4xx before any insert (or the
batch is atomic), and no internal database detail is returned.

Actual: the good rows `adv-partial-good-0` and `adv-partial-good-1` were both inserted
(confirmed by SQL) while the response was `500
{"error":"new row for relation \"bug_reports\" violates check constraint
\"bug_reports_level_check\""}` - partial commit, no transaction, and the Postgres
constraint name is leaked to the anonymous caller. The client (`capture.ts:230-238`)
does NOT `acknowledge` on a thrown transport error, so a retried flush re-POSTs the same
batch and inserts the good rows a second time, forever, for any batch that contains a
row the server cannot insert. `bug-reports-*` rows were cleaned up after the probe.

Screenshot / log: screenshots/phase101-adv/probe2-route.log (plus the mixed-batch curl and
follow-up SQL in this entry)

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-551

## ADV-208: No size bound on captured `message`/`stack_trace`/`context` - a single >256 KB capture is queued but can never be delivered, and it blocks the flush head (poison pill)

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: launched the built app against the shipped (real) Function URL and captured
one error whose `message` was 300 KB (`'A'.repeat(300*1024)`), then waited 20 s (past the
2 s debounce plus the full 5-try backoff) and read the queue file and app liveness.

Expected: capture either bounds/splits the payload or drops it locally so it cannot
poison the outbound pipeline; the report eventually leaves the queue.

Actual: `capture` accepted it (`{"ok":true,"queued":1}`) and persisted a 307,713-byte row.
The route caps the batch at 256 KB and returns 413 (`hello.ts:39`), so the POST always
fails; the client retries 5 times then gives up without acknowledging, and the row stays
at the head of the queue. `peek(batchSize)` always returns oldest-first, so every later
flush retries the same oversized head and no newer report can drain until >200 newer rows
evict it via drop-oldest - i.e. up to 200 real reports are silently never sent. App stayed
alive (no crash). The queue file can also balloon toward 200 x ~300 KB.

Screenshot / log: screenshots/phase101-adv/probe-oversize.log,
driver screenshots/phase101-adv/p101-oversize.cjs

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-552

## ADV-209: The transport has no request timeout and the single-flight guard never resets on a hung connection - one silent endpoint wedges the bug-report pipeline for the whole session

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: started a local TCP server that accepts the connection and reads the request
but never responds, pointed `TFLEX_FUNCTION_API_URL` at it, launched the built app, made
one capture (flush starts and hangs), waited past the debounce, made a second capture,
then waited another 20 s and read the queue plus the server's accept/request counters.

Expected: `fetch` has a timeout/AbortController, a hung socket is abandoned, the queue is
retried/recovered on a later flush, and the UI/capture path is unaffected.

Actual: the server saw exactly 1 accept / 1 request; 24 s later both `hang-probe-1` and
`hang-probe-2` were still queued and no second request was ever attempted. `runFlush`
(`capture.ts:231`) `await`s `fetch` with no `AbortSignal`, so the promise never settles;
`flush()` (`capture.ts:144-151`) keeps returning that same never-settling `flushPromise`,
so `scheduleFlush` is a no-op for every later capture. The app did not crash and the UI
stayed responsive, but no bug report is ever delivered again until restart. Only a probe
server was used; no product code was changed.

Screenshot / log: screenshots/phase101-adv/probe-hang.log,
driver screenshots/phase101-adv/p101-hang.cjs

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-553

## ADV-210: The in-app auth popup keeps `window.opener` on the privileged main window - a script in the provider chain can navigate the app to an attacker origin that still holds the full `window.tflex` preload bridge

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: HIGH

What I did: launched the shipped dev build via `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`, clicked the title-bar
account control, then "Continue with Google". The in-app popup opened and followed the real
provider chain to `https://accounts.google.com/...`. In that popup I ran
`window.opener.location.href = 'https://example.com/?tfl772=tabnabbing'` (equivalent to any
script executing in the popup), then read the MAIN window's URL and evaluated
`window.tflex.accounts.getStatus()` on it. Repro: `node test-fixtures/tfl772_adversary_probe.cjs`
(result JSON `test-fixtures/tfl772_probe_result.json`, fields `tabnabbing.*`).

Expected: the provider window must not hold a usable opener on the app's privileged window.
The app renderer runs from `file://` with a `contextBridge` bridge, and every IPC handler in
`src/main/index.ts` acts on the payload without validating the sender origin/frame, so any
origin that keeps the preload is a full app bridge. The Phase 102 contract keeps the popup
allowlist as "a security net"; the opener relationship is a hole in it. `window.open` at
`src/renderer/components/AccountsDialog.tsx:367` passes no `noopener`/`noreferrer`, and the
main window has no `will-navigate` guard (`src/main/window.ts` installs only
`setWindowOpenHandler`, which governs new windows, not navigation).

Actual: the popup had `window.opener` (`hasOpener:true`; cross-origin read of
`opener.location.href` was correctly blocked, but writing `location` is allowed), and the
main window navigated to `https://example.com/?tfl772=tabnabbing` (`mainUrlAfterNav`). On
that attacker origin `window.tflex` was still present and live:
`{hasTflex:"object", hasAccounts:true, ipcResult:{ok:true, status:"signed-out"}}` - the
preload bridge and IPC survived the cross-origin navigation. That bridge exposes the app's
full IPC surface (file open/save/export, `shell.openPath`, settings, signatures, update
install), so a single script execution anywhere in the popup's navigation chain (a
compromised/XSS'd provider page, or an open redirect that lands script) escalates from a
third-party web origin to local file access under the user's account. Phase 50's OS-browser
path had no opener relationship, so this is a new weakening introduced by the diff.

Screenshot / log: `test-fixtures/tfl772_probe_result.json` (`tabnabbing`),
driver `test-fixtures/tfl772_adversary_probe.cjs`.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-558 (HIGH). CTO triage (TFL-751, 2026-10-05): Phase 102 re-enables the in-app popup, so this opener/escalation hole is in scope for this merge. Fix: main-process hardening - a main-window `will-navigate` guard so the privileged window can never be navigated away from the app (the escalation), plus best-effort opener severing - assigned backend-dev (TFL-777). Blocks the Phase 102 commit.

## ADV-211: The in-app auth popup's own `window.open` bypasses `decideAuthPopup` - the popup has no `setWindowOpenHandler`, so the provider page spawns arbitrary untracked windows

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: with the Google popup open on `https://accounts.google.com/...`, I called
`window.open('https://evil.example.com/', '_blank')` from inside the popup, then counted and
listed the app's remote windows from main. Repro: `node test-fixtures/tfl772_adversary_probe.cjs`
(result `popupChild.*`).

Expected: Phase 102 feature A states "The popup is confined to https on exactly the configured
auth host; every other URL is still refused by `decideAuthPopup`", and the deny-by-default
popup allowlist is "kept as a security net". A window opened FROM the popup is still a new
window in the app and must not bypass that rule.

Actual: `window.open` returned a WindowProxy and a real window was created at
`https://evil.example.com/` (`windowsCreated:1`). `installAuthPopupHandler` installs
`setWindowOpenHandler` only on the MAIN window (`src/main/window.ts:228`); the popup created
at `did-create-window` (`window.ts:253-299`) gets no handler, so Electron's default allow
applies to every window the provider page opens. That window is not added to the handler's
tracked `popups` set, so it is not closed on completion or when the main window closes (stray
window / process that outlives the flow).

Screenshot / log: `test-fixtures/tfl772_probe_result.json` (`popupChild`).

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-559 (MEDIUM). CTO triage (TFL-751, 2026-10-05): a window opened by the provider popup bypasses the deny-by-default allowlist and is untracked. Fix: install a deny-all `setWindowOpenHandler` on the child popup in `installAuthPopupHandler` - assigned backend-dev (TFL-777). Blocks the Phase 102 commit.

### Phase 107 Canvas Paper Stage diff-pass - design critique of the changed surface (skill: design-critique)

User: someone reading or editing a PDF in the editor viewport. Job on this surface: read the page
content while the app chrome and the stage stay out of the way. Success: the page is unmistakably
the focus, its edges are crisp against the stage in every theme, and navigation/zoom never makes
the view jump.

- Must-fix - none. The change is a visual/geometry treatment with no new control; the only controls
  it touches (fit/zoom, layout, Multi Mode) keep their promised actions (verified by the phase107
  e2e and the named unit set).
- Should-fix - **States (truthfulness of the "physical sheet"):** in light mode the 1px ring
  `#DCE0E7` sits on a `#ECEFF4` stage (~1.03:1 contrast), so the page edge nearly disappears and the
  sheet reads flat at fit; in dark mode the same role is clearly visible. If the intent is a crisp
  sheet edge in both themes, lift the light ring toward the shadow's own tone. (Operator-chosen
  token values; flagged as a critique, not a defect.)
- Should-fix - **Affordance / density:** the light two-layer shadow is very subtle at fit, so the
  page and the stage can merge; the dark theme carries the separation. Consider a slightly stronger
  contact layer in light so the sheet reads as lifted, matching dark's clarity.
- Nice-to-fix - **Consistency (cross-surface):** the page-frame token also drives
  `.print-preview-sheet` (ADV-217), so the print preview now shows a heavier frame than before; give
  that surface its own shadow so the Canvas role stays Canvas-only.
- Strengths to keep: the page stays paper-white in both themes (PDF fidelity untouched); square
  corners match the real PDF bounds; the frame is box-shadow chrome only (border/margin 0, bitmap
  box unchanged); the fit margin (28px) and gap (24px) are consistent and the scroll/zoom anchor is
  stable (probes C/D); both Multi Mode panes carry the same stage with independent scroll.

## ADV-218: The active rail item loses its selected violet fill on hover - the generic `.btn-toggle:hover` rule out-specifies the DEF-578 active-fill selector

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: launched the dev app through `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`, opened `report.pdf`,
clicked the Review stage, moved the pointer to (600,500) and read
`getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.stage-rail-btn-active')).backgroundColor`
(= `rgb(240, 235, 252)`, the DEF-578 selected surface `#F0EBFC`), then hovered the
active Review button and re-read the same property. Probe:
`test-fixtures/phase108-adversary/adv_p108_rail.spec.cjs` test `ADV-108-I`.

Expected: the active destination keeps its committed soft-violet fill while hovered
(the design names the violet fill as the selected affordance and reserves the
"restrained neutral hover" for inactive destinations; phase-108.md ruling 3).

Actual: on hover the active fill becomes `rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.04)` (light
`--bg-hover`) - the selected violet fill disappears. The pointer rests on the item
after a click, so this is the common state, not an edge case. Cause: the generic
`.btn-toggle:hover:not([disabled]):not([aria-disabled="true"])`
(`src/renderer/styles.css:3617`, specificity 0,4,0) beats the rail's active-fill
selector `.stage-rail .stage-rail-btn[aria-pressed="true"]`
(`src/renderer/styles.css:15608`, 0,3,0). The DEF-578 "fix attempt 2" defeated the
non-hover `.btn-toggle[aria-pressed="true"]` override (0,2,0) but did not account
for the higher-specificity hover rule; the resting fill is correct, the hovered fill
is not. The marker (`::before`) and the accent ink survive, so selection is still
recoverable, but the committed fill flashes off under the cursor.

Reproduction:
1. Launch via the canonical helper and open any sample.
2. Click any stage (e.g. Review) and leave the pointer on it.
3. Read the active button's computed background -> `rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.04)`;
   move the pointer off the rail -> `rgb(240, 235, 252)`.

Evidence: `test-fixtures/phase108-adversary/adv_p108_rail.spec.cjs` (ADV-108-I);
log `[p108-adv] I activeBg rest=rgb(240, 235, 252) hover=rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.04)`.

Suggested fix (for the developer, not applied by me): add a
`.stage-rail .stage-rail-btn[aria-pressed="true"]:hover` fill rule (same specificity
as the generic hover rule, later in source, so it wins) or raise the active-fill
selector's specificity above the generic `:hover` chain, binding it to
`--tf-siderail-selected-surface` so hovering the active item never repaints it with
the neutral hover wash.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-584 (CTO, 2026-10-06): the active destination must keep
its committed violet fill while hovered; the design reserves the neutral hover for
inactive destinations (phase-108.md ruling 3), and the pointer rests on the item
after a click. Assign to frontend-dev. (Filed as DEF-584 by qa TFL-916; now CLOSED.)

## ADV-219: In forced-colors the active rail item has no visual cue - the fill collapses and the 3px marker is forced to the Canvas colour, with no border fallback

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: LOW

What I did: opened a sample, activated the Review stage, then
`win.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' })` and read the computed styles of the
active and an inactive rail button and of the active button's `::before`. Probe:
`test-fixtures/phase108-adversary/adv_p108_rail.spec.cjs` test `ADV-108-H`;
screenshot `screenshots/phase108-adversary/adv-h-forced-colors.png`.

Expected: the design requires forced-colors to "preserve selected shape/border and
programmatic state using system colors as appropriate"
(`Visual overhaul/Siderail/Specifications/siderail-design-spec.md:41`), and the
phase's success criterion 2 requires the active target to be unambiguous.

Actual: in forced-colors the active button background becomes
`rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.04)` versus the inactive `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0)` (a 4%-alpha
white over the forced Canvas - effectively no fill), the `::before` marker's
background is forced from `rgb(124, 58, 237)` to `rgb(255, 255, 255)` (the Canvas
colour), and `border-top-width` is `0px`. On a white forced-colors Canvas the white
marker is invisible and no border/outline remains, so the active workspace is
distinguishable only by `aria-pressed` (screen reader) - the sighted high-contrast
user sees four identical items. The rail is uniquely exposed here because
`.stage-rail-btn { border: 0 }` (`src/renderer/styles.css:15584`) removes the 1px
border the canonical toggle would otherwise carry into forced-colors; no
`@media (forced-colors: active)` rule exists in `styles.css`. `aria-pressed="true"`
and the accessible names do survive.

Reproduction: open a sample, activate a stage, enable a forced-colors / Windows High
Contrast theme, and inspect the rail - the active item shows no fill, border or
marker.

Evidence: `screenshots/phase108-adversary/adv-h-forced-colors.png`; log
`[p108-adv] H normal=... markerBg:"rgb(124, 58, 237)" forced=... markerBg:"rgb(255, 255, 255)" ...`.

Suggested fix (for the developer, not applied by me): add a rail-scoped
`@media (forced-colors: active)` block that gives the active item a system-colour
shape cue - e.g. a `1px solid ButtonText` border or an `outline` - and
`forced-color-adjust: none` on the marker, so selection survives when the soft fill
is forced away.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-585 (CTO, 2026-10-06): the design requires forced-colors
to preserve a selected shape/border cue (siderail-design-spec.md:41) and criterion 2
requires an unambiguous active target; `aria-pressed` alone is screen-reader-only, so
the sighted high-contrast user sees four identical items. Assign to frontend-dev.
(Filed as DEF-585 by qa TFL-916; now CLOSED.)

### Phase 108 Workspace Rail diff-pass - design critique of the changed surface (skill: design-critique)

User: someone reading or editing a PDF who moves between the Pages, Edit, Review and
Deliver workspaces. Job on this surface: switch workspace without losing document
state or hunting for the control. Success: the four destinations read as one
deliberate set, the active workspace is unmistakable in both themes and in
high-contrast, and Settings is clearly a separate utility pinned to the rail foot.

- Must-fix - none. No new interactive control; the four stage buttons and the gear
  keep their promised actions (verified live: each click switches `data-active-stage`
  / opens Preferences without changing the workspace), and Ctrl+1..4 is intact and
  guarded in text inputs.
- Should-fix - **States (truthfulness of selection):** the active item's violet fill
  is replaced by the neutral hover wash whenever the pointer is over it (ADV-218).
  The one affordance the phase is built around flickers off under the cursor.
  **Try:** a `.stage-rail .stage-rail-btn[aria-pressed="true"]:hover` fill rule bound
  to `--tf-siderail-selected-surface`.
- Should-fix - **Accessibility (not colour-only):** in forced-colors the active item
  has no shape, border or marker cue (ADV-219); selection becomes screen-reader-only.
  **Try:** a `@media (forced-colors: active)` border/outline on the active item.
- Nice-to-fix - **Consistency (stale copy):** `App.tsx:10976,10979` still describe
  the rail as a "44px track" (out of Phase 108's edit scope, so left untouched), which
  will mislead the next reader. **Try:** update the comment with the next App.tsx
  change.
- Nice-to-fix - **Hierarchy / density:** the 11px labels sit at the documented UI
  floor; they fit the 56px content box at 100% text scaling, but at 200% Windows text
  scaling `white-space: nowrap` would push them past the fixed 72px rail (no expanded
  mode ships this phase). **Try:** confirm on the target DPI; the design already
  permits widening labels/expanded mode under text scaling.
- Strengths to keep: the geometry is exact - 72px track flush with the stage column
  at 1440 through 640, zero sibling overlap; every control reachable and hittable at
  the 640x480 floor; labels visible at every width; the inset 3x20px marker and the
  resting `#F0EBFC` fill match the design; reduced-motion collapses the marker
  cleanly; the rail-scoped tokens leave the frozen shared palette untouched.

## Phase 109 View Strip footer diff-pass (TFL-918)

Baseline: `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase109_viewstrip.spec.cjs` -> 12 passed
(1.3m), log `test-fixtures/phase109-adversary/baseline-e2e.log`. The phase e2e never
reaches the footer's `<=419px` overflow tier (at 640x480/100% the single-mode footer
measures 476px, compact not overflow) and never exercises the frosted theme, which is
why the two findings below survived it.

## ADV-221: In the frosted theme the full-bleed document scroller covers the View Strip footer - 11 of its 12 controls are not hit-testable

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: HIGH

What I did: launched the real app through `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` `launchApp`, opened
`report.pdf`, set 1440x900, cycled the app-menu "Toggle Theme" row to each shipped
theme, and hit-tested every control inside `[data-view-strip]` at its own centre with
`document.elementFromPoint`, then measured `.document-scroller` against `.view-strip`
(`test-fixtures/phase109-adversary/probe6.cjs`, `probe5.cjs`).

Expected: the footer is grid row 6 of `.workspace-main` and `.document-scroller`
occupies row 5, so in every theme the scroller stops at the footer's top edge
(scroller bottom == footer top == 852px at 1440x900) and the footer paints above it
and is clickable - exactly as it is in the light and dark themes.

Actual: in the FROSTED theme `.document-scroller` is `position: absolute; inset: 0;
height: auto; z-index: 0` (`src/renderer/styles.css:13914-13933`), so it spans the
WHOLE `.workspace-main` box including the new row 6. Measured at 1440x900 frosted:
scroller `[256,88,920,812]` (bottom 900) vs footer `[256,852,920,48]` (top 852) - a
48px overlap, i.e. the entire footer band. The scroller is a positioned `z-index: 0`
box painted above the static grid-item footer, so the PDF page and its `.textLayer`
cover the View Strip. Per-control hit-test at 1440x900: light theme 12/12 controls
hit-true; frosted theme **11/12 return `div.textLayer` or `div.document-content` as
the top element** (`hit:false`) - only the leftmost "Previous page" still hits. The
overlap is reversible by toggling back to light/dark (scroller bottom returns to
852) and reappears on every switch to frosted, so it is a static frosted-layout
omission, not a transition frame. (Playwright's own `.click()` on "Fit width" still
eventually applied because it re-scrolls/retries the element into an actionable
position; a raw pointer click at the control's real coordinates lands on the page.)

Reproduction:
1. `node test-fixtures/phase109-adversary/probe6.cjs`.
2. Open `report.pdf`, 1440x900, use the app menu -> "Toggle Theme" until
   `document.documentElement.dataset.theme === "frosted"`.
3. In devtools: `document.querySelector('.document-scroller').getBoundingClientRect()`
   -> bottom 900; `document.querySelector('.view-strip').getBoundingClientRect()` ->
   top 852; `elementFromPoint` at any footer button centre -> `.textLayer`.

Evidence: `screenshots/phase109-adv-frosted-footer-covered.png`;
`test-fixtures/phase109-adversary/probe6.log` (full hit table), `probe5.log`
(theme-toggle matrix light/frosted/dark).

Suggested fix (for the developer, not applied by me): make the frosted
full-bleed scroller stop at the footer top the way `.canvas-overlay` already
does - replace `bottom: 0` with `bottom: var(--view-strip-h, 48px)` in the
`:root[data-theme="frosted"] .document-scroller` rule (and keep `top: 0`), so
the reserved footer row is never under the page content.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-587 (CTO, TFL-863, 2026-10-06): confirmed on the rendered frosted theme - the full-bleed .document-scroller spans .workspace-main row 6 (scroller bottom 900 vs footer top 852 = 48px overlap) and 11/12 footer controls are not the top element, while light/dark are 12/12. Fix: stop the frosted scroller at the footer top with bottom: var(--view-strip-h, 48px). Assigned to frontend-dev (TFL-921). Blocks the Phase 109 commit.

## ADV-222: The `.view-strip-more` overflow host can never display, so at the `<=419px` overflow tier the page-layout and Book View controls are unreachable

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: HIGH

What I did: launched the real app, opened `report.pdf`, set the physical window to
the 640x480 floor, applied Windows text/DPI scaling 150% via
`BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()[0].webContents.setZoomFactor(1.5)`, and audited the
single-mode footer's tier and the visibility/hit-test of every named viewing control
(`test-fixtures/phase109-adversary/probe4.cjs`, `probe-reach.cjs`).

Expected: success criteria 2 and 7 - at the `<=419px` overflow rung the container
query hides `.view-strip-layout` and `.view-strip-book` AND reveals `.view-strip-more`
(`display: inline-flex`), whose menu re-homes the one/two/four layout and the Book
View entry, so every control stays reachable at 640x480 and under Windows text
scaling.

Actual: at 640x480 + 150% scaling the footer's inline-size container is 263px
(`window.innerWidth` 427), which matches `@container single-view-strip
(max-width: 419px)`: `.view-strip-layout` and `.view-strip-book` compute
`display: none` (visible layout options 0, visible Book View entries 0) - but
`.view-strip-more` ALSO computes `display: none` (visible More toggles 0). The
overflow host never appears, so "One page", "Two pages side by side", "Four pages in
two rows" and "Book View" are present in the DOM but have zero box and are
unreachable by pointer and by keyboard. Root cause: the reveal rule
`@container single-view-strip (max-width: 419px) { .view-strip-more { display:
inline-flex; } }` (`src/renderer/styles.css:5440-5442`) and the base rule
`.view-strip-more { display: none; }` (`src/renderer/styles.css:5451-5455`) have the
same specificity (0,1,0), but the base rule is declared LATER in source order, so
`display: none` wins and the host is permanently hidden. The phase e2e missed it
because at 640x480/100% the footer is 476px (compact rung, P109-12) - only `<=419px`
at text scaling exposes it - and P109-12 asserts the More trigger is *present*, not
that it is visible.

Reproduction:
1. `node test-fixtures/phase109-adversary/probe4.cjs`.
2. Open `report.pdf`; set the window to 640x480; set
   `webContents.setZoomFactor(1.5)` (`window.innerWidth` -> 427).
3. In devtools: `.view-strip` width 263; `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector(
   '.view-strip-more')).display === 'none'` while `.view-strip-layout` and
   `.view-strip-book` are also `none`; every `[data-page-layout-option]` and
   `[data-book-view-open]` has `getBoundingClientRect().width === 0`.

Evidence: `screenshots/phase109-adv-overflow-config.png`;
`test-fixtures/phase109-adversary/probe4.log`, `probe-reach.log` (full control table).

Suggested fix (for the developer, not applied by me): declare the base
`.view-strip-more { display: none; }` BEFORE the `@container` block, or raise the
reveal's specificity (e.g. `.view-strip .view-strip-more`), so the `<=419px` reveal
actually wins.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-588 (CTO, TFL-863, 2026-10-06): confirmed - the base .view-strip-more{display:none} is declared AFTER the <=419px reveal at equal specificity, so the overflow host never displays and the layout/Book View controls are unreachable at 640x480 + 150% scaling. Fix: order/specificity so the reveal wins. Assigned to frontend-dev (TFL-921). Blocks the Phase 109 commit.

### Phase 109 View Strip footer diff-pass - design critique of the changed surface (skill: design-critique)

User: someone reading or editing a PDF who wants page/zoom/layout/pan control without
leaving the document. Job on this surface: move through the document and change how it
is presented from one predictable band. Success: every viewing control is where the
user last learned it, reachable at any supported width and theme, and the band never
steals the page.

- Must-fix - **States / platform (truthfulness):** in the frosted theme the footer is
  entirely covered by the page (ADV-221) - the controls look present but are not the
  top element under the cursor. **Try:** the `bottom: var(--view-strip-h, 48px)` fix.
- Must-fix - **Accessibility / responsive (reachability):** at the `<=419px` overflow
  tier the layout group and Book View are hidden with no replacement (ADV-222), so
  both are keyboard-unreachable. **Try:** fix the `.view-strip-more` cascade.
- Should-fix - **Consistency (theme parity):** the footer geometry is correct in
  light/dark and wrong in one of the three shipped themes; the phase spec promises
  "identical in light/dark/frosted". **Try:** add a frosted case to the phase e2e's
  screenshot/geometry sweep.
- Nice-to-fix - **Affordance (idle):** the open state of the More menu lives inside
  `.view-strip-view`, which the dock idle dims to `opacity: 0.4` after 3s
  (`styles.css:5311-5314`), so an open menu would render dimmed and, because opacity
  makes a stacking context, its `z-index: 30` would be trapped under the later
  `.canvas-overlay`. Not reachable as shipped (ADV-222 hides the host), so recorded
  for the fix, not filed separately. **Try:** exempt the open menu from the idle dim.
- Strengths to keep: the light/dark geometry is exact - a single 48px row, dock
  clearance a measured 16px at both 1440x900 and 640x480, and one footer per pane in
  Multi Mode; the accessible names and `data-*` hooks are preserved verbatim; the
  page-input replace-on-type (DEF-351) and blur-commit work; reduced motion collapses
  the footer/menu transitions; Book View correctly unmounts the footer (no ghost).

### Areas probed with no finding (Phase 109 diff-pass)

- Dock/footer clearance: 16px in single mode and 70px to the shared dock in Multi
  Mode at 1440x900/640x480, both themes, panels open and collapsed (P109-6 plus my
  probe). No overlap.
- Pan mode + footer: with Pan armed the footer controls remain the top element and
  hit-testable in light/dark (`probe-geom.log` section B).
- Page-input stale state: type "5" at page 1, blur without Enter -> `currentPage`
  becomes 5 and the input reads 5; the readout effect does not linger
  (`probe-reach.log` section B). No stale value found.
- Book View lifecycle: footer count 1 -> 0 (Book View) -> 1 (close); no ghost footer
  (`probe-viewstrip.log` Part 8).
- Sibling regions: the Phase 109 hunks do not restyle the dock, rail, tabs or panels;
  the only sibling bleed found is the frosted scroller (ADV-221).
- Known FOREIGN failures (`phase32_multi_mode` header relocation, `toolsRegistry`
  dock-verb-set, maximized `setSize` oracle, 64px rail oracle): not re-reported.

## ADV-223: Home sample cards show a generic per-task glyph, not a real first page or a file-type fallback - `long.pdf` and `report.pdf` render identically (Phase 106 chunk C)

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did:
1. Launch the app with a seeded profile (or the real profile) and open Home; the
   four bundled sample cards render under "Explore Jovrel".
2. Read each card's thumbnail markup: `HomeSampleCard.tsx:34-36` renders
   `<span class="sample-thumb" data-sample-format="pdf"><Icon name={task.icon}/></span>`
   - a fixed `--placeholder-from/to` gradient box with one Quiet Precision glyph,
   never a rendered page and never an image/canvas.
3. Compare the four cards: `form.pdf` -> `forms` glyph / "Try form fields - PDF";
   `long.pdf` -> `find` glyph / "Read and navigate - PDF"; `report.pdf` -> **the same
   `find` glyph / "Read and navigate - PDF"**; `scanned.pdf` -> `recognizeText` /
   "Explore recognition - PDF". `long.pdf` and `report.pdf` are pixel-identical.

Expected: Phase 106 success criterion 3 and REQUIREMENTS/`docs/phase-specs/phase-106.md`
lines 88-92 ("real task framing and a real rendered first page or an honest
per-file-type fallback") and the committed Home design spec
(`Visual overhaul/Home Screen/Specifications/home-screen-design-spec.md:17`):
"previews must be real rendered first pages or an honest fallback based on file
type; do not use generic sparkle tiles", and `live-app-refinements.md:7`:
"never ... identical sparkle rectangles, keeping scan/form/long/report distinctions
honest". The operator's stated gap was exactly that every sample tile looked the
same; two of the four still do.

Actual: no sample ever renders a first page; the fallback is a per-TASK glyph on an
identical gradient, not per-file-type. `long.pdf` and `report.pdf` are fully
indistinguishable (same glyph, same label, same subtitle, same gradient), so the
"long vs report" distinction the design requires is absent, and the only sample
"preview" is the same placeholder rectangle the operator rejected.

Screenshot: `test-fixtures/phase106-adversary/adv-p106-recents-light.png`
(and `-dark.png`); probe dump `test-fixtures/phase106-adversary/adv-p106-recents.json`
(see `.samples`). Probe script:
`test-fixtures/phase106-adversary/adv-phase106-probe.cjs`.

Suggested fix (for the developer, not applied by me): render the real first page of
each bundled sample into `.sample-thumb` (it is already decoded through the existing
`readSample` IPC when opened; a cached first-page raster per sample is enough), or,
if previews are deliberately deferred, make the fallback file-type-based and give
`long` and `report` distinct, honest illustrations/labels so no two cards are
identical.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-592 (CTO, TFL-857, 2026-10-06). Confirmed against Phase 106 success criterion 3 and the committed Home design spec: the sample "previews" are a per-TASK glyph on an identical gradient, and `long.pdf` / `report.pdf` are indistinguishable, so the required per-sample (or per-file-type) honest fallback is absent. Owner frontend-dev (TFL-857 chunk C-fix).

### Phase 106 Home diff-pass - design critique of the changed surface (skill: design-critique)

User: someone opening the app who wants to get straight into a document. Job on this
surface: resume a recent, open a file, or pick a real sample - not browse a landing
page. Success: the fastest path to a document is obvious, the list is truthful about
what each file is, and nothing on the page lies about history or status.

- Must-fix - **Clarity/affordance (samples):** the sample "previews" are empty grey
  placeholders with a tiny glyph; two are identical, so the section reads as broken
  images rather than a choice of tasks (ADV-223). **Try:** the ADV-223 fix.
- Should-fix - **Accessibility/affordance (motion pause):** the top-right pause is an
  unlabelled icon-only toggle that changes the GLOBAL Animations setting and persists
  it; a user who only wants to still the decorative arcs silently disables every app
  animation, and a motion-sensitive user cannot tell from the control what it does.
  The reuse is required by the spec, so this is a labelling/placement fix, not a new
  field. **Try:** make the tooltip/aria label state the app-wide effect ("Pause all
  animations") or move it next to the motif it controls.
- Should-fix - **States (missing recents):** a moved/deleted recent is shown exactly
  like a live one; the user only learns it is gone from an error toast on click, after
  which the entry is silently pruned (`App.tsx:2204-2213`). **Try:** annotate a recent
  that fails an existence check (faint "Missing" chip) and keep it until the user
  removes it, rather than pruning on first failed open.
- Nice-to-fix - **Copy:** the recents empty help "Open a PDF and it will appear here."
  is narrower than the surface, which now deliberately lists DOCX/XLSX/image sources.
  **Try:** "Open a document and it will appear here."
- Strengths to keep: source-format truth is exact and honest (DOCX/XLSX/File/PDF read
  from the real extension, never a blanket "PDF"); duplicate basenames are genuinely
  disambiguated ("Archive / 2024" vs "E: / Backup"); the full path lives only in the
  accessible description/title; long and unicode names ellipsize with no overflow at
  640x480; the empty, loading and no-samples states are designed; recents/removal and
  open-session preservation work; the pause reuses `animationsEnabled` with no new
  persisted field and survives a restart; keyboard focus reaches every control.

### Areas probed with no finding (Phase 106 diff-pass)

- Source-format truth: 9 seeded formats inspected - `.docx`->DOCX/document,
  `.xlsx`->XLSX/spreadsheet, extensionless and `.hiddenfile`->File/other, PDF and
  `samples/`->PDF, CJK path->PDF. Every chip label and `data-source-format` was
  correct; no blanket "PDF" (`adv-p106-recents.json`).
- Duplicate disambiguation: two `report.pdf` rows widened to "Archive / 2024" and
  "E: / Backup" with distinct accessible descriptions. No collision.
- Overflow: `.recent-list` has no horizontal overflow (row right 815 = list right
  815 at 1440; row right 604 vs list right 605 at 640); `.doc-name` ellipsizes; the
  long unicode name did not push the chip/time out; `documentElement` overflow-x = 0
  at 640/860/1024/1440/2560.
- Constrained/wide layout: `.orbit-desk-inner` stays max 1120px centred, padding
  32px at wide and 20px at the <=860 breakpoint; `.welcome-body` is two columns
  above 860 and one column at 860 and below; the motion toggle stays `position:
  absolute`, top/right pinned, and is the hit-test target at its own centre at every
  size (640 is the enforced minimum window width; a 480 request clamps to 640).
- Motion policy: reduced-motion, document hidden, minimize and blur all gate the
  drift, and the paused state survives a full app restart with `data-animations=off`
  and the control reading "Resume motion" - no new settings field, no drift while
  paused (qa's spec covers the same states; my `persist` run confirms the restart).
- Handler/silence sweep: every actionable Home element produced an effect - motion
  toggle flips the setting, edit pen arms/disarms, a recent open fires the existing
  handler (an error toast for the missing file, which also prunes it), and the remove
  minus drops the row. No no-op control found.
- Session preservation: open a sample (1 tab, no Home) -> new empty tab (2 tabs, Home
  shown) -> click back to the sample tab (canvas present, 2 tabs). No session loss,
  scroll/undo state untouched by the Home visit.
- Sample overwrite class: samples open with `onDiskPath: null` and
  `saveInPlaceEnabled` is false for them (`App.tsx:9955-9956`), so in-place Save is
  disabled and Ctrl+S cannot rewrite a bundled asset. No overwrite found.
- Rapid stress: 15 motion toggles and 15 edit toggles in a row left consistent state
  (motion off / pressed true / animations off; edit pressed true, 2 minus badges,
  plus present) with zero page errors. 25 Home mount/unmount cycles showed no page
  error and a flat `performance.memory` reading (not a reliable heap oracle, so no
  leak is claimed either way).
- Theme parity: chip contrast 6.38 (light), 5.16 (dark), 14.11 (frosted); motif
  opacity 0.22/0.20/0.20, inside the required 0.18-0.28 band in all three themes.
- Overlap with Phase 105: Home renders no chrome command, tab control or session
  model; it consumes the existing `onOpenFile`/`onOpenRecent`/`onSampleClick`/
  `onMergeClick`/`onCreateFromImages` handlers and the existing `homeTools` row
  unchanged.

## ADV-224: The Phase 110 supporting-text token drops light-theme Home hero text below the 4.5:1 floor - `.welcome-sub` measures 4.07:1 where the retired `--fg-muted` cleared 5.22:1

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: Launched the shipped app through the canonical helper
(`test-fixtures/phase110-adversary/probe.cjs`, which requires `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`),
set `<html data-theme="light">`, and read the computed colour of `.welcome-sub`
together with the nearest OPAQUE ancestor background (walked with `getComputedStyle`):
`.welcome-sub` computes `rgb(102,112,133)` = `#667085` (the new
`--tf-text-supporting`, `src/renderer/styles.css:46`), and its opaque surface is
`.welcome.orbit-desk` = `rgb(228,233,239)` = `--bg-sunken #e4e9ef`
(`src/renderer/styles.css:541`, rule `.welcome.orbit-desk` `background:
var(--bg-sunken)`). Recomputed the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance ratio with the
project's own formula (`test/unit/renderer/phase38LegibilityContrast.test.ts`):
`#667085` on `#e4e9ef` = 4.07:1. The selector is `.welcome-sub`
(`src/renderer/styles.css:3276-3278`, `color: var(--tf-text-supporting)`), the same
home surface also carries `.welcome-section h3 .count` (supporting ink, 12px).
Sanity anchors: the same probe measured dark `.welcome-sub` `#929BAC` on `#08090b`
= 7.12:1 (fine) and the frosted composite (`.welcome.orbit-desk` white 0.42 film
plus `.welcome-hero` white 0.62 film over `#eef1f5` -> approx `#fbfcfd`) = 4.8:1
(fine). The full probe output is `test-fixtures/phase110-adversary/probe-output.json`.

Expected: Supporting/helper text clears the project's documented 4.5:1 floor on its
ACTUAL opaque surface in every theme. `--fg-muted` (the token these selectors used
before Phase 110) was deliberately darkened in Phase 38 to clear that floor: light
`#556070` on the same `#e4e9ef` hero = 5.22:1. The Phase 110 typography spec claims
`#667085` "raises contrast on both white and `#F5F6F8` surfaces"
(`Visual overhaul/Typography/Specifications/typography-design-spec.md:31`) and its
only measured ratios are `light/helper-on-surface 4.97` / `light/helper-on-canvas
4.6` (`.../supporting-text-contrast.json`) - none of which is the Home `#e4e9ef`
sunken surface.

Actual: On the light Home hero the supporting ink is now 4.07:1, below 4.5:1 and
below the phase's own >=4.6 target - a legibility REGRESSION from the token swap
(5.22 -> 4.07). It is not caught by any test: the Phase 38 contrast sweep
(`test/unit/renderer/phase38LegibilityContrast.test.ts`) only scores
`--fg-strong/--fg/--fg-muted` on `--bg-elevated/--bg-raised/--bg-toolbar/--bg-rail/
--panel-bg`; it never scores the NEW `--tf-text-supporting` token, and `--bg-sunken`
is not one of its surfaces. The Phase 110 unit specs pin the colour VALUE
(`#667085`) and the selector list but never the contrast, and the Phase 110 e2e only
checks light/dark colour equality, not frosted. This is the attack-class-3 +
attack-class-8 hit: the semantic supporting colour is misused on a surface the
design never validated.

## ADV-225: The Phase 105 application menu is completely unstyled above 900px - every `.app-menu*` rule lives only inside `@media (max-width: 900px)`, so at the default 1440px window the popover renders as a 925px in-flow block overlapping the title row and the document rail

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: HIGH

What I did: launched the shipped app through the canonical helper
(`e2e/lib/launch.cjs`), pinned reduced motion, set the window to 1280x800
(measured `innerWidth` 1280, `devicePixelRatio` 1), opened a document, opened
the application menu, and read computed styles plus rects (probe
`p105-adv-probe3.cjs`). Results: `.app-menu` computed `position: static`;
`[data-app-menu-popover]` computed `position: static` with `top: auto;
right: auto; z-index: auto`; the popover rect is left 412.6, top -189.3, width
924.8, height 461.6; the `.app-menu` wrapper rect is left 412.6, top -225.3,
width 924.8. Root cause: ALL `.app-menu*` rules are declared only inside
`@media (max-width: 900px)` (`src/renderer/styles.css:18135` opens the band;
`.app-menu` 18156, `.app-menu-popover` 18175-18188; band closes 18202). Above
900px there is no rule, so `.app-menu-popover` falls back to `position: static`
with no width/height/background/border/box-shadow/z-index/overflow, and
`.app-menu` is a plain block. Because `.header-actions` is `align-items: center`
in the 48px title row, the 461.6px block is vertically centred on the title row
(top -225) and stretches to 924.8px wide. Confirmed in the built bundle
(`dist/renderer/assets/index-423TE2bp.css`): the only `.app-menu` rule is
emitted inside `@media (width<=900px){...}`. The default window geometry is
1440x900 (`src/main/services/settings.ts:290`), so the native launch width is
well above 900.

Expected: the new application menu popover is anchored under its
`[data-app-menu]` trigger, opaque and bounded, at every supported width (CTO
rulings 4 and 6; the phase geometry is a fixed 48px row, not width-conditional).

Actual: at 1280 and 1440 the application-menu popover is an unstyled
924.8x461.6 in-flow block overlapping the title bar and the document rail, with
the trigger pulled up to top -225 (screenshot
`screenshots/adv-225-appmenu-above900.png`). The new application menu - a core
chunk-C control - is effectively unusable at any width > 900px; it only renders
correctly at <=900px. Why the phase e2e missed it: test 1 clicks the (still
present, if mispositioned) `[data-menu-action]` rows, and test 5's
`.titlebar-drag` assertion (`e2e/phase105_topbar_rail.spec.cjs:682-693`) passes
because `-webkit-app-region` is INHERITED - the probe measured
`.titlebar-drag` `getPropertyValue('-webkit-app-region')` = `drag` (inherited
from the parent `.app-header`) even though the element has no rule and is
0-width. So the drag-region half of the change is fine; the popover misrender is
the defect.

Screenshot: screenshots/adv-225-appmenu-above900.png

## ADV-226: The All-tabs switcher popover is painted beneath the Inspector - its stacking context is capped by `.tab-list-all { z-index: 3 }`, so the switcher's right side (dirty dot, duplicate-folder context) is occluded and unclickable

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: launched the app (reduced motion pinned), set 1280x800, opened 12
documents so the rail overflows and the All-tabs control sits at the rail's
right end, then opened `[data-all-tabs]` and sampled `document.elementFromPoint`
across the settled popover rect. Results: `.inspector` is at left 1016, right
1280, width 264, `z-index: 30`, `position: absolute`; `[data-all-tabs-popover]`
is at left 860, right 1180, top 85, bottom 445, width 320, `position: fixed`,
`z-index: 80`; `.tab-list-all` is `position: relative; z-index: 3`. At the
popover's left edge (x 880) the topmost element is the row's own
`.all-tabs-name`; at x 1020 and x 1160 - inside the Inspector's rect - the
topmost element is the Inspector (`glass-sidebar-header inspector-header`,
`glass-sidebar-body inspector-body`, `inspector-row`). So the Inspector paints
OVER the switcher's right ~164px. Root cause:
`src/renderer/components/DocumentRail.tsx:951-1023` renders the switcher
`TfMorph` as a child of `<li className="tab-list-all">`; that `<li>` has
`position: relative; z-index: 3` (`src/renderer/styles.css:9112-9124`), which
establishes a stacking context, so the popover's `z-index: 80`
(`styles.css:9157`) never competes at the root. `.inspector` is a direct child
of `.app-main` (`position: relative`, no z-index, `styles.css:1587`), so its
`z-index: 30` wins at root. Placement
(`DocumentRail.tsx:492`): `left = max(8, min(rect.right-320, innerWidth-328))`;
with the All-tabs control at the rail's right end the 320px popover's right
edge lands ~16px inside the window, overlapping the Inspector's trailing 264px.

Expected: the switcher is "one complete, anchored, opaque, collision-aware
switcher ... full filenames, the accurate total count, actual dirty state and
duplicate-name context" (CTO ruling 6). A `position: fixed` popover should sit
above the docked workspace panels.

Actual: with the Inspector open (which is the normal state whenever a document
is active - `inspectorOpen = tabs.activeId !== null && !activeIsEmpty`,
`src/renderer/App.tsx:9561`), the switcher popover paints UNDER the Inspector
(screenshot `screenshots/adv-226-switcher-over-inspector.png`): the right ~164px
of each row is covered - where `.all-tabs-dot` (the dirty indicator) and
`.all-tabs-context` (the duplicate-folder disambiguator) render - and a click
there hits the Inspector instead of the row. The filenames stay readable because
`.all-tabs-name` is left-aligned. This is why the phase e2e missed it: test 3
opens the switcher with only 4 tabs, so the All-tabs control sits mid-rail and
the popover never reaches the Inspector; the many-tabs case (12/30, required by
success criterion 8) does. Any root-level surface with z-index > 3 that overlaps
the popover rect has the same effect (`.stage-rail` z-index 8, `.action-dock`
z-index 7).

Screenshot: screenshots/adv-226-switcher-over-inspector.png

Disposition: ACCEPTED - MEDIUM; fix assigned to frontend-dev (TFL-944 chunk F2); qa to file as DEF and close at the FIX-READY retest

## ADV-227: The `settings:changed` echo filter ignores `homeMotionPaused` - a stale echo can silently revert the Home motion pause (the same gap TFL-938 mirrors for the existing `animationsEnabled` field)

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: LOW (settings-persistence correctness; TFL-938 also violates the explicit DEF-072 comparator contract)

What I did: read the TFL-938 diff and confirmed `src/renderer/state/settingsEcho.ts` is UNCHANGED by
this change (`git diff --stat -- src/renderer/state/settingsEcho.ts` is empty; `git show
HEAD:src/renderer/state/settingsEcho.ts | Select-String "animationsEnabled|homeMotionPaused"` prints
nothing, so neither the new `homeMotionPaused` nor the pre-existing `animationsEnabled` participates in
the echo comparator). Then I exercised the real modules directly (no reimplementation) with a probe at
`test-fixtures/phase106-tfl938-adversary/probe.ts`, bundled with the repo's own esbuild and run on
Node 24:

```
node_modules\.bin\esbuild.cmd test-fixtures\phase106-tfl938-adversary\probe.ts --bundle --platform=node --format=esm --outfile=<scratch>\tfl938-probe.mjs
node <scratch>\tfl938-probe.mjs
```

The relevant probes model the DEF-037/DEF-072 stale-echo race: local write seq 2 set
`homeMotionPaused=false`, then an older echo carrying `homeMotionPaused=true` (every echo-compared field
identical) arrives. Observed output:

```
{ "attack": "2-echo", "name": "stale echo carrying old homeMotionPaused=true is discarded",
  "pass": false,
  "detail": { "shouldApply": true, "sameSettingsSaysIdentical": true,
              "staleHome": true, "latestHome": false } }
{ "attack": "2-echo", "name": "stale echo carrying old animationsEnabled=true is discarded",
  "pass": false,
  "detail": { "shouldApply": true, "sameSettingsSaysIdentical": true } }
TOTAL=23 FAILED=2
```

Expected: `shouldApplyEcho(staleEcho, 2, latest)` returns `false` for both fields, exactly as it does
for `theme`, `recentsCap`, `optimizePreset` and the palette (`test/unit/renderer/settingsEcho.test.ts`
"discards a stale echo ..."). The DEF-072 header in `settingsEcho.ts:51-60` states the contract
verbatim: "every AppSettings field MUST participate in the content comparison ... new fields added in
future phases must add their own lines here".

Actual: `sameSettings()` (`settingsEcho.ts:82-100`), `differsOnlyInRecentFiles()` (`:113-141`) and
`differsOnlyInGeometry()` (`:227-249`) have no comparison line for `homeMotionPaused` (nor
`animationsEnabled`), so `sameSettings(staleEcho, latest)` collapses to `true` on that difference and
the stale payload is APPLIED. The Main-process `save()` coalescing (`settings.ts:1474-1479`, lazy
`this.current` read) makes a same-turn double toggle safe, but any second write that lands after the
first `_doSave` completes while its `settings:changed` echo is still in flight (a rapid Pause->Resume
double-tap, or a window maximize/resize geometry echo overtaking a Home toggle) reverts the pause. Fix
shape (for frontend-dev - I did not edit anything): add a `homeMotionPaused` equality line to all three
comparators, and while there add the missing `animationsEnabled` line the same contract requires.

Screenshot: none (logic-level race). Fixture/probe: `test-fixtures/phase106-tfl938-adversary/probe.ts`.

## ADV-228: The File trigger cannot close its own open menu - a real mouse click closes on pointerdown and the trailing click reopens it

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM (dismissal / toggle contract regression; no data loss)

What I did: launched the app via `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`, clicked `[data-menu-button]` to open the File menu
(popover present, `aria-expanded="true"`), then clicked `[data-menu-button]` again with a real pointer click
and counted `[data-menu-popover]` after 600 ms. Repeated three times. Separately I recorded the DOM event
order with a capture-phase `pointerdown`/`mousedown`/`mouseup`/`click` listener, and compared a real pointer
click against a synthetic `element.click()` (no pointerdown) and against keyboard Enter on the trigger.

Expected: the second click closes the menu and `aria-expanded` returns to false. The trigger's `onClick` is
`setMenuOpen((v) => !v)` (`TitleBar.tsx:268`), and the retired TitleBar handler explicitly exempted the
trigger from its outside-pointerdown close (`if (menuButtonRef.current?.contains(t)) return;`, removed by
this diff), so pre-migration the trigger toggled closed.

Actual: the menu stays open on 3/3 real mouse clicks. The captured order on the open trigger is
`pointerdown` (target = trigger) -> `mousedown` (the trigger has already lost `titlebar-menu-button-active`,
i.e. the menu has already closed) -> `mouseup` -> `click` (reopens). `CommandMenu`'s window pointerdown
handler (`CommandMenu.tsx:449-457`) exempts only `rootRef` (the popover), never the opener, so the
pointerdown closes the menu and the click toggle immediately reopens it. A synthetic `.click()` with no
preceding pointerdown closes the menu (1/1), and keyboard Enter on the trigger also closes it, isolating the
pointerdown+click pairing as the cause. Fix shape (for the frontend-dev - I edited nothing): the opener
element must be exempted from the dismiss (an `openerRef`, or ignore a pointerdown inside the trigger's
`closest('.titlebar-menu')`), or the trigger should not toggle on click while the pointerdown already
dismissed.

Screenshot: none (state behaviour). Evidence: `adv228-trigger-event-sequence.json`,
`adv228-229-230-probe3.json`.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-601 (MEDIUM) - relaying frontend-dev. Real dismissal/toggle regression introduced by the C5 CommandMenu migration: the opener must be exempted from CommandMenu's outside-pointerdown dismiss so a real click on the trigger collapses the open menu.

## ADV-229: Escape stops closing the File menu whenever focus is not on a menu row

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM (dismissal / keyboard contract regression; no data loss)

What I did: opened the File menu, clicked the non-focusable group heading `.titlebar-menu-heading` (a
`div role="presentation"`), read `document.activeElement` (BODY, not inside `.command-menu`), then pressed
Escape. Ran the heading click 3 times; separately clicked the popover padding near its bottom-right corner
then pressed Escape.

Expected: Escape closes the menu regardless of which part of the popover has focus, and returns focus to the
trigger. The retired TitleBar had a global `window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey)` that closed the menu
on Escape from anywhere (removed by this diff).

Actual: the menu stays open in all 4 trials (`escapeClosed: false`). `CommandMenu` binds Escape to the row
list's `onKeyDown` only (`CommandMenu.tsx:269`, attached at `:282-287`); clicking the heading or padding
moves focus to BODY, so the list never receives the key. Control: with focus forced onto a row, Escape closes
1/1. Any click inside the popover that misses a row disarms Escape while the menu is still visible. Fix
shape: add a document-level Escape listener while open (or make the popover root focusable and keep focus
inside it).

Screenshot: none (state behaviour). Evidence: `adv229-escape-heading.json`.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-602 (MEDIUM) - relaying frontend-dev. Real keyboard regression: Escape must close while focus is off the row list; add a document-level Escape listener while the menu is open (or keep focus inside the surface).

## ADV-230: The CommandMenu border-radius shorthand overrides the shipped square top-left corner, so the File popover no longer joins the trigger's silhouette

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: LOW (visual / design-system consistency; no functional impact)

What I did: opened the File menu and measured the trigger and popover geometry and computed radii at rest
after the enter animation settled.

Expected: the popover's top-left corner is square and flush with the trigger's bottom-left corner (the
title-bar "one silhouette" joined-corner contract; `.titlebar-menu-popover { border-top-left-radius: 0 }` at
`styles.css:14932-14934`, with the open trigger squaring its bottom corners at `styles.css:14961-14962`).

Actual: popover `border-top-left-radius` is 12px while the trigger's bottom corners are 0px (gap 1px, fine).
`.command-menu { border-radius: var(--radius-group) }` (`styles.css:21152`, `--radius-group: 12px`,
`styles.css:226`) is later in the stylesheet at equal specificity, so its shorthand overrides the shipped
`border-top-left-radius: 0`; the joined silhouette gains a rounded notch on the trigger's left corner. Fix
shape: scope the radius so the top-left stays 0 (e.g. re-assert `border-top-left-radius: 0` after the
shorthand, or use longhand radii in `.command-menu`).

Screenshot: `adv230-joined-corner.png`; `file-menu-light.png` shows the full surface.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-603 (LOW) - relaying frontend-dev. Keep the popover top-left square so the trigger + popover reads as one joined silhouette.

## Design critique: File menu on CommandMenu (TFL-975)

User context: a desktop PDF user opening, merging, saving and closing documents; the File popover is a
discoverability surface - the native accelerators own the shortcuts, so the primary job is "find the right
document action and read its accelerator" with the mouse.

### Must-fix (blocks ship)
- **Affordance / states:** the trigger does not read as a toggle - clicking it while open appears to do
  nothing (ADV-228). **Try:** close on trigger activation, keep the open wash, and let the second click
  collapse the menu.
- **Interaction:** Escape silently fails after a click on the heading or padding (ADV-229). **Try:** keep the
  menu's Escape scope at the surface level, not the row list.

### Should-fix (before broader rollout)
- **Consistency:** the rounded top-left corner breaks the joined trigger+menu silhouette (ADV-230). **Try:**
  square the top-left so the pair reads as one surface.

### Nice-to-fix (when there's room)
- **Error prevention:** every File row is enabled with no document open, so Save / Save As / Close Tab
  dispatch a silent no-op (the known DEF-065 renderer gate). The primitive now supports `disabled` +
  `disabledReason`, so the File group could surface "No document open" instead of a dead click. **Try:** gate
  the active-doc rows via the new `disabled`/`disabledReason` fields.

### Strengths to keep
- Accelerators are right-aligned `.kbd` chips on every row, and the documented `[data-menu-action]` contract
  is preserved exactly - the e2e selectors still resolve.
- Auto-focus lands on the first row on open and returns to the opener on close; Arrow/Home/End traversal
  wraps and skips nothing it should not.
- The surface is opaque and legible in light and dark, and the reduced-motion path is genuinely instant (no
  travel), so the swap did not regress the motion budget.

## ADV-231: The settings echo filter ignores every panel-layout field, so a stale echo silently reverts a just-committed panel width or collapse

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM (silent revert of a user setting; self-heals on the next echo, but a
  timing-dependent variant can persist it to disk; no data loss)

What I did: ran a probe that imports the REAL renderer comparator
(`src/renderer/state/settingsEcho.ts`) and calls the exact `shouldApplyEcho(...)` decision the App's
`settings.changed` listener at `App.tsx:1441-1463` makes. For each Phase-112 field I built a "latest local
write" snapshot and a stale echo whose ONLY difference is that field, then asked the filter whether the
echo would be applied. Command: `node --experimental-strip-types
test-fixtures/phase112-adversary/adv_echo_probe.mjs`; raw output in
`test-fixtures/phase112-adversary/adv_echo_probe.out.log`.

Expected: a stale echo that disagrees with the newest local write on a persisted field must be discarded
(`shouldApplyEcho === false`); `sameSettings(staleEcho, persisted) === false`. This is the DEF-037/DEF-072
Lamport contract, and Phase 112 exports `syncPanelWidth(...)` at `App.tsx:1459-1460` precisely to consume
the echo IF it is accepted, so an incorrectly-accepted echo flows straight into the width state.

Actual: `shouldApplyEcho` returns `true` for a stale echo carrying an older `panelLeftWidthPx`,
`panelRightWidthPx`, `inspectorCollapsed`, or `pagesPanelCollapsed`; `sameSettings` reports the two
settings equal despite the disagreement (output line "sameSettings(stale,persisted) (width differs):
actual=true"). Root cause: none of the four panel-layout fields has a comparison line in `sameSettings`
(`settingsEcho.ts:88-108`), `differsOnlyInRecentFiles` (`:121-151`) or `differsOnlyInGeometry`
(`:247-271`). Phase 112 added three new fields and reused `pagesPanelCollapsed`; all four are written
through `trackAndSave` (`App.tsx:1702-1727`, `:9808-9833`) but none participates in the filter, so an echo
from an older write is not recognised as stale. It is applied and `syncPanelWidth`/`setInspectorCollapsed`
(`App.tsx:1459-1463`) overwrite the newer local value. This is the same class already recorded for
`homeMotionPaused` in ADV-227 and documented in the file's DEF-599 note; the phase did not extend the
comparators for its own fields.

Runtime symptom and persistent variant: a burst of two width/collapse commits (or a commit followed by an
`addRecentFile` backend write that builds from main's not-yet-updated `this.current`,
`settings.ts:1610-1613`) can deliver an echo from the older write. Because the other fields match, the echo
passes the filter and the panel jumps back to the previous width/collapse; the next echo usually restores
it, but if the stale payload is the newer one main persisted (the `addRecentFile` race), the revert is
written to disk. Repro is deterministic at the pure-function level (probe above); the UI-level revert is
timing-dependent.

Screenshot: none (state/service behaviour). Evidence: `test-fixtures/phase112-adversary/adv_echo_probe.mjs`
and `.out.log`.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-604 - real Phase 112 gap: the panel-layout fields (panelLeftWidthPx/panelRightWidthPx/inspectorCollapsed/pagesPanelCollapsed) must participate in the settings echo filter. Filed as DEF-604 (the CTO brief's DEF-601 id collided with a closed Phase 105 File-menu defect); fixed by frontend-dev TFL-1000, CLOSED by qa TFL-1001.

## ADV-232: A non-contiguous page range is collapsed to [first,last] before the engine call, so the Deliver inspector's prepared range silently exports unrequested intermediate pages

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM (silent wrong output; extra pages in the exported file(s), no data loss)

What I did: ran a probe that imports the REAL shipped parser (`parsePageRange`,
`src/renderer/engine/types.ts`), parses each range expression, then applies the transform every export
dialog performs right before calling the engine
(`ExportDialog.tsx:165-172`, `docx` `DocxExportDialog.tsx:187-190`, `xlsx`/`pptx`
`OfficeExportDialog.tsx:210-212`): `const [start,end] = [parsed[0], parsed[parsed.length-1]]`. The engine
payload contract is a CONTINUOUS 1-based inclusive `[start,end]` (`src/shared/types.ts:373-379`). Command:
`node --experimental-strip-types test-fixtures/phase112-adversary/adv_range_probe.mjs`; output in
`test-fixtures/phase112-adversary/adv_range_probe.out.log`.

Expected: the pages the user selected are the pages exported. The parser's discrete list is the
authoritative selection (Phase 112 success criterion 7: "pages/range validated by the actual parser").

Actual: 4 of 6 non-empty expressions are silently widened: `"1,3"` -> engineRange `[1,3]` (3 pages for 2
requested), `"1,3,5"` -> `[1,5]` (5 for 3), `"2,4-6"` -> `[2,6]` (5 for 4), `"1-2,4"` -> `[1,4]` (4 for 3).
The parser is correct; the dialog's `[first,last]` collapse discards the gaps. The Phase-112 Deliver
inspector prepares exactly such a set: `exportRangeExpression` (`exportConfig.ts:219-238`) emits `"1,3,5"`,
which the host seeds through `onInspectorExportRun` (`App.tsx:6140-6164`), so the new surface newly routes
non-contiguous prepared ranges into this pre-existing collapse. The dialog's own `valid` gate
(`ExportDialog.tsx:151-158`) passes because `parsePageRange` is correct - the widening happens after
validation, with no error. (Provenance: the `[start,end]` line predates Phase 112, but the diff-pass must
flag it because Phase 112 makes it reachable from the Deliver panel and criterion 7 owns range honesty.)

Screenshot: none (data/output behaviour). Evidence: `test-fixtures/phase112-adversary/adv_range_probe.mjs`
and `.out.log`.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-605 - real Phase 112 gap: criterion 7 range honesty. A non-contiguous selection must not be silently widened to [first,last]. Filed as DEF-605 (brief id DEF-602 collided); fixed by frontend-dev TFL-1000 (contiguous-run export, no widening), CLOSED by qa TFL-1001. Note: the shipped fixture `adv_range_probe.mjs` is a stale oracle - it hand-models the removed transform; refresh is a deferred fixture-only follow-up.

## ADV-233: A stale recents-only echo is trusted as an authoritative backend write, so it can silently revert a renderer-written Pin (the C6b sameRecentFiles fix is bypassed)

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM (silent revert of a pin; self-heals on the next echo; no data loss)

What I did: ran the same probe (`adv_echo_probe.mjs`) against the recents path. Built a latest local write
with a recent pinned `true` and a stale echo of the prior state with the same path/name/openedAt but
`pinned: false`, then asked `shouldApplyEcho` and its two sub-checks.

Expected: the stale pin echo is discarded. Phase 112 C6b added `pinned` / `sourceLabel` / `sourceKind` /
`converted` / `workingFormat` to `sameRecentFiles` (`settingsEcho.ts:187-201`) specifically so a stale
recents echo cannot revert a pin, and `onToggleRecentPin` / `onRemoveRecent` now write recents through the
renderer local path (`App.tsx:2552-2588`, `trackAndSave`).

Actual: `shouldApplyEcho` returns `true`. `sameRecentFiles` is correct - `sameSettings(stale, persisted)`
is `false` because the pin differs - but `differsOnlyInRecentFiles(stale, persisted)` returns `true`
(output: "differsOnlyInRecentFiles(stale,persisted): actual=true"), and that branch at `settingsEcho.ts:298`
applies the echo before `sameSettings`' recents guard can matter. The branch assumes recents-only deltas
are backend `addRecentFile` echoes; since this phase moved Pin/Remove onto the renderer local-write path,
a stale recents-only echo is now indistinguishable from the canonical one and reverts the pin. The C6b
comparison lines only help the `sameSettings` path, never the `differsOnlyInRecentFiles` path.

Screenshot: none (state behaviour). Evidence: `test-fixtures/phase112-adversary/adv_echo_probe.mjs`
and `.out.log`.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-606 - real Phase 112 gap: settingsEcho.sameRecentFiles is bypassed by the differsOnlyInRecentFiles branch, so a stale recents-only echo can revert a Pin. Filed as DEF-606 (brief id DEF-603 collided); fixed by frontend-dev TFL-1000 (sameRecentMetadata gate), CLOSED by qa TFL-1001.

## Phase 112 adversary diff-pass (TFL-997) - surfaces that held

- **Export config / office gate - HELD.** `ExportConfigSection` re-parses the seeded range and gates the
  action on `validation.valid && gate.enabled` (`Inspector.tsx:604-627`); the seed enters the dialog as
  TEXT and is re-parsed and re-validated by the dialog (`ExportDialog.tsx:121-155`,
  `OfficeExportDialog.tsx:145-176`), so the inspector cannot bypass the dialog's validation. `xlsx`/`pptx`
  route through `officeExportGate`, which returns the bridge-absent reason when `bridgePresent` is false
  (`dockModel.ts:126-136`), so the office gate holds when `window.tflex.export` is absent. Range-parser
  edge cases (empty, descending, out-of-range, huge) are rejected by `parsePageRange` returning `null`
  (probe: `""` -> `null`; `lo > hi` and `hi > total` -> `null`). No export-time flatten was introduced;
  PDF forms stay interactive by default (no new flatten call on the Deliver path).
- **Recent-files safety - HELD (with ADV-233 on persistence).** `Remove from Recent` only rewrites the
  settings list and clears the local missing flag (`App.tsx:2552-2570`); it never deletes or moves a file.
  `recent:showInFolder` validates a non-empty string, `existsSync`-guards, never throws and never deletes
  (`main/index.ts`, `ShowInFolderResult`); `recent:locateMissing` opens the single Open-PDF picker and
  resolves a path or null. Hostile/missing paths resolve typed `missing`/`failed`, not a throw.
- **Settings normalisation - HELD.** `normalizeBoundedWidth` accepts only finite in-range numbers and
  drops the single field otherwise (`settings.ts:510-517`); `inspectorCollapsed` accepts only real
  booleans (`:1318-1320`); a present-but-invalid value never rejects the surrounding record. Covered by
  `test/unit/main/settings.test.ts:2029-2177`.
- **Delete / merge / save regression - HELD.** The App.tsx diff touches no delete, extract, rotate, merge
  or save handler; the only merge-adjacent change is the insertion of the new export block after
  `onPickMergeFile`. No new IPC channel was added for page operations.
- **Panel data freshness - HELD in the panels.** The migrated panels are presentation over host-published
  state (`ContextPanel` re-parents `ThumbnailRail` / `AnnotationsPanel`; the Inspector resolves the
  selected annotation from the published text-panel snapshot,
  `Inspector.tsx:1049-1100`), so no new async thumbnail/analysis/page-size result is owned by a panel and
  no stale result can target the wrong page from the diff. The existing document-version guards in
  `DocumentView`/`SideRail` are unchanged.
- **Resize / collapse geometry - HELD with one note.** `clampPanelWidth` floors/ceils to 220-320 / 260-380
  and a non-finite value resolves to the default, so keyboard Home/End and a drag cannot produce a 0 or
  negative panel; the handle is only rendered while its panel is expanded (`App.tsx:11320-11337`), so a
  collapsed panel has no live resizer. `fitPanelWidths` reserves the document budget and the panels floor
  at their collapsed/min widths, so no dock-centering collision (`dockBand(320, 476)=0` correctly lifts the
  dock). Note (not filed, LOW): `fitPanelWidths` still reserves the inspector width even when
  `inspectorOpen` is false, so in the narrow empty-placeholder-tab state (rail visible, no document) the
  rail can be clamped below the persisted width for a panel that is not on screen - cosmetic.

## Design critique: Phase 112 panels (Deliver export config + Home Recent + resize handle)

User context: a desktop PDF user preparing an export and picking a recent document; the panels are
configuration/navigation surfaces where the primary job is "state the output precisely" and "find the file
again", and where a wrong control costs a mis-exported file or a lost document.

### Must-fix (blocks ship)
- **Error prevention:** the Deliver range field accepts non-contiguous sets but the export silently emits
  the span between the ends (ADV-232). **Try:** reject gaps in the inspector, or pass the discrete page
  list through and have the dialog export exactly those pages.

### Should-fix (before broader rollout)
- **State integrity:** a stale settings echo can revert a prepared width, a collapse or a pin (ADV-231,
  ADV-233). **Try:** add the panel-layout fields to all three comparators and narrow the recents-only
  branch to genuinely backend-originated writes.
- **States / disabled reason:** when the range is invalid the primary Export button is disabled but its
  `title` shows the format label, not the reason; the reason sits elsewhere in the section. **Try:** put
  the validation error into the disabled button's tooltip so the cause is co-located with the dead control.

### Nice-to-fix (when there's room)
- **Clarity:** the format group labels mix "Images · PNG (lossless)" and "Text (.txt)" in one list; the
  group split (`image` / `office`) is not surfaced. **Try:** two labelled sub-groups so the image-vs-writer
  choice is legible at a glance.
- **Resize affordance:** the resize handle is a 1px separator with a grip; at 200% DPI a 44px coarse
  target is not guaranteed by the primitive itself. **Try:** size the hit area from the coarse-pointer
  token, not a fixed px.

### Strengths to keep
- The panels keep ONE home per object type: the annotation list stays in the left navigator and the right
  panel renders only the selected annotation's facts and actions (`Inspector.tsx:1049-1123`), so the
  "no duplicated list / empty state" criterion reads cleanly.
- Empty / loading / error / success / gate states are all rendered (`Inspector.tsx:692-752`) and disabled
  actions explain themselves (`PanelPrimitives.tsx:150-195`), so no control is a silent no-op by
  construction.
- The resize handle exposes `role="separator"` with aria value bounds and a full keyboard path
  (Arrow/Home/End), and the width contract is clamped in one pure module shared by CSS, the panels and
  the dock geometry.

## ADV-234: On-canvas text-box / image-placement action bars render detached from their selection

- Session: phase-close
- Suggested severity: HIGH

What I did: launched the dev build only through `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`, opened the
`report.pdf` sample, armed EDIT (`Ctrl+2`) + the `editTextBox` dock verb, dragged a
text box on page 1, typed and committed it, selected it, then measured the
`.edit-box` and `[data-edit-box-toolbar]` rects; scrolled `.document-scroller` by
260px; clicked the View Strip `Zoom in`. Repeated for an image placement
(`.edit-image-placement` + `.edit-image-toolbar`, placed via the real file
chooser). Probe: `test-fixtures/phase1028-adversary/adv_canvas.spec.cjs`;
raw measurements: `test-fixtures/phase1028-adversary/adv_canvas.output.json`.
Expected: the bar floats just under its selection and tracks it across document
scroll and zoom, per `ContextToolbox`'s `coordinateSpace="page-view"` contract and
the TFL-987 comment ("position ABSOLUTE inside the page's containing block").
Actual: the bar computes `position: fixed`, not `absolute`. Text box: box at
viewport (967,248) but bar at (140,208) - 827px to the LEFT and above the box; after
a 260px document scroll the box moved -260 while the bar moved 0 (drift 260px);
after Zoom in the relation drifted a further 72px in x. Image placement: box
(987,348), bar (160,354) - 827px left; after a 240px scroll the box moved -240 and
the bar moved 0 (drift 240). Root cause: in `src/renderer/styles.css` the
`.context-toolbox--page-view { position: absolute }` rule (lines 21123-21125) is
nested INSIDE the `@media (pointer: coarse)` block opened at line 21117, so it is
inert on a fine-pointer desktop; the later, equal-specificity
`.context-toolbox { position: fixed }` (line 21084) then beats the legacy
`.content-action-bar` / `.edit-box-toolbar` / `.edit-image-toolbar` absolute rules.
Impact: the primary surface for Confirm/Delete of a placed text box or image
(and the image Replace/Crop/Remove bar) renders in the upper-left of the window,
overlapping unrelated UI and far from the object; the edit affordance is lost and
the object cannot be confirmed by aiming at it. Violates the REQUIREMENTS
look-and-feel rules.
Screenshot: screenshots/phase1028-adversary/tfl1028-textbox-toolbar-initial.png
(bar upper-left, box top-centre), `tfl1028-textbox-toolbar-after-scroll.png`,
`tfl1028-image-toolbar-initial.png`. Suggested fix: lift `.context-toolbox--page-view`
out of the media query (top level), or scope the fixed rule to
`.context-toolbox:not(.context-toolbox--page-view)`.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-607 (HIGH) - relaying frontend-dev. Real C6 regression: the ContextToolbox page-view bars render detached on fine-pointer desktops.

## Design critique: TFL-855 migrated menus + on-canvas toolboxes

User context: a desktop PDF user editing text boxes / images on the page and
running document verbs from menus; the job is "act on the object I can see" and
"finish the transaction", where a misplaced action bar costs a lost edit.

### Must-fix (blocks ship)
- **Affordance / positioning:** the selected-object action bar is not co-located
  with its object (ADV-234) - it reads as unrelated floating chrome and the
  Confirm/Delete target cannot be aimed at. **Try:** make the page-view toolbox
  absolute within the page (fix the media-query nesting) so it sits under the box.

### Should-fix (before broader rollout)
- **Edge clamp:** the dock Pin/Unpin menu can drop ~15px below the window floor at
  a low anchor (ADV-235). **Try:** clamp against the measured menu height.
- **Copy/consistency:** in the dock More overflow, enabled verb rows still carry a
  `title` equal to their description while disabled rows carry the disabled reason
  in the same slot; the two meanings are not distinguishable by tone. **Try:** omit
  the description `title` on enabled overflow rows, or mark it explicitly.

### Nice-to-fix (when there's room)
- **Discoverability:** the on-canvas toolbar's page-edge flip uses the shared
  above/below logic but with no visual nudge; near the page bottom the bar can
  cover the object it edits. **Try:** prefer the side with more clearance.

### Strengths to keep
- One menu DOM contract and one keyboard model across File / app / dock / picker /
  thumbnail surfaces, with disabled reasons exposed and focus returned to the
  opener.
- TaskDialog / PreviewTaskDialog keep the real host context and state; Split, Stamp
  and Create-from-images show no fabricated content and their disabled/enabled
  transitions reflect real validation.
- Reduced motion is honoured centrally (TfMenu/TfBar/TfDialog) with no travel.

## Design critique: the Phase 113 Quiet Actions surfaces (Home, title bar, dock, menus, dialogs)

User context: a desktop PDF user whose job is "open/act on a document and finish
the transaction with as few decisions as possible"; success is the action fires
once, the surface looks the way it behaves, and nothing is lost. Precedes:
Home/Workspace navigation. Follows: the document operation.

### Must-fix (blocks ship)
- **Affordance / state honesty:** a one-shot file command (Home Merge, title-bar
  Open) fires twice on a double-click (ADV-236). Even though pre-existing, the
  phase's own criterion 6 claims duplicate activation is guarded; the shared
  primitive's busy guard is real but unwired on these controls. **Try:** set a
  synchronous re-entry guard at handler entry, or route these through the

### Should-fix (before broader rollout)

- **Busy-state coverage:** the busy label / `aria-busy` / reserved-width contract
  is exercised by exactly one control (AccountMenu Sync now) and could not be
  reached offline; the contract is therefore effectively unproven in the shipped

### Nice-to-fix (when there's room)

  not this phase, but worth confirming the real drag surface. **Try:** verify the

### Strengths to keep
