## ADV-238: The outline row More menu and the destination popover render offset from their row and are clipped by the outline body

- Session: diff-pass (Phase 111 chunk H/I)
- Suggested severity: HIGH
- Classification: NEW-in-this-phase

What I did: static diff + a headless-Chromium CSS probe. The outline row More
button calls `openRowMenu` (`src/renderer/components/SideRail.tsx:1681-1688`),
which clamps the trigger's VIEWPORT rect with `clampMenuPosition` and stores it;
the menu is then rendered as a `CommandMenu` inside `.outline-panel`
(`SideRail.tsx:1903-1914`), and `CommandMenu` applies that rect as
`position: fixed; left/top` (`src/renderer/components/CommandMenu.tsx:615-624`).
The retarget select is the same: `position: fixed; left: rowMenuPos.left;
top: rowMenuPos.top` (`SideRail.tsx:1915-1942`). Both are descendants of
`.context-panel-outline-body`, which carries
`animation: tf-anim-materialize ... both` (`src/renderer/styles.css:16706`) whose
final keyframe is `to { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); }`
(`src/renderer/styles/animations.css:344-346`). With `fill-mode: both` the
element retains `transform: matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)` after the animation, so it
becomes the containing block for fixed descendants; the body also has
`overflow: hidden` (`styles.css:16700`).

Repro: `node test-fixtures/adv-tfl1077/adv_navigator_probe.cjs` (P1). The probe
mirrors the exact keyframe + `.context-panel-outline-body` rule and a fixed child
requested at viewport (100, 360) inside an ancestor at (100, 92).

Expected: the fixed menu/popover renders at the trigger's viewport coordinates,
above neighbouring content, and is not clipped.

Actual (probe output): `bodyTransform "matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)"`,
`menuRendered { x: 200, y: 452 }` against `menuRequested { left: 100, top: 360 }`
- i.e. the menu is offset by exactly the ancestor's viewport origin (100, 92) and
`clippedByAncestorBottom: true`. In the app the outline body sits below the 52px
panel header + 40px view selector (and, in Split, below the Pages section), so
the row More menu renders roughly 90-150px lower than its row and is clipped at
the panel bottom; the lower rows' menu items (Delete, and the destination select
which replaces the menu) are pushed under the clip. This also happens with the
Animations preference off, because `:root[data-animations="off"] *` only zeroes
`animation-duration` and keeps the end state (`styles.css:13921-13929`); only OS
`prefers-reduced-motion` sets `animation: none` on this element
(`styles.css:16712-16715`).

Oracle: this is the phase's own change - before Phase 111 the outline used the
inline horizontal verb strip (`SideRail.tsx:1824` pre-image, removed in the diff)
and its retarget was an inline `<select class="outline-verb outline-retarget">`;
no fixed-position descendant existed in the animated body. The phase introduced
both fixed surfaces.

Suggested fix: end the materialize keyframe at `transform: none` (or animate
opacity only, or wrap only the tree content), or render the row menu/retarget
popover through a portal to `document.body` so the fixed coordinates are
viewport-relative. Any of the three restores the trigger-anchored placement.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-615 (HIGH, NEW-in-this-phase). Fix dispatched as TFL-1078.

- TFL-1081 fixture correction: the P1 clipping assertion originally quoted here
  (`clippedByAncestorBottom: m.y + m.height > b.bottom`) was later found to be
  TRUE for every source state - the fixture placed the menu below the ancestor
  bottom even with no containing block, and `getBoundingClientRect()` ignores
  `overflow: hidden` clipping - so it could never pass on the fix and never
  discriminated the defect. It is replaced in
  `test-fixtures/adv-tfl1077/adv_navigator_probe.cjs` with a real hit-test clip
  probe (a requested-menu point below the ancestor bottom must hit `#menu`) plus
  a settled-`transform` negative control that `passed` requires to be flagged.
  The finding's substantive basis is unchanged: on the buggy ancestor the fixed
  menu renders offset at `{x: 200, y: 452}` versus requested `{left: 100,
  top: 360}` (`anchoredToViewport: false`, `bodyTransform: "matrix(1, 0, 0, 1,
  0, 0)"`); on the fix it renders `{x: 100, y: 360}` with `bodyTransform:
  "none"` and `clippedByAncestorBottom: false`.

## ADV-239: A deeply indented outline row overflows the 240px navigator and scrolls horizontally

- Session: diff-pass (Phase 111 chunk H/I)
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM
- Classification: NEW-in-this-phase

What I did: static diff + headless-Chromium probe. `.outline-panel` sets only
`overflow-y: auto` (`src/renderer/styles.css:5282-5288`), so `overflow-x`
computes to `auto`; the phase's row is now `padding-left: 8 + depth*16` plus a
non-shrinking 18px toggle, a 32px destination column and a 32px More
(`styles.css:5292-5376`, `SideRail.tsx:1780-1859`). Indent is the real
`editIndent` handler (`src/renderer/state/outlineEditor.ts:195-217`) and is not
depth-capped by the editor (the shared tree caps at 64 levels).

Repro: `node test-fixtures/adv-tfl1077/adv_navigator_probe.cjs` (P2) renders a
240px `.outline-panel` containing one 168px-indented row (depth 10).

Expected (phase success criterion 3 / attack surface 4): "no horizontal outline
scrolling"; the row's More stays reachable at the 240px floor.

Actual (probe output): `overflowX "auto"`, `scrollWidth 256`, `clientWidth 240`,
`horizontalOverflow: true`. With the coarse-pointer 44px More
(`styles.css:5378-5383`) the same overflow starts at depth 8; at the default
280px panel it starts around depth 11. When it overflows, the row's More button
leaves the visible box and a horizontal scrollbar appears on the outline.

Suggested fix: `overflow-x: hidden` (or `overflow: hidden auto`) on
`.outline-panel`, and/or clamp the indent so the fixed columns always fit (e.g.
cap the effective `padding-left` to the available width).

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-616 (MEDIUM, NEW-in-this-phase). Fix dispatched as TFL-1078.

## ADV-240: The outline tree's new `aria-level` sits on roleless divs, and the destination popover has no Escape / dismiss / focus return

- Session: diff-pass (Phase 111 chunk H/I)
- Suggested severity: LOW
- Classification: NEW-in-this-phase

What I did: read the Phase 111 outline diff and probed the DOM with the phase's
own focused specs. The diff adds `aria-level={depth + 1}` to the view-only row
(`src/renderer/components/SideRail.tsx:1649`) and to the editable row
(`SideRail.tsx:1786`), but neither row has a `role`, and `OutlinePanel` contains
no `role="tree"`, `role="treeitem"` or `role="group"` anywhere (grep of
`SideRail.tsx`). `aria-level` is only valid on a `treeitem`/`heading`/`row`
role, so it is ignored by assistive tech; the phase's D2b claim of screen-reader
tree navigation is not realized. Separately, the "Set destination..." popover
(`SideRail.tsx:1915-1942`) is an auto-focused `<select>` with only an `onChange`
commit: it has no Escape handler, no outside-pointer dismiss and no
focus-return, so a keyboard user who opens it and decides not to change the
target cannot cancel it.

Expected: real tree semantics (`role="tree"` on the list, `role="treeitem"` +
`aria-level`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-selected` on each row, `role="group"` on
nested lists), and a dismissible retarget surface with Escape + focus return
(the More menu itself already does this via `CommandMenu`).

Actual: `aria-level` on a roleless `<div>` (ignored); the retarget select only
closes on a value change.

Suggested fix: add the tree roles to the outline list/rows, or drop the orphan
`aria-level`; add an Escape/outside-pointer dismiss to the retarget popover that
returns focus to the row's More button.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-617 (LOW, NEW-in-this-phase). Fix dispatched as TFL-1078.

## Design critique: the Phase 111 Document Navigator surfaces (view selector, page cards, outline rows, Split Navigator)

User context: a desktop PDF user whose job is "find a page or bookmark, act on it,
and get back to reading"; success is that the current view, the batch selection
and the bookmark destination each read honestly and every row control is where it
says it is. Precedes: the canvas. Follows: the document view.

### Must-fix (blocks ship)
- **Affordance / positioning:** the outline row More menu and the destination
  popover detach from their row and are clipped at the panel bottom (ADV-238).
  The primary bookmark actions (Rename / Indent / Outdent / Delete / Set
  destination) are the inventory this chunk adds, so a displaced trigger is a
  core-surfaces failure, not polish. **Try:** end the outline body's materialize
  keyframe at `transform: none`, or portal the row menu/retarget popover to the
  body.

### Should-fix (before broader rollout)
- **Edge case / overflow:** a depth-9+ bookmark at the 240px floor, or depth-8
  with a coarse pointer, scrolls the outline horizontally and pushes the row's
  More out of view (ADV-239). **Try:** `overflow-x: hidden` on `.outline-panel`
  plus a clamp on the effective indent padding.
- **Accessibility:** the added `aria-level` is on roleless rows and the retarget
  popover cannot be cancelled (ADV-240). **Try:** add real `tree`/`treeitem`
  roles and an Escape/outside-dismiss path.

### Nice-to-fix (when there's room)
- **State honesty:** the panel More row flips label on the PERSISTED layout, not
  the EFFECTIVE one, so in a short window whose persisted layout is `split` (but
  which has fallen back to stacked) it still offers "Use stacked layout".
  Harmless but reads as a stale state. **Try:** label from
  `resolvedNavigatorLayout`.
- **Test coverage:** add the two navigator fields to the stale-echo sweep so the
  DEF-072 completeness guard actually covers them.

### Strengths to keep
- Current page vs batch selection is genuinely separated: a neutral current card
  with a violet leading marker + "Viewing" label, and the checkbox tint distinct
  from it - no inferred selection.
- The card checkbox and More are real sibling controls: the checkbox toggles the
  host set without navigating and opening More never jumps the page.
- The split fallback is measured from the real body box and degrades to the
  tabbed view rather than clipping; the divider is a real keyboard separator with
  live `aria-valuenow`.
- Cleanup is complete: the dead `SideRail` component, `SideRailProps`,
  `useRailSwapAnimation` and the `.rail-content-swap` rule are gone with only
  negative guards left behind.

## ADV-241: The Command Palette still exposes document-only commands (Save / Save a copy / Close Tab) on Home, enabled and silently no-op, behind an active Home tab

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: Traced every route to the document-only commands on the active
surface. The C4/R05 correction filters the File menu and the application menu
through `filterMenuGroupsForSurface` (`src/renderer/state/commandCapability.ts:48`,
consumed at `src/renderer/App.tsx:9915-9931`), hides the toolbar Save / Save As /
Print / Find (`src/renderer/components/AppHeader.tsx:284-360`), gates the
keyboard routes on `activeDocId` (`src/renderer/App.tsx:9566-9662`), and disables
the native items from the surface predicate (`App.tsx:9396`
`snapshotMenuEnabled(activeTabHasDocument, activeTabHasDocument)`). It does NOT
touch the Command Palette. The palette's own availability gate keys Save / Save
As / Close Tab on `availability: "tab"` and resolves that to
`tabs.activeId !== null`:

- `src/renderer/App.tsx:11184-11196` — `paletteAppActions.save` / `.saveAs` /
  `.closeTab` gate on `activeTabIdRefLocal.current !== null` only.
- `src/renderer/App.tsx:11337-11338` — `case "tab": return tabs.activeId !== null;`.
- `src/renderer/state/toolsRegistry.ts:1089-1107` (`save`, `saveAs`) and
  `:1231-1240` (`tabClose`) — `availability: 'tab'`.
- The palette lists the full registry (`CommandPalette.tsx:99-100`, `entries`
  defaults to the single registry) and is reachable on Home via the app menu's
  "Command Palette..." row (`App.tsx:9893`, action `showToolsPalette`,
  document-agnostic) or the `Ctrl+Shift+P` chord.

Repro (runtime probe a later run must execute — the phase's own
`e2e/tfl1116_r05_home_command_gating.spec.cjs` covers File menu / application
menu / toolbar / keyboard but never opens the palette):

1. Launch fresh (Home, zero documents).
2. Click a sample to open a document; then `[data-new-tab]` to create and
   activate an empty tab (the exact "document open BEHIND an active Home tab"
   state the R05 contract names, and the state its Case C tests).
3. Press `Ctrl+K` or `Ctrl+Shift+P` to open the Command Palette.
4. Search `Save`/`Save a copy`/`Close Tab`: the rows are PRESENT and, because
   the empty tab still has a non-null `tabs.activeId`, ENABLED.
5. Press Enter on "Save": it dispatches `onSave(activeTabId)` →
   `App.tsx:5130-5131` `openTabsRef.current[tabId]` is `undefined` for an empty
   tab → immediate `return`. Nothing happens, no toast, no state change.

Expected: on Home these commands are ABSENT (R05) — at minimum not offered as a
runnable, enabled row. Actual: present and enabled, and activating one is a
silent no-op (a click that triggers nothing, which the adversary rules classify
as a finding: it hides a missing surface gate behind a passing-looking control).
On a zero-tab Home they are at least present-but-disabled, still short of
"absent"; the enabled variant above is the concrete exploit.

Note: `undo` / `redo` are also listed but resolve to disabled on Home via
`appActionGates` (`App.tsx:10996-11002`) — that half is at least honest.

Fix direction (not applied): route the palette's availability through
`deriveCommandSurface`/`isDocumentOnlyMenuAction` (or drop
`DOCUMENT_ONLY_MENU_ACTIONS` rows from the palette corpus on `"home"`), and key
the `save`/`saveAs`/`tabClose` gate on `activeTabHasDocument`, not
`tabs.activeId !== null`.

## ADV-242: Book View reading location is lost when the reader leaves via a tab switch, not the Close button (R25 partial)

- Session: diff-pass
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: R25 wired the Book View reading location back through `onClose`.
`BookView.tsx:60` now types `onClose: (finalPage?: number) => void`;
`BookView.tsx:446-448` `handleClose` reports `displayIndex + 1`; the only caller
of `handleClose` is the header Close button (`BookView.tsx:650`). App persists it
at `App.tsx:11852-11863` (`initialPage={open.persisted.currentPage}` in,
`persistFor(meta.id)({ ...open.persisted, currentPage: finalPage })` out). But
Book View is rendered conditionally on `bookViewActive` (`App.tsx:1110`,
`App.tsx:11833`), and no other exit path invokes `onClose`: `activateTab`
(`App.tsx:10320-10339`) and `onTabStripActivate` do not call `closeBookView`
(`setBookViewTabId` appears only at `App.tsx:10730` open and `:10733` close).
`.book-view` is `flex: 1 1 auto` inside the stage (`styles.css:21446`), so the
AppHeader tab strip stays visible and clickable while Book View is open.

Repro (runtime probe a later run must execute; the phase's
`e2e/tfl1116_r24_r25_location.spec.cjs` only closes via the Close button):

1. Open a fixture with >= 8 pages, jump to page 5.
2. Open Book View — it starts at page 5 (correct).
3. Turn forward twice so the reader is on page 7 (`[data-book-progress]` reads 7).
4. Click a DIFFERENT tab in the tab strip (do not press Close). Book View
   unmounts and `onClose` never fires.
5. Click back to the original tab. Because `bookViewTabId` was never cleared,
   Book View RE-OPENS, but at `open.persisted.currentPage` = 5, not 7 — the
   reached location is lost, and the DocumentView footer/persisted reading page
   also still read 5.

Expected: leaving Book View by any route carries the reached location back (R25).
Actual: only the Close button does; a tab-away/tab-back round trip discards it.

Fix direction (not applied): clear `bookViewTabId` in `activateTab` (closing Book
View explicitly and reporting the page first), or lift the reading location out
of `handleClose` into a state that is published on unmount.

- **Overlay containment (C3/R03) — CLEAN.** `placeOverlay`
  (`overlayPlacement.ts:71-113`) clamps `left`/`top` into
  `[GAP, viewport - GAP - size]`, never returns a negative coordinate, flips
  below/above on fit, and bounds the box with `maxHeight = max(minHeight,
  min(maxHeightCap, sideSpace))`. `useOverlayPlacement`/`useSubmenuPlacement`
  measure the transform-independent `offsetWidth/offsetHeight` (DEF-618) and
  recompute on resize + capture-phase scroll; the root portals to `document.body`
  with `right:auto; width:max-content` (`CommandMenu.tsx:288-304`). Traced the
  960x640-minimum and maximized cases for the app menu (anchor near the right
  header edge, `align: "start"`): the horizontal clamp pins the right gutter to
  >= 8px and the vertical clamp pins to the 8px gutter; oversized boxes pin to
  the leading gutter rather than escaping. No path produces an out-of-viewport or
  negative coordinate. Probe run: code trace of every branch + the existing
  `e2e/tfl1116_r03_app_menu_fit.spec.cjs` oracle (not executed — build mutex).
- **Navigation sync (C5/R04, R24, R25 entry/exit) — CLEAN except ADV-242.**

  `e2e/tfl1116_r04_navigation_sync.spec.cjs`.
- **Document-scoped state (C2/R02, DEF-620/622) — CLEAN.** `exportDraft` is keyed
  by `tabs.activeId`, immutable, and resolved through `exportDraftFor`
  (`App.tsx:9942-9962`); a collapse remount/tab switch re-reads the stored draft
  because the Inspector's `ExportConfigSection` is controlled (`exportDraft !==
  undefined`), and reading it never runs an export. `livePageSizeScopeKey`
  (`pageSizeScope.ts:30-36`) keys Multi Mode by pane and single mode by tab id,
  and the report site and read site use the same function
  (`App.tsx:11944-11947` vs `:10643`), so no cross-tab map collision. Probe run:
  code trace of the write/read scope keys + the two existing unit specs.
- **Settings / R09 runtime gate — CLEAN.** `isDevelopmentBuild`
  (`devEnvironment.ts:29-41`) prefers the preload `isPackaged` boolean and falls
  back to Vite `PROD`/`DEV`; `recordSampleRecent` (`sampleRecents.ts:32-46`)
  writes `samples/<name>` only when dev, and the only sample-open path
  (`App.tsx:2662-2667`) routes through it, so production cannot pollute the MRU.
  The Home motion-pause write (`App.tsx:11718-11728`,
  `preferences.ts:258-264`) preserves-if-valid and short-circuits the default.
  Probe run: code trace + `test/unit/renderer/devEnvironment.test.ts`.

## Design critique: the changed Home / navigator / overlay surfaces (TFL-1116 C16)

User context: a desktop PDF user whose job is "get a document open and reading,
then find/act on a page, without the chrome lying about what is available";
success is that every surface offers only commands that can actually run.
Precedes: launching the app. Follows: the document canvas.

### Must-fix (blocks ship)
- **Affordance / consistency:** the Command Palette offers document-only commands
  on Home as runnable, enabled rows that do nothing (ADV-241). Because the
  palette is the app's browse-everything surface, an enabled dead row is worse
  here than a missing one — it trains the user to distrust the palette. **Try:**
  filter the palette corpus by `commandSurface`, mirroring the menus.

### Should-fix (before broader rollout)
- **State honesty:** Book View's reading location silently resets when the reader
  changes tab instead of pressing Close (ADV-242). **Try:** make any Book View
  exit publish the reached page, not just the Close button.

### Nice-to-fix (when there's room)
- **Error/empty copy:** on a zero-tab Home the palette still lists Save / Save a
  copy / Close Tab as disabled rows with no reason; consider hiding them (R05's
  "absent") rather than showing a disabled set the user can never need on Home.

### Strengths to keep
- The File menu, application menu, title-row toolbar and keyboard all derive
  their document-only visibility from ONE pure evaluator
  (`commandCapability.ts`), so those four routes cannot drift apart again.
- The overlay placement is one shared pure rule for root and submenu, measured
  transform-independently, so a long accelerator label can no longer stretch the
  app menu to the window edge.
- The navigator reveal distinguishes a committed jump from a user scroll with a
  single counter, preserving the Bug-3 "don't recentre while reading" behaviour
  while still revealing an external jump.

## CTO triage log (2026-10-07) - TFL-1116 C16 diff-pass

- ADV-241: ACCEPTED -> DEF-626 (MEDIUM). The R05 correction does not cover the
  Command Palette; the document-only Save / Save a copy / Close Tab rows remain
  present and enabled on Home (behind an active empty tab) and silently no-op.
  Owner frontend-dev (TFL-1176). Not REJECTED: gate 1 requires document-only
  commands to be absent from the command surface on Home.
- ADV-242: ACCEPTED -> DEF-627 (MEDIUM). R25 reports the Book View reading
  location only via the header Close button; leaving Book View by switching tabs
  loses the reached location. Owner frontend-dev (TFL-1176).

## ADV-243: Toggle Theme leaves `themeDefault` stale — the AR-08 residue and the Preferences/shell disagreement are still reproducible

- Session: diff-pass (phase-gate, TFL-1146)
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did (built app v1.51.0, `scaleFactor` 1.5, window 1220x961 DIP maximized,
launched with a fresh userData through `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`):
1. App menu -> Edit > Preferences. The "Theme default" dropdown shows `Light`.
2. Select `Dark`. Live `<html data-theme>` becomes `dark`, and `settings.json`
   becomes `theme=dark, themeDefault=dark` — the atomic AR-08 fix works for a
   dropdown pick.
3. Close Preferences. App menu -> View > Toggle Theme (the shipped cycle route;
   `nextTheme('dark')` -> `light`).
4. Live `<html data-theme>` becomes `light`, but `settings.json` is now
   `theme=light, themeDefault=dark` — the exact residue the AR-08 fix comment
   (`src/renderer/state/theme.ts:35`) claims "can never" occur.
5. Reopen Preferences: the dropdown reads `Dark` while the shell is visibly
   `Light`.

Expected: per Additional Live Review item 6 ("selecting Dark must change all app
surfaces coherently and persist after relaunch") and item 7 of the audit
(AR-08), `themeDefault` and the effective theme stay coherent after any theme
change, so Preferences never shows a theme that disagrees with the shell.

Actual: `onToggleTheme` (`src/renderer/App.tsx:1790-1798`) writes only
`theme: nextTheme(prev.theme)` and never touches `themeDefault`. The shipped
Toggle Theme command therefore produces `theme=light, themeDefault=dark`, and
Preferences (`themeDefault={settings.themeDefault ?? settings.theme}`,
`App.tsx:13136`) then displays a theme that disagrees with the effective one.
The correction pass only made the dropdown pick atomic; it did not make the
toggle coherent nor reconcile the residue.

Evidence:
- `screenshots/adv-243-theme-residue.png` (Preferences open: dropdown `Dark`,
  shell light).
- Probe `test-fixtures/tfl1188-adversary/live_probe_theme.cjs` — prints
  `PERSISTED theme=light themeDefault=dark` and
  `VERDICT residue=true (select=dark, live=light)`.
- Unit probe `test-fixtures/tfl1188-adversary/adv_probe.test.ts`
  ("a live theme toggle keeps the persisted themeDefault equal to the effective
  theme (AR-08 invariant)") — fails.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-628 (MEDIUM). CTO triage 2026-10-07 (TFL-1146): in scope - AR-08 requires the persisted and effective theme to be coherent and not present two conflicting states; the View > Toggle Theme command is a live theme route that leaves `themeDefault` stale. Routed to frontend-dev; qa to close after retest.

## ADV-244: Extract accepts malformed tokens with trailing garbage and acts on the leading number

- Session: diff-pass (phase-gate, TFL-1146)
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did (built app v1.51.0): opened the bundled `report.pdf` (34 pages),
opened the Extract dialog (View/Edit tool `extract`), and typed these values into
`#split-page-range`, reading `#split-range-status` and the confirm button state:
`1abc`, `2-3x`, `1.9`, `12px`.

Expected: per Additional Live Review item 5 ("Distinguish empty input, syntax
errors, ... out-of-bounds pages ..."; "Keep Extract/Split disabled until the
entire input is acceptable"), a token carrying trailing garbage is a syntax
error: the field reads `malformed`, `pages` is null, and Extract stays disabled.

Actual: all four inputs classify as `valid` and Extract is ENABLED:
`1abc` -> "1 page selected" (page 1), `2-3x` -> "2 pages selected" (pages 2-3),
`1.9` -> "1 page selected", `12px` -> "1 page selected". `classifyPageRange`
(`src/renderer/engine/types.ts:966-967, 982`) uses `Number.parseInt`, which
silently discards the non-numeric suffix, so the whole-input gate is bypassed and
a malformed entry is acted on. QA's `e2e/tfl1183_ar07_08_09_live.spec.cjs` covers
`abc` and `9-2` but never a number-plus-suffix, so this passed QA.

Evidence:
- `screenshots/adv-244-range-trailing-garbage.png` (`1abc`, state `valid`,
  Extract enabled).
- `test-fixtures/tfl1188-adversary/live_probe_range.log` (full case table).
- Unit probe `test-fixtures/tfl1188-adversary/adv_probe.test.ts`
  ("rejects tokens with trailing garbage rather than acting on the leading
  number") — fails.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-629 (MEDIUM). CTO triage 2026-10-07 (TFL-1146): in scope - AR-07 requires syntax errors to be distinguished and Extract/Split disabled until the WHOLE input is valid; `Number.parseInt` silently drops a trailing suffix. Routed to frontend-dev; qa to close after retest.

## ADV-245: Out-of-bounds span names only the upper endpoint, never the lower one

- Session: diff-pass (phase-gate, TFL-1146)
- Suggested severity: LOW

What I did (built app v1.51.0): same Extract dialog on the 34-page `report.pdf`;
typed `50-60` and `35-40`.

Expected: per AR-07 ("It should identify allowed range 1–34 and the invalid
token"), a span whose lower end is also above the document maximum names every
offending endpoint, so the user is not led to believe the lower number is
acceptable.

Actual: `50-60` -> "Page 60 is outside the document's 1-34 pages." and
`35-40` -> "Page 40 is outside the document's 1-34 pages." — `50` and `35`
respectively are unnamed. `classifyPageRange`'s span branch
(`src/renderer/engine/types.ts:971-976`) adds `lo` only when `lo < 1`; it never
adds `lo` when `lo > totalPages`, so only the `hi` endpoint is reported for a
wholly-above-range span. The gate itself is correct (Extract disabled, pages
null); this is the new `invalidTokens` feature's message precision.

Evidence:
- `screenshots/adv-245-range-span-endpoint.png`.
- `test-fixtures/tfl1188-adversary/live_probe_range.log`.
- Unit probe `test-fixtures/tfl1188-adversary/adv_probe.test.ts`
  ("names BOTH ends of a wholly out-of-bounds span") — fails.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-630 (LOW). CTO triage 2026-10-07 (TFL-1146): in scope - AR-07's `invalidTokens` message must name the offending token(s); a wholly-above-range span currently names only its upper endpoint. Routed to frontend-dev (folded with DEF-629); qa to close after retest.

## Design critique: the TFL-1146 changed surfaces (Preferences Appearance, compact drawer, Home Recents)

User context: a desktop PDF reader who sets preferences once and expects the
shell to match them, and who navigates a document from a compact window.

### Must-fix (blocks ship)
- **State honesty:** the "Theme default" row claims "Applies immediately, and is
  the theme the app starts in on the next launch", but after View > Toggle Theme
  the dropdown and the live shell show different themes with no visible override
  indicator (ADV-243). **Try:** have Toggle Theme write the default too (or show
  the live override beside the default) so the surface never contradicts the
  shell.
- **Inputs / validation:** the range field shows a green "N pages selected" and
  an enabled Extract for `1abc` (ADV-244). **Try:** reject any token whose text
  is not a clean integer/range before it can register as valid.

### Should-fix (before broader rollout)
- **Error copy:** an out-of-bounds span names only its top end (ADV-245).
  **Try:** name every endpoint outside 1..totalPages, or quote the whole token.

### Nice-to-fix (when there's room)
- **Copy:** the "Theme default" hint does not mention the View > Toggle Theme
  override at all; a short clause would explain why a later session can differ.

### Strengths to keep
- The Preferences pick is now a single atomic write (`applyThemeDefault`), so
  picking Dark can no longer leave the documented `theme=light, themeDefault=dark`
  residue on its own.
- Range validation keeps Extract/Split disabled for genuine out-of-bounds and
  malformed input, and names the bound (`1-34`) for the simple cases the audit
  cited.
- The compact drawer exposes `aria-expanded` in both states and returns focus to
  the collapse control on Escape and close.

## TFL-1201 diff-pass — ER20 export truthfulness + ER24 stamp placement: NO FINDINGS

- Session: diff-pass (TFL-1201)
- Build under attack: app v1.51.0, dev renderer built from HEAD `dc68679` plus the
  uncommitted TFL-1197/1199 working-tree changes (`npm run build` exit 0).
- Suggested severity: none — no finding met the bar. No ADV entry is filed.

No ADV-246 (or any) entry is created: the five mandated attack classes for this
diff all held, and I will not fabricate a finding. The exact commands and
observed results are recorded below so the CTO can audit the negative result.

### Attack 1 — Export truthfulness (displayed count/scheme vs actual written files)

The shipped renderer save path is an anchor download (`downloadBlob`,
`src/renderer/utils/exportDownload.ts:25`). Playwright's Electron transport does
not surface `download` events for this build (verified: `mechanism_check.log`
shows `[download-events] []` while the real write fired), so the probe observes
the real write at its primitive — `HTMLAnchorElement.prototype.click` with the
product's `download` filename and blob — and materializes those exact bytes into
`test-fixtures/tfl1201-adversary/out-export-truth/`. No product file is patched;
this is runtime observation of the only save call the app makes.

Command: `node test-fixtures/tfl1201-adversary/probe_export_truth.cjs`
(plus `probe_unicode.cjs`). Results:

- 34-page `report.pdf` + Images - PNG + All pages: display `"34 files"` and
  scheme `<stem>-page-1.png … <stem>-page-34.png`; actual = **34** files, all 34
  start with the PNG magic `89504e470d0a1a0a`, and the first/last names equal the
  displayed scheme exactly. (`out-export-truth/caseA-report-png-all/`)
- 1-page fixture + PNG + All pages: display `"1 file"`, scheme
  `fixture-onepage-page-1.png`; actual = **1** file, valid PNG.
- 34-page + PNG + custom `1,1,34`: display `"2 files"`, scheme spans page-1 …
  page-34; actual = **2** files (`…-page-1.png`, `…-page-34.png`). The duplicate is
  deduped by the real parser, the count is honest, and the dialog re-parses the
  seed to a matching `1,34` (`rangeSummary` shows the raw user text `1,1,34`).
- 34-page + Text (.txt): display is the single name `<stem>.txt` and **no**
  `[data-export-config-output-scheme]` element is rendered.
- Hostile source name (`Adversary Rëport Ünïcode v1.2.pdf`, spaces + unicode +
  extra dot) + PNG + `1,3`: display `"2 files"` scheme
  `Adversary Rëport Ünïcode v1.2-page-1.png … …-page-3.png`; actual names are
  byte-identical to the displayed scheme.

### Attack 2 — Export gating preserved

Same probe. Invalid range `1,999` on a 34-page doc: `[data-export-config-output-value]`
shows `—`, the action `[data-inspector-action="export"]` is `disabled`, and the
range error names the bound (`Page 999 is outside the document's 1-34 pages.`).
Typing `9999` into the DPI field clamps to `600`; typing `10` clamps to `72`. No
new copy path bypasses validation or alters the save flow (the summary is a pure
display function with no side effects).

### Attack 3 — Stamp placement (ER24)

Command: `node test-fixtures/tfl1201-adversary/probe_stamp.cjs` on a disposable
`getSamplePath('report.pdf')` copy. Results: dialog confirm reads
`Start placement` and the page picker `[data-stamp-page-select]` is gone;
confirming arms the ghost `[data-stamp-layer]` with **0** `[data-stamp-annotation]`;
Escape before any click detaches the layer with **0** annotations and no undo
entry; a single page click places **exactly one** stamp (`canUndo=true`) and
disarms the layer; a second immediate click does **not** place a second stamp
(still 1); Undo removes it (0). The source copy's sha256 and byte size are
identical before and after (`9b39af69…`, 33028 bytes) — no in-place write.

### Attack 4 / 5 — Image dialog content height, cancel, resize, reopen

Command: `node test-fixtures/tfl1201-adversary/probe_dialog.cjs`. At 985x645 the
empty Create-from-images dialog is 444 px (no list, no grow marker), the filled
one grows to 464 px (list + grow marker), and the footer confirm stays in view in
both. Resizing while open to 960x1392 and back to 1024x768 keeps the confirm in
view with zero horizontal-overflow descendants. Escape cancels with no document
mutation (Home still shown, tab count unchanged, no toast); reopening restores the
empty state with no stale list and no stray toast/flash.

### Classes that held (TFL-1201 diff-pass)

- **ER20 export copy — HOLDS.** Displayed count and naming scheme equal the real
  written files for 34p/1p/duplicate-range/txt and a hostile unicode+space name.
- **Export gating — HOLDS.** Invalid range disables the action; DPI clamps to
  72..600; the summary is display-only.
- **ER24 stamp flow — HOLDS.** Arm / no-stamp-before-click / Escape-cancel /
  one-click-one-stamp / Undo / source untouched.
- **ER18 image-dialog grow + boundary — HOLDS.** Content-driven height, reachable
  footer, resize-safe, clean reopen.

Baseline: `npm run build` exit 0 (typecheck + renderer + node).

### Design critique: the TFL-1201 changed surfaces (Deliver export config, Stamp dialog, image dialog)

User context: a desktop PDF user preparing a multi-file image export and placing a
stamp on a document; they glance once at the output summary and expect it to match
what lands on disk.

#### Must-fix (blocks ship)
- None.

#### Should-fix (before broader rollout)
- **Copy:** in the duplicate-range case the "Pages" row echoes the raw input
  (`1,1,34`) while the output row says `2 files`, so a fast reader can briefly
  wonder where the third file went. **Try:** optionally echo the resolved scope
  beside the count (e.g. `2 files (pages 1, 34)`).

#### Nice-to-fix (when there's room)
- **States:** the `…` ellipsis scheme is precise but terse; a one-line "one PNG
  per selected page" clause would remove any remaining ambiguity for first-time
  exporters.

#### Strengths to keep
- The count and naming example reuse the ONE real filename helper
  (`defaultExportFilename`), so the copy cannot drift from the save flow.
- The scheme degrades honestly: office formats keep the single-name display and
  render no scheme element at all.
- The stamp dialog now states the real click-to-place + Escape-cancel flow and no
  longer promises a page/centering the handler ignores.

## ADV-246: A settings-write rollback can drop a newer legitimate settings value and revert the UI to an older snapshot

- Session: diff-pass (TFL-1254, Phase 114 chunk C)
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: attacked the chunk-C claim "a failed settings write restores the prior
value in the UI" at the renderer event level. I modelled the exact chunk-C
bookkeeping (`settingsWriteSeqRef` -> seq, `settingsPersistedRef` -> ref,
`onSettingsRestore` -> `ref = diskSnapshot` with seq untouched) and fed every
decision through the REAL `shouldApplyEcho` the `settings.changed` listener uses
(`node --experimental-strip-types test-fixtures/tfl1254-adversary/probe_rollback_echo.mjs`):

1. Write #1 (theme `frosted`) goes out optimistically: `trackAndSave` -> seq 1, ref X.
2. A rapid second change (theme `light`) goes out before the failure surfaces:
   `trackAndSave` -> seq 2, ref Z.
3. Write #1 fails; main rolls back and pushes `settings:writeError`; the hook calls
   `loadSettings()` and `onSettingsRestore(disk)` with the pre-toggle value P ->
   `settingsPersistedRef = P`, **seq stays 2** (`App.tsx:1901-1905`).
4. Write #2 then succeeds and main broadcasts its `settings.changed` echo (content Z).

Expected: the echo for the write that actually reached disk (Z) is applied, so the
UI converges on the value on disk.

Actual: `shouldApplyEcho(Z, seq=2, ref=P)` returns **false** — `writeSeq !== 0`,
content differs from the snapshot, and it is not a recents-/geometry-only diff
(`settingsEcho.ts:430-459`) — so the legitimate newer echo is discarded while
`shouldApplyEcho(P, seq, ref)` returns true. The probe output:

```
after two writes: seq = 2
echo Z without restore -> true (expect true)
after restore: ref = P, seq = 2
echo Z AFTER restore -> false (false = legitimate newer value DROPPED)
echo P AFTER restore -> true (true = stale value re-applied)
```

So after a failed write, a newer successful write's echo can be permanently
dropped and the UI left showing the older restored value while disk holds the newer
one. The next whole-object write the renderer makes (it persists `{...settingsState}`)
can then overwrite the newer disk value with the stale UI state, turning the
divergence into silent loss of the newer setting. `onSettingsRestore` overwriting
`settingsPersistedRef` without advancing `settingsWriteSeqRef` is the root cause;
the restore snapshot is assumed to be newer than any in-flight write, which the
interleaving above violates.

Reachability: needs a write failure (the exact scenario this feature exists for)
plus one more settings write issued before the failure round-trip completes (rapid
toggles/sliders). Verified at the decision-logic level with the shipped pure
filter; the scheduler timing of the fs write is what decides whether the restore
snapshot or write #2's echo wins.

Test gap (escape): the dev's own `test/unit/renderer/phase114_settingsRollback.test.tsx`
exercises the hook in isolation with stable callback props and a mocked bridge; it
never wires the hook's `onRestore` to `settingsPersistedRef` + `shouldApplyEcho`, so
it cannot see this race. The hook contract holds; the integration does not.

Evidence: `test-fixtures/tfl1254-adversary/probe_rollback_echo.mjs`,
`test-fixtures/tfl1254-adversary/probe_rollback_echo.log`.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-637 (MEDIUM). CTO triage 2026-10-08 (TFL-1219): real
integration race - after a failed-write restore the echo filter has
`settingsPersistedRef` set but `settingsWriteSeqRef` not advanced, so a newer
legitimate `settings.changed` is dropped and the UI diverges from disk (a later
whole-object write can then clobber the newer disk value). Owner frontend-dev;
fix tracked as TFL-1262 (restore must keep the echo filter coherent).

## ADV-247: When `loadSettings()` fails after a write error, the UI keeps the value that never persisted

- Session: diff-pass (TFL-1254, Phase 114 chunk C)
- Suggested severity: LOW

What I did: followed the hook's write-failure branch
(`src/renderer/hooks/useSettingsWriteRollback.ts:28-37`). On `settings:writeError` it
calls `onError(message)` (the toast) unconditionally, then
`window.tflex.loadSettings().then(result => { if (result.ok) onRestore(result.value); }).catch(() => undefined)`.

Expected: per the claim, a failed write restores the prior value in the UI. If the
authoritative re-read cannot be obtained, the UI must still not keep a value that
never persisted (or the failure must be surfaced as a distinct state).

Actual: when `loadSettings()` rejects, or resolves with `ok: false` (io / corrupt
read, `src/main/services/settings.ts:1552-1576`), no `onRestore` fires, so the
optimistically-applied value stays in the UI with only the generic toast. The
restore is best-effort, so the claim holds only when the re-read succeeds; the
"keeps a value that never persisted" case the change is meant to close is still
reachable on the load-failure path. Narrow (needs the same store to be
unreadable while a write failed), hence LOW.

Evidence: source trace `useSettingsWriteRollback.ts:30-35` (no restore on the
non-`ok` and catch branches).

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-638 (LOW). CTO triage 2026-10-08 (TFL-1219): when the
`loadSettings()` re-read rejects or returns `ok:false`, no restore fires and the UI
keeps the value that never persisted. Owner frontend-dev; fix tracked as TFL-1262
(fall back to the last confirmed snapshot).

## ADV-248: A settings write queued behind a failed write is persisted as the rolled-back value, silently dropping the newer change

- Session: diff-pass (TFL-1254, Phase 114 chunk C)
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: traced the backend the chunk-C rollback rides
(`src/main/services/settings.ts`, DEF-230), because "restores the prior value"
depends on what actually reaches disk. `save(s)` sets `this.current = normalize(s)`
and enqueues `_doSave(this.current)` — the argument is read **when the queued task
runs**, not at enqueue time (`settings.ts:1578-1583`). On a failed write the catch
sets `this.current = structuredClone(this.persisted)` (`settings.ts:1636-1637`).

Expected: a second settings write issued after a first one fails still persists its
own value (the newer one), so the user's latest change is not silently dropped.

Actual: sequence — write #1 (value X) fails; write #2 (value Z) was enqueued before
write #1 settled. Write #1's catch rolls `this.current` back to P; write #2's task
then runs `_doSave(this.current)` and reads P, so it persists P and echoes P. The
user's newer Z never reaches disk, and the renderer converges to P (via ADV-246's
restore/echo path) with only the generic toast. The new `loadSettings()` call in
`useSettingsWriteRollback.ts:31` compounds the same hazard: `load()` also mutates
`this.current`/`this.persisted` from disk (`settings.ts:1573-1574`) while queued
writes read `this.current` at execution, so a rollback re-read can additionally
clobber a pending write.

This is pre-existing DEF-230 backend behaviour rather than one of the two diff
files, but the chunk-C feature's promise ("the UI drops the value it optimistically
showed") is built on it and does not close the corresponding disk-side loss; filed
so the CTO can route it. Static trace only (build mutex held by qa for TFL-1255 and
the task forbids builds/e2e), not runtime-reproduced.

Evidence: `src/main/services/settings.ts:1578-1583, 1615-1638, 1573-1574`;
`src/renderer/hooks/useSettingsWriteRollback.ts:31`.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-639 (MEDIUM). CTO triage 2026-10-08 (TFL-1219):
`save()` reads `this.current` when the queued task runs, so a failed write's
rollback makes the next queued write persist the rolled-back value - the newer
change is silently dropped on disk. CTO re-rules Phase 114 scope to allow this
main-process persistence-correctness fix (no settings field, no new IPC). Owner
backend-dev; fix tracked as TFL-1263 (snapshot the argument at call time).

## Classes that held (TFL-1254 diff-pass)

- **`onRestore`/`onError` identity churn (attack 2) — HOLDS. No missing event.**
  The hook's effect deps are `[onRestore, onError]`
  (`useSettingsWriteRollback.ts:37`). `onSettingsWriteError` depends on `pushToast`
  (`useCallback`, `[]`, `App.tsx:1885-1887`), `onSettingsRestore` depends on
  `applySettings` (`App.tsx:1901-1905`), and `applySettings` depends only on
  `setTheme` (`App.tsx:1471-1506`), which is `useCallback(..., [])`
  (`useAnimations.ts:523, 597`). All three identities are stable across renders, so
  the `settings:writeError` listener is not torn down/re-registered mid-flight and
  cannot miss an event. This also means the sibling `settings.changed` effect's
  `applySettings` dep (`App.tsx:1600`) does not re-run `runBoot`.
- **Failed THEME write revert (attack 4) — HOLDS for the normal path.**
  `onToggleTheme` applies the theme optimistically (`App.tsx:1799-1814`); on rollback
  `applySettings` sees `<html data-theme>` differs and calls `setTheme(restored)`
  (`App.tsx:1503-1505`), which is a single, genuine revert crossfade — not the
  DEF-199 double-apply (that guard is on an *identical* theme and `lastAppliedRef`
  is the failed theme, so the revert is legitimate). Residual, not filed: on the
  `view-transition` strategy `applyTheme` writes `data-theme` inside the async
  update callback (`useAnimations.ts:567-568`, `state/theme.ts:8`), so a restore
  landing in the one-frame window before that callback runs would read the old
  attribute, skip the revert, and then let the pending transition paint the failed
  theme — a `settings` vs `<html>` desync. The writeError+load round-trip is far
  longer than that window, so I could not justify filing it; noted for the
  maintainer.
- **No double toast / double restore on repeated failures — HOLDS.** Each
  `writeError` yields exactly one toast and one `loadSettings()`; repeated failures
  re-apply the same disk snapshot idempotently.

Method note: build mutex held by qa (TFL-1255) at review time and the task forbids
`build`/e2e, so this pass is source-review plus one plain-Node probe of the shipped
pure filter (`shouldApplyEcho`), no vitest/build/e2e. Baseline: not run (mutex).

## ADV-249: A foreign annotation whose /T or /M is a hex string loses its author and modified date on the next save

- Session: diff-pass (unassigned heartbeat; Phase 116 engine change `annotations.ts` /T + /M, uncommitted, parent TFL-1228)
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM (silent loss of existing metadata in the user's file on save)

What I did: attacked the uncommitted Phase 116 change (`annotations.ts:796-799`
read via `parsePdfString`, `:1007-1012` `hasAuthor`/`hasModifiedAt`, `:1710-1718`
write via `serializeAnnotation`) with a PDF whose annotation `/T` (author) and
`/M` (modified date) are encoded as `PDFHexString` (UTF-16BE). That is what a
foreign viewer writes for any non-Latin1 author (Acrobat/Preview/Chrome all emit
hex for CJK, Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic). Probe:
`node test-fixtures/tfl116-adversary/probe-ann-metadata.mjs`; specimen
`test-fixtures/tfl116-adversary/foreign-hex-author.pdf`.

Expected (per the chunk's own claim "engine read + preserve" and the adjacent
`/NM` reader that deliberately accepts `PDFHexString` at `annotations.ts:154-170`):
the hex `/T` and `/M` decode like any other text string and are re-serialized.

Actual: `parsePdfString` (`annotations.ts:796-799`) accepts ONLY
`val instanceof PDFString` and returns `undefined` for a `PDFHexString` (they are
not related classes in pdf-lib). So `hasAuthor`/`hasModifiedAt` are both false,
the `AnnModel` carries no author/date, and `serializeAnnotation` omits both
entries. Because every save rebuilds modeled annotations from the `AnnModel`
(`serializeAnnotations` strips the source dicts, `annotations.ts:1956-1958`, and
`serializeAnnotation` pushes a fresh `dictEntries` list, `:1674-1718`) the
original `/T` and `/M` are gone from the output bytes. Probe output:

```
=== A: foreign /T and /M encoded as PDFHexString (UTF-16BE) ===
  on disk instanceof PDFString : false
  on disk instanceof PDFHexString: true
  disk raw decodeText           : José Author
  product parsePdfString(/T)    : undefined
  product parsePdfString(/M)    : undefined
  -> hasAuthor = false
=== D: end-to-end metadata loss for a hex-encoded foreign /T ===
  parsed author: undefined
  after save+reload: has /T ? false
  after save+reload: has /M ? false
  -> original CJK author + date LOST on save
```

`parseAnnotationsFromDoc` (`annotations.ts:1081-1094`) admits every modeled
subtype annotation regardless of origin, and the main save path re-serializes them
(`engine.ts:7213` and `:7386`), so any real-world PDF carrying a comment authored
in a non-Latin script loses that author/date the first time it is saved from
TFlex. The round-trip is not content-corrupting but it is silent, irreversible
metadata loss in the user's only copy - the class the doctrine ranks highest.

Reachability: open any PDF whose annotation `/T`/`/M` are hex strings (UTF-16BE)
and save. The sibling `/NM` reader already handles exactly this encoding, so the
new `/T`/`/M` reader is an inconsistency in the same file, not a new capability.

Test gap: the dev's `test/unit/main/phase116_annMetadata.test.ts` builds the
source with `PDFString.of(...)` only (`:29-30`), so it never exercises the
`PDFHexString` branch that real documents use.

Fix direction (for the CTO to route; not fixed here): decode `/T` and `/M` with a
`PDFString | PDFHexString` aware helper (as `parseAnnotationNameId` already does)
and re-emit non-Latin1 text with `PDFHexString.fromText`.

Evidence: `test-fixtures/tfl116-adversary/probe-ann-metadata.mjs`,
`test-fixtures/tfl116-adversary/probe-ann-metadata.log`,
`test-fixtures/tfl116-adversary/foreign-hex-author.pdf`.

Disposition: PENDING.

## ADV-250: A non-Latin1 annotation author is written into /T as mojibake because the write path uses PDFString.of

- Session: diff-pass (unassigned heartbeat; Phase 116 engine change `annotations.ts` /T + /M, uncommitted, parent TFL-1228)
- Suggested severity: LOW (latent - the write line is in the diff, but no renderer currently sets `AnnModel.author`; fix or land the setter with the encoder)

What I did: exercised the write half of the same change,
`annotations.ts:1713-1714` `PDFString.of(ann.author)`, against non-Latin1 authors
in the shipped `@cantoo/pdf-lib` (probe above, sections B and C).

Expected: an author name is stored as readable text and decodes back to the
same string on reload.

Actual: `PDFString.of` silently encodes only Latin1/PDFDocEncoding; for
`'李雷'` it produces a literal whose `decodeText()` is `"N÷"` (no throw, no
error), and that is exactly what lands in `/T` after save+reload:

```
  of("李雷") -> decodeText="N÷" ok=false
  CJK reloaded /T decodeText: "N÷"
```

So once any surface lets the user set an author (the Thread Stream chunks that
follow), a CJK/Cyrillic/Greek name will be persisted as corrupt bytes. `'José'`
(Latin1) round-trips fine, so the dev's ASCII-only test passes while the defect
stays hidden. The correct encoding for non-Latin1 text is
`PDFHexString.fromText(ann.author)` (the read path must then accept it too - see
ADV-249; the two should be fixed together).

Evidence: `test-fixtures/tfl116-adversary/probe-ann-metadata.mjs` (sections B/C),
`test-fixtures/tfl116-adversary/probe-ann-metadata.log`.

Disposition: PENDING.

## Classes that held (Phase 116 /T + /M diff-pass)

- **Absent / whitespace-only values stay absent — HOLDS.** `hasAuthor` /
  `hasModifiedAt` trim before deciding (`annotations.ts:1009-1010`) and the write
  side re-checks `trim().length > 0` (`:1713, :1716`), so neither a missing entry
  nor a whitespace-only one leaks a `''` placeholder into the dict or the model.
- **Latin1 literal round-trip — HOLDS.** A `PDFString` `/T` (what TFlex itself
  writes, and what most ASCII-authored PDFs carry) parses and re-serializes
  byte-exact; probe section C shows `'José'` reloads as `'José'`.
- **Non-string `/T` (name / number / array) is dropped, not thrown — HOLDS.**
  `parsePdfString` returns `undefined` for anything that is not a PDF string, so a
  hostile dict entry cannot crash the open or save path.
- **Phase 115 `FormField.required` / `/TU` read — HOLDS.** `decodeTextObject`
  (`forms.ts:495-504`) is duck-typed on `.decodeText()` and therefore accepts
  `PDFHexString` as well as `PDFString`, so a hex `/TU` tooltip is not dropped;
  the Required bit test (`forms.ts:678`) mirrors the existing ReadOnly pattern.
  Residual, not filed: `tooltip !== ''` (`forms.ts:681`) does not trim, so a
  whitespace-only `/TU` surfaces as a blank accessible name (`"   "`); advice, not
  a defect.

Method note: unassigned idle heartbeat with no ready adversary issue (both open
assignments TFL-1248 and TFL-1259 are dependency-blocked via their `heartbeat-context`
`blockedBy` chains). Build mutex was absent and not taken; this is source review
plus one plain-Node probe against the shipped `@cantoo/pdf-lib` - no vitest, build
or e2e. Findings left PENDING for CTO triage; fixture and probe left uncommitted
for git-agent.



## ADV-251: A mid-dispatch Remove silently skips the next queued file (live-array mutation across the openPdf await)

- Session: diff-pass (unassigned heartbeat; Phase 118 intake model chunk B `src/renderer/intake/model.ts`, uncommitted, TFL-1248 / parent TFL-1230)
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: drove the shipped `createIntakeModel().dispatch` with three ready PDFs
(`a`, `b`, `c`) and removed the row currently being opened - the realistic shape,
because `IntakeTray` keeps every Remove button enabled while a multi-PDF open runs
(the tray has no busy state). Plain-Node probe (Node type-stripping), no
vitest/build/e2e: `node test-fixtures/tfl1248-adversary/probe-intake-dispatch.mjs`.

Expected: removing a row affects only that row; the remaining queued files still
open, in order (success criterion 3/7 and the task's "no silent ... drop of extra
files").

Actual: `dispatch` iterates the LIVE queue with `for (const item of list)`
(`model.ts:223`) and awaits `openPdf` inside the loop. A `remove()` during that
await splices the array, so the array iterator's next index lands past the
following unvisited item: `b.pdf` is never visited - not opened, not reported as
skipped - and stays `ready` with no error. It silently disappears from the
dispatch pass. Probe output:
```
=== D: remove while a dispatch is in flight ===
  opened: ["C:\\q\\a.pdf","C:\\q\\c.pdf"]
  skipped ids: []
  b.pdf (id=id2) was NOT removed by the user - visited by dispatch? false
  remaining queue: [["id2","ready"],["id3","done"]]
```
The same hazard applies to `reorder` during the await (order shifts under the
iterator). `items()` returns a copy, but `dispatch` does not use it. Fix direction
(route via CTO; not fixed here): iterate a snapshot (`list.slice()`) and/or guard
`dispatch` with an in-flight flag surfaced to the tray so Remove/reorder are
disabled while a dispatch runs.

Evidence: `test-fixtures/tfl1248-adversary/probe-intake-dispatch.mjs`,
`test-fixtures/tfl1248-adversary/probe-intake-dispatch.log` (section D).

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-655 (CTO triage 2026-10-08, TFL-1230). The dispatch loop must not lose a queued file to a mid-flight Remove: snapshot the queue before iterating and skip ids no longer present in `list`, so a Remove affects only that row. In scope for Phase 118 (truthful intake). Fix in flight as TFL-1346.

## ADV-252: Two dispatches during one slow PDF open build the images PDF twice

- Session: diff-pass (unassigned heartbeat; Phase 118 intake model chunk B `src/renderer/intake/model.ts`, uncommitted, TFL-1248 / parent TFL-1230)
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: queued two images then a PDF (`[one.png, two.png, doc.pdf]`), started
`dispatch`, and - while the PDF `openPdf` was still pending - started a second
`dispatch` (a double trigger of "open all", the "repeat-storm / run during another
operation" attack class). Probe section E.

Expected: `createFromImages` runs exactly once per image collection; a second
dispatch while one is in flight either no-ops or reports busy.

Actual: image items are only moved to `converting` AFTER the PDF loop
(`model.ts:246-247`), so they stay `ready` throughout the `openPdf` await. The
second dispatch collects the same still-`ready` images and calls
`createFromImages`, and when the first dispatch resumes its own already-collected
`imageItems` call it again - two PDF builds for one image set:
```
=== E: repeat-storm - two dispatches while one PDF open is pending ===
  openPdf calls=1 (expect 1)
  createFromImages calls=2 (expect 1 - a value of 2 is a duplicate PDF build)
```
`dispatch` has no in-flight guard and exposes no busy state for the host to
disable the action. PDF opens are protected by the `converting` guard; the image
batch is not. Fix direction (route via CTO): set each image item to `converting`
at collection time and make `dispatch` reject or no-op a concurrent call.

Evidence: `test-fixtures/tfl1248-adversary/probe-intake-dispatch.mjs`,
`test-fixtures/tfl1248-adversary/probe-intake-dispatch.log` (section E).

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-656 (CTO triage 2026-10-08, TFL-1230). A second dispatch() during an in-flight open must no-op and image items must enter `converting` at collection time. The host already guards with `intakeRunningRef` (App.tsx:6407), so this is model-level defense-in-depth. In scope for Phase 118. Fix in flight as TFL-1346.

## Classes that held (Phase 118 intake model chunk B)

- **No extension-only trust / no bogus "Ready" - HOLDS.** `add` always yields
  `validating` + `kind:"unknown"` (`model.ts:169-175`); the kind and readiness come
  only from the caller's `classify` detection result. Probe section A.
- **Duplicate basenames disambiguated, order preserved - HOLDS.** `uniqueName`
  yields `report.pdf` then `report (2).pdf`; insertion order is the queue order
  (`model.ts:123-133, 166-178`). Probe section B.
- **Synthetic / pathless `File` - HOLDS (no crash).** `new File([], "")` adds,
  classifies and removes without throwing; the row name renders empty (cosmetic
  only, not filed). Probe section C.
- **Remove is queue-only - HOLDS.** `remove` splices and returns; the model does
  no IO and holds no path to a filesystem delete (`model.ts:197-201`).
- **No parallel store / no IO / no network - HOLDS.** `model.ts` imports nothing;
  `IntakeTray.tsx` imports only icons, `IconButton` and `unsupportedFileMessage`;
  there is no fetch / IPC / print / mail call in the module.

Method note: unassigned heartbeat. TFL-1248 is dependency-blocked (heartbeat-context
`blockedBy` = TFL-1247, whose terminal blocker is TFL-1242; neither is `done`) and a
fresh build mutex (`owner` qa, task TFL-1273) was held, so no vitest / build / e2e was
run. This is source review plus one plain-Node probe against the shipped
`src/renderer/intake/model.ts`. The running-app entry points this task names (OS drop
routing, clipboard intake, Home, Create-from-images) do not exist on disk yet - chunks
C-F are unwritten and no app file imports `src/renderer/intake/` - so those attack
classes were NOT exercisable. Findings left PENDING; probe and fixture left uncommitted
for git-agent.

## ADV-253: Restore defaults silently truncates the recent-files history it promises to keep

- Session: phase-114 gate
- Suggested severity: MEDIUM

What I did: attacked the Phase 114 (chunk H) "restore-defaults scope (no
document/history/asset loss)" claim end-to-end. Seeded an isolated profile with
`recentsCap: 20` and 15 real recent-files entries, launched the app through the
canonical `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` helper, opened the Settings Studio with the real
Ctrl+, accelerator, clicked Restore defaults, and confirmed the shared dialog. Then
read the on-disk `settings.json` of that profile. Fixture/seed and steps:
`e2e/tfl1280_adversary_restore.spec.cjs` (test 1). Support probe driving the REAL
`SettingsService` + REAL `restoreDefaultSettings`: `test-fixtures/tfl1280-adversary/probe-restore-history.mjs`.

Expected: the confirm dialog states, verbatim, "Restores the appearance, tab,
recent-files and import settings to their defaults. Your documents, recent-files
history, window layout and saved signatures are kept." (`RESTORE_DEFAULTS_SCOPE`,
`PreferencesDialog.tsx:137-138`), and phase-114.md criterion 9: Restore defaults
"restores settings only, never documents, history or user assets". The 15 history
entries must survive.

Actual: the replace-style restart (`SettingsRow`) — `onRestoreDefaults` sends the whole
object (`App.tsx:13471-13476`), `restoreDefaultSettings` lowers `recentsCap` to 10 while
keeping `recentFiles`, and the main-process `normalizeSettings` then runs
`normalizeRecentFiles(rawObj.recentFiles, recentsCap)` (`src/main/services/settings.ts:1182,1190`)
which slices the history to the new cap (`settings.ts:427-428`). Five entries are
permanently dropped from disk. Live log (`e2e-restore-live.log`):

```
[tfl1280] before: cap = 20 history = 15
[tfl1280] after : cap = 10 history = 10
```

The probe against the real service reproduces it headlessly: 15 on disk -> 10 after
`restoreDefaultSettings` + `SettingsService.save()`. The dev unit test
(`test/unit/renderer/phase114_importRestore.test.tsx:262-315`) only asserts the pure
result keeps `recentFiles` and seeds a single entry, and the phase e2e E4 also seeds a
single entry, so neither exercises the backend truncation. This contradicts the scope
the user just accepted; the loss is silent (no toast, no notice), and the affected list
is a persisted user asset the criterion names explicitly.

Evidence: `e2e/tfl1280_adversary_restore.spec.cjs` (test 1, failing),
`test-fixtures/tfl1280-adversary/e2e-restore-live.log`,
`test-fixtures/tfl1280-adversary/probe-restore-history.mjs`,
`test-fixtures/tfl1280-adversary/probe-restore-history.log`.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-660 (renumbered from DEF-644 by the CTO TFL-1355 ruling 2026-10-08: the Phase 118 Intake Tray intake defects own DEF-644/645/646 in the shipped code/tests/e2e/CONTROL-INDEX/docs/phase-specs/phase-118.md, and ADV-253 was filed with the standing qualifier "renumber if taken") (MEDIUM; filed by qa in the Phase 114 close pass). CTO triage 2026-10-08 (TFL-1219):
confirmed - `restoreDefaultSettings` lowers `recentsCap` to 10 and the backend
`normalizeSettings` slices `recentFiles` to the cap on save
(`src/main/services/settings.ts:1182-1190,427-428`), so history is lossy although the
scope text promises it is kept. This is a CTO brief error: chunk E listed
`recentsCap` among the reset fields. Fix: stop resetting `recentsCap` (preserve it
and `recentFiles`) and reword the scope text truthfully. Owner frontend-dev; fix
tracked as TFL-1282.

## ADV-254: A double failure on the Restore-defaults path keeps the unpersisted reset in the UI (DEF-638 re-entered)

- Session: phase-114 gate
- Suggested severity: LOW

What I did: attacked the chunk-H "failure rollback honesty" claim on the Restore-defaults
action, using the exact DEF-638 precondition (a write fails AND the rollback re-read
fails). Seeded a profile with `theme: dark`, launched, opened the Studio, and replaced
the profile's `settings.json` with a directory so the queued write's `rename` fails and
the rollback `loadSettings()` read fails with `EISDIR`/`ok:false`. Then clicked Restore
defaults and confirmed. Repro: `e2e/tfl1280_adversary_restore.spec.cjs` (test 3).

Expected: per the accepted DEF-638/ADV-247 contract — "the UI still drops the optimistic
value instead of keeping one that never persisted" — the renderer must fall back to the
last confirmed snapshot when the re-read fails (`useSettingsWriteRollback.ts:53-58`), so
the theme should revert to the boot theme `dark`.

Actual: the UI keeps `frosted` — the Restore-defaults value that never persisted. Live log:

```
[tfl1280-rf] boot theme = dark
[tfl1280-rf] theme after double failure = frosted (last confirmed = dark)
```

Root cause: `onRestoreDefaults` calls `applySettings(reset)` BEFORE the write is confirmed
(`App.tsx:13474`), and `applySettings` unconditionally sets
`lastConfirmedRef.current = s` (`App.tsx:1528`). The reset therefore becomes the "last
confirmed" snapshot the fallback restores. Every other writer (theme/cap/tab/enable) sets
`settings` optimistically without calling `applySettings`, so `lastConfirmedRef` only ever
held genuinely persisted values before this call site. Precondition is the same narrow
double failure DEF-638 accepted as LOW, hence LOW.

Evidence: `e2e/tfl1280_adversary_restore.spec.cjs` (test 3, failing),
`test-fixtures/tfl1280-adversary/e2e-restore-live.log`; source trace
`App.tsx:1528,1968-1982,13471-13476`, `useSettingsWriteRollback.ts:53-58`.

Disposition: ACCEPTED -> DEF-661 (renumbered from DEF-645 by the CTO TFL-1355 ruling 2026-10-08: the Phase 118 Intake Tray intake defects own DEF-644/645/646, and ADV-254 was filed with the standing qualifier "renumber if taken") (LOW; filed by qa in the Phase 114 close pass). CTO triage 2026-10-08 (TFL-1219):
confirmed - `onRestoreDefaults` calls `applySettings(reset)` optimistically and
`applySettings` sets `lastConfirmedRef.current`, so on the DEF-638 double failure the
unpersisted reset becomes the fallback snapshot. Fix: the restore-defaults optimistic
path must not mark the value confirmed; only an applied echo / `onSettingsRestore`
updates `lastConfirmedRef`. Owner frontend-dev; fix tracked as TFL-1282.

## Design critique: Phase 114 Settings Studio (TFL-1280)

Scope: the migrated renderer surfaces only (`PreferencesDialog.tsx`,
`SettingsStudio.tsx`, the `.settings-*` styles). User job: adjust app preferences in one
place and understand when each takes effect. Success: every setting lands, with its timing
and persistence state visible. Reviewed by source (live screenshots not captured this
pass; the app launches were driven through the canonical helper).

### Should-fix (before broader rollout)
- **States / feedback visibility:** the persistence-status line is the LAST child of the
  scrolling groups column (`.settings-studio-body { overflow-y: auto }`), so on the long
  General or Import panels the honest failure sentence and "All changes saved." scroll
  below the fold. **Try:** pin the status line to the sheet footer/body edge so it stays
  visible while the panel scrolls.

### Nice-to-fix (when there's room)
- **Copy:** the Import group shows the timing twice — the group
  `description="Applies to the next import."` and a closing `SettingsSupport` repeating
  "…Applies to the next import." **Try:** keep one instance, prefer the group description.
- **Edge cases:** the recents-cap input commits on blur/Enter and relies on the reducer to
  clamp; typing an out-of-range value that clamps to the CURRENT value (e.g. "999" while the
  cap is 50) writes nothing and leaves the raw typed text in the box, so the displayed value
  diverges from the stored one until the next cap change. **Try:** on commit, always
  reflect the clamped value back into the field even when the reduce is a no-op.

### Strengths to keep
- The nav is a real `role="tablist"` with roving tabindex, arrow/Home/End keys and a
  visible focus ring; Escape and focus return to `[data-app-menu]` are wired.
- The forced-colors block remaps the selected nav item and focus to system `Highlight`
  roles instead of ornamental fills.
- Timing help is honest per row ("Applies immediately; … next launch", "… next import")
  and there is no invented Apply/Cancel footer.

## Classes that held (Phase 114 Settings Studio gate pass)

- **Failure rollback honesty, normal path - HOLDS (live).** With `settings.json` set
  read-only, a Studio theme change flipped optimistically and then reverted to the boot
  theme, `[data-prefs-persist-status]` read "Settings could not be saved: EPERM: … Your
  previous value was restored.", and disk kept the prior theme. Repro test 2 of
  `e2e/tfl1280_adversary_restore.spec.cjs` (passes).
- **ADV-246/247/248 fixes present - HOLDS (source + unit).** `noteSettingsRestore`
  resets the write seq on restore (`useSettingsWriteRollback.ts:37-44`, used at
  `App.tsx:1973`); the hook's `getLastConfirmed` fallback exists (`:53-58`); and

## Design critique: Phase 120 Output Studio print window (TFL-1259)

User: a person who has a document open in Jovrel and wants a physical print or a PDF
copy. Job: pick the destination and page scope, understand what will come out, and run
it. Success: the job lands where they expect with the settings they chose.

### Should-fix (before broader rollout)
- **Copy / honesty:** the consequence summary labels the page set ("Pages 1-34 of 34")
  but never the print ORDER, so with Reverse on (or odd/even + reverse) the summary
  reads identically to the forward run. **Try:** when the resolved order differs from
  ascending, append the direction (e.g. "1-34, reversed") so the summary describes the
  job, not just the set. (Same code path as ADV-255.)

### Nice-to-fix (when there's room)
- **States:** the dark-theme preview shows dark letterbox bands around the white page
  (ADV-256). **Try:** give `.print-preview-cell` the same paper-white background as the
  sheet, or size the sheet from the real page aspect, so the paper reads uniformly
  white in every theme.
- **Hierarchy:** in the compact layout the "Destination" and "Pages" groups dominate the
  first screen while "Layout"/"Appearance" sit below the fold; the primary action is
  pinned, so this is acceptable, but the group order could lead with "Pages" (the most
  common tweak) before "Destination".

### Strengths to keep
- Two-column settings|preview when wide, one-column stacked when narrow, switched by ONE
  declared logical-pixel breakpoint - no per-call-site media query, no second subsystem.
- Grouped settings use native `<fieldset>/<legend>` and `<details>/<summary>`, so the
  advanced groups collapse but every control stays reachable and keyboard-operable.
- The pre-execution consequence summary (pages / destination / format) is derived from
  the real hook state and states the real operation; the failure strip keeps the
  settings and names the one retry path.
- The preview renders the real geometry and page rasters, and the paper stays white in
  light and dark; disabled states and the Escape/cancel contract are coherent.
